Uncertain passages

1514 notes the verse translator left on 780 poems, with the likeliest problems first. They were sorted by keyword, so some will be in the wrong group. The prose was translated separately and has no notes, so its errors will not appear here.

  1. The Arabic may be wrong381 notes
  2. The meaning is unclear405 notes
  3. Names and places289 notes
  4. One reading chosen among several439 notes

The Arabic may be wrong

The translator suspected a misprint, a corrupt word, or a misplaced line division, then translated its best guess.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
Dwellings I inhabited for a time,until gray appeared at my temples.
منازل قد عمرتها زمناحتى بدا في عذارى الشهب

عذارى is understood as عذاري, 'the hair at my temples/cheeks,' with a final-letter spelling variation or transcription error.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
Those dwellings no longer delight anyone standing therewith the splendor of human forms or the clamor of voices.
تلك المنازل ما تمتع واقفابزهى الشخوص، ولا وغى الأصوات

بزهى الشخوص is obscure as printed and may contain a textual error. 'The splendor of human forms' is tentative, taking زهى as related to زهو, 'splendor' or 'pride.'

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
The life one has lived is worthiest of a young man's tears;the sorrowful must one day find consolation.
والعيش أولى ما بكاه الفتىلا بد للمخزون أن يسلى

المخزون ('stored up') appears to be a misprint for المحزون ('the sorrowful'), which is the reading translated here.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
As dearly as loved ones are esteemed,so are their traces honored after they are gone.
بقدر كرامة الأحباب يكرم بعدها الأثر

The text reads بعدها ('after her/it'), with no clear feminine singular antecedent. The translation takes this as referring to the loved ones’ departure; the wording may be corrupt.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
Indeed, I once saw yougathering all my love within you; your former days were praised, O finest dwelling-place.
ولقد أراكوأنت جامعة الهوى يثنى بعهدك خير دار مقام

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: the first hemistich probably ends after وأنت جامعة الهوى. The supplied division is preserved here. The syntax of يثنى بعهدك خير دار مقام is uncertain; the translation tentatively takes it as praise of the dwelling's former days, followed by an address, 'O finest dwelling-place.'

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Whose are the dwellings, deserted at ʿAbāʾ?Had I wished, they would have stirred my tears this morning.
لمن المنازل أقفرت بعباء؟لو شيت هيّجتِ الغداةَ بكائي

شيت probably represents شئت, with the hamza omitted or misprinted. The translation reads شئت and هيجت as first-person verbs; the unvocalized text also permits other readings, including taking the dwellings as the subject of هيجت: ‘they would have stirred my tears.’

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
Their ruins grieved my companion, and there welled uphis tears among them, though I had not said, “Weep with me.”
شجدت صاحبي أطلالها فتهللتمدامعه فيها، وما قلت: أسعد

شجدت appears corrupt; translated as شجت, “grieved,” with أطلالها (“their ruins”) as its subject.

On encampments (manāzil), line 5
Great are their guest-bowls, capacious their cooking pots,sought out forever by day and visited by night.
عظام مقاريهم جماع فدورهميد الدهر تنتاب النهار وتطرق

فدورهم appears to be a misprint for قدورهم, 'their cooking pots,' adopted here. جماع is understood as 'capacious,' describing pots large enough to hold a whole slaughtered animal.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
Would that the dwellings and homeswere enclosures and graves.
ليت المنازل والديارحضائر ومقابر

حضائر is uncertain here. I have provisionally translated it as 'enclosures,' reading it as a possible variant or misprint of حظائر.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
The most trouble-free dwelling is a grave in which one rests;and the finest clothing, so far as I know, is the shroud.
أعفى المنازل قبر يستراح بهوأفضل اللبس فيما أعلم الكفن؟

أعفى is an unusual comparative here; I understand it as 'most free from trouble or burdens.' The source's final question mark has no clear grammatical basis and may be a transcription error.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
If you call on me to remember the pledges, theywere broken, and became part of the treasures laid away.
إما تناشدني العهود فإنهاخيست فكانت بين ذخر المقتنى

The second hemistich is obscure and may be corrupt. «خيست» can suggest that the pledges were violated, but its connection with «فكانت بين ذخر المقتنى» (‘and became among stored-up treasures’) is unclear. The translation is tentative.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
Youth shook off its leaves and left mea slender reed: however you press it, it bends.
نفض الصبي أوراقه، وأعادنيخوط اليراعة، كيف تغمز تنحني

I read «الصبي» as «الصبا» (‘youth’), apparently a transcription error, in keeping with the imagery of aging.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Is Laylā resolved to depart, and you have not died?It is as though you are heedless of what looms over you!
أمزمعة للبين ليلى ولم تمتكأنك عما قد أظلك غافل؟

للبيت ('for the house') appears to be a misprint for للبين ('to depart'), the reading adopted here.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
Each day amid your grounds I heave a sighwhose blaze sends sparks flying.
لي كل يوم في ربوعك زفرةيرمى لظاها بالشرار الطائر

يرمى is taken as يرمي, 'casts' or 'sends forth,' with a likely spelling or transcription error in the final letter. Read literally as a passive, it would mean that the blaze 'is pelted with' sparks.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
until it greens every effaced and barren tract,long deserted, and waters every withered, drooping plant.
حتى تروض كل ماح ما حلعاف، وتروى كل ذاو ذابل

The printed ما حل is read as the single word ماحل, ‘barren’ or ‘parched’; the spacing appears erroneous.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Look at the dwellings of the house of Munqidh: they arean admonition to the discerning, a lesson to the beholder.
أنظر منازل آل منقذ إنهاعظمة اللبيب، وعبرة للناظر

The text عظمة اللبيب, literally ‘the greatness of the discerning person,’ appears corrupt. The translation assumes an intended sense of ‘an admonition to the discerning,’ probably involving عظة rather than عظمة.

On encampments (manāzil), line 7
How long will you two reproach me? Forkeeping faith with old pledges, am I to blame?
فإلام لومكما؟ أفيرعي العهود على آمه؟

The closing phrase «على آمه» is unclear as printed. The translation tentatively reads it as «عليّ آمة», understood to mean 'blame upon me'; the wording may be corrupt.

On encampments (manāzil), line 4
And I am drawn—despite my eloquent lament to them—by their mute dwelling sites.
ويطبينيعلى فصاحة شك واي إليها ربوعها العجم

The hemistich division appears displaced: h1 contains only ويطبيني ('and draws me'), while h2 contains the remainder of the verse. شك واي is read as شكواي ('my lament').

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Among the wonders of time is that every dwellingof Wajra, on the flanks of Rummān, lies effaced.
ومن عجب الأيام أن كل منزللو جرة من أكناف رمان دارس

The printed «لو جرة» appears to have an erroneous space; I read «لوجرة», ‘of Wajra.’ Whether Wajra here names a person or a place is uncertain. Rummān appears to be a place name, but its precise identification is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Perhaps love, if you greet a dwellingat Akyāb, will bring its lingering pangs back upon you.
لعل الهوى إن أنت حييت منزلابأكياب مرتد عليك عقابله

Akyāb (أكياب) is an unidentified place; the spelling may be corrupt. عقابله also appears corrupt, probably for عقابيله, meaning lingering or recurrent aftereffects, here translated as 'lingering pangs.'

On encampments (manāzil), line 5
My heart is like a bird in a snarethat recognized its folly when its snares released it.
كأن فؤادي طائر في حبالةرأى غيه لما اعتقته حبائله

اعتقته is problematic. Read as أعتقته, it means 'released it,' as translated, but the image of a trapped bird suggests a possible misprint for اعتاقته, 'held it back' or 'detained it.'

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
I am the one whose own gaze brought him death;Against whom can vengeance be claimed, when the slain man is the slayer?
وأنا الذي جلب المنية طرفهفمن المطالب، والقتيل القائل؟

The source reads القائل, 'the speaker.' I have taken this as a likely misprint for القاتل, 'the slayer': his own gaze caused his death, making the slain man his own killer.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
You pass from station to station, ever farther from your beloved,and keep weeping for him with streaming tears.
تطوى المنازل عن حبيبك دائباوتظل تبكيه بدمع ساجم

I read تطوى as تطوي, ‘you traverse [the journey’s stages],’ in keeping with the second-person address that follows. The final letter may be a spelling or transcription error.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
Deserted, they show at Dhū al-Laḥīn, as though they werefaded remnants of a tattoo, or lines in a book.
قفرا تلوح بذي اللحين كأنهاأنضاء وشم، أو سطور كتاب

The place name ذي اللحين is unidentified; the vocalization used in “Dhū al-Laḥīn” is tentative, and the transmitted spelling may be corrupt.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
A deeply attached love refused to let me bear Saʿdā’s absence,and a deadly yearning for Saʿdā that claimed a share of my heart.
أبى الصبر عن سعدى هوى ذو علاقةووجد بسعدى شارك القلب قاتل

«شارك القلب» literally suggests ‘shared with the heart’ or ‘participated in the heart’. Its construction and intended sense are unclear, and the text may be corrupt. ‘Claimed a share of my heart’ is a tentative rendering.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
For I still have tears left, if I am to weepover every dwelling where my people once stayed.
فإني لباقي الدمع أن كنت باكياعلى كل دار حلها مرة أهلي

The unusual phrase لباقي الدمع is rendered as ‘I still have tears left.’ The translation reads أن conditionally as إن (‘if’), possibly correcting a typing or OCR error.

On encampments (manāzil), line 4
You want me to be content, yet you are miserly;and who can satisfy friends through miserliness?
تريدين أن أرضى، وأنت بخيلةومن ذا الذي يرضى الاخلاء بالبخل

The second يرضى is understood as يُرضي (‘satisfies, pleases’), with الأخلاء (‘friends’) as its object; the printed final letter may be an orthographic or transcription error.

On encampments (manāzil), line 4
I said—though a ruler’s shifting will sometimes sets the dwelling far from one burdened with longing—
فقلتوالدار أحيانا يشط بها صرف الأمير على من كان ذا شجن

صرف الأمير, rendered tentatively as “a ruler’s shifting will,” is unexpected in this context and may be corrupted. The supplied hemistich division after فقلت also appears misplaced, but has been preserved.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
O Mayy’s two dwellings, peace be upon you both,despite the distance: the distant lover remains loving and true.
أمنزلني مي سلام عليكماعلى النأي، والنائي يود وينصح

أمنزلني appears corrupt, probably for أمنزلتي, ‘O two dwellings.’ The dual address is confirmed by عليكما.

On encampments (manāzil), line 4
Once lovely women dwelt there, like oryx cowswith hearts inclined to youthful passion, and like oryx calves.
ولقد تكون بها الأوانس من مهىميل القلوب إلى الصبي وجآذر

الصبي is probably a misprint for الصِّبا, 'youth' or 'youthful passion,' rather than الصبي, 'the boy'; the translation follows that reading.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
You were moved to longing, and the dwellings stirred you [unclear phrase];ah, how often longing returns to you with grief.
طربت وهاجتك المنازل من جنألا ربما يعتادك الشوق بالحزن

The phrase من جن at the end of the first hemistich is unclear. It may contain a corrupted reading or an unidentified name; it has been left untranslated.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
I looked toward Zaynab’s departing caravan in the morningand lamented over it—if only lamenting could avail.
نظت إلى أظعان زينب بالضحىفأعولتها لو أن إعوالها يغني

نظت appears to be a typographical or OCR error for نظرت, ‘I looked.’

On encampments (manāzil), line 5
Those dwellings and hills were scoredby the burdens of heavy rainclouds borne by those winds.
خطت على تلك المنازل والربىمنهن أعباء الغمام المثقل

The wording is uncertain. خطت is taken as ‘traced’ or ‘scored,’ with أعباء الغمام المثقل (‘the burdens of heavy rainclouds’) as its subject. It may instead be a misprint for حطت (‘descended’ or ‘deposited’). The referent of منهن (‘from them’) is also unclear; ‘borne by those winds’ is a tentative interpretation.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
Yet once it was, for life’s pleasures,and for fair women and young men, a praiseworthy dwelling.
على أنه قد كان للعيش مرةوللبيض والفتيان منزلة حمدا

The final phrase منزلة حمدا is grammatically unclear as printed. 'A praiseworthy dwelling' is tentative; حمدا may be a textual error.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
And there is she with whose love my heart is distraught,though it has gained nothing of worth from her.
وفيها الذي هام الفؤاد بحبهاعلى أنه لم يحظ منها بطائل

The masculine relative pronoun الذي conflicts with the feminine pronouns in بحبها and منها. It may be a misprint for التي; the translation follows the feminine pronouns.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
Sighs assail me whenever I remember them,nearly wearing my chest away.
تعتادني زفرات حين أذكرهاتكاد تنفد منهن الحيازيم

تنفد means ‘be exhausted’ or ‘run out,’ an unusual expression with الحيازيم (‘chests’ or ‘breastbones’). It may be a misprint for تنقد, ‘split apart.’ The translation retains the supplied reading.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Why do the dwellings not answer our company?Have they gone deaf, or has decay lasted so long that we have wasted away?
ما للمنازل لا يجبن حزبناأصممن أم قدم البلى فبلينا؟

حزبنا is translated as written, ‘our company,’ but may be a transcription error for حزينا, ‘a grieving man.’

On encampments (manāzil), line 5
It was coyness, so we forgaveit; then it ended in aversion.
كان دلالا فغفرناه، فتم مللا

فتم مللا is awkward as printed and may contain a textual error. 'Then it ended in aversion' provisionally understands تم as reaching completion and مللا as weariness or loss of affection.

On dwellings (diyār), line 5
And some people say—[their remoteness stirs me?]—“Ibn al-Ashraf, Kaʿb, is still grieving.”
ويقول أقوامأثير بشحطهم إن ابن الأشرف ظل كعب يجزع

أثير بشحطهم is unclear. شحط means distance or remoteness; “their remoteness stirs me” is only a tentative reading of the supplied wording, which may be corrupt. The hemistich division also appears displaced: the first hemistich contains only ويقول أقوام.

On dwellings (diyār), line 8
I have been told that all the Banū al-Mughīrabowed in grief at the killing of Abū al-Ḥakīm and were brought low.
نبئت أن بني المغيرة كلهمخشعوا لقتل أبي الحكيم وجدعوا

The text gives أبي الحكيم, hence Abū al-Ḥakīm. This probably refers to Abū al-Ḥakam, better known as Abū Jahl, who was killed at Badr; الحكيم may be a misprint for الحكم.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Are you departing without having stopped at Muntabih,and leaving Umm al-Faḍl in al-Ḥaram?
أراحل أنت لم تلمم بمنتبهوتارك أنت أم الفضل بالحرم؟

منتبه is taken provisionally as a place name, Muntabih. I cannot identify the place or establish its vocalization; the spelling may be corrupt.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
Indeed, I once knew within them—shall I see it again, a morning destination and an evening refuge for the seeker of eminence?
ولقد عهدت بهافهل أرينه مغدى لمنتجع العلى ومراحا

The text appears defective or incorrectly divided. The unusually short first hemistich, ولقد عهدت بها, leaves what the speaker knew there unstated. The masculine singular pronoun in أرينه (“shall I see it”) also has no clear antecedent. The translation preserves the apparent incompleteness.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
Their dwellings lie deserted, and their traces have been changed,since their inhabitants departed, by the succession of ages.
أفوت منازلهم وغير رسمهابعد الأنيس تعاقب الأزمان

أفوت appears to be a typographical or OCR error for أقوت, ‘became deserted,’ which is the reading translated here.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
When I saw there was no hope, I turned my she-camelaway from the dwelling, and despair overcame my fortitude.
فلما بدا لي اليأس عديت ناقتيعن الدار، واستولى على عزائي

The final clause, واستولى على عزائي, is ambiguous: I have taken despair as its unstated subject. If على is a misprint for عليّ, it would instead mean ‘my fortitude gained mastery over me.’

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
the homes.
المنازل

Al-manāzil ('the homes') appears to be the displaced final word of line 3, completing its second hemistich and supplying the subject of 'weep,' rather than a separate verse.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Whose are these dwellings, clothed in their decay?Their sight has made you forget, yet you do not forget them.
لمن الديار تسربلت ببلاهاأنستك رؤيتها، وما تنساها

أنستك رؤيتها literally means 'their sight made you forget,' but what was forgotten is unstated, and the contrast with 'you do not forget them' is unclear. Possibly أنستك is a misprint for آنستك, 'brought you comfort.'

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
Do not lie: I do not see you turning awayfrom them, even if you say you will desist.
لا تكذبن فما أراك بمنتهعنها، وإن خبرت أن ستناهي

The ending أن ستناهي appears defective; the translation takes it as 'that you will desist,' possibly intended as أن ستناهى. خبرت is read as خبّرت, 'you said/reported,' though the unvocalized form is ambiguous.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
I burst into tears for al-Tawbādh when I recognized it,and it proclaimed the All-Merciful’s greatness when it saw me.
وأجهشت للتوباذ لما عرفتهوكبر للرحمن حين رآني

The source spells the mountain’s name التوباذ (Al-Tawbādh); it is commonly known as التوباد (Al-Tawbād), so the final letter may be a transcription error.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
Those dwellings—no cloud passes over themand pours upon them without an eye streaming too.
تلك المنازل ما تمر سحابةفهمي بها إلا وعين تهمل

فهمي appears corrupt, probably for فتهمي, ‘and pours down’; the translation follows that reading.

On dwellings (diyār), line 5
People are only like dwellings: their inhabitantsare there the day they settle, but tomorrow the dwellings are empty wastes.
وما الناس إلا كالديار وأهلهابها يوم حلوها وغدوا بلا قع

«بلا قع» is evidently a mistaken division of «بلاقع», “empty wastes.” «وغدوا» also appears corrupt; the translation follows the likely reading «وغدًا», “and tomorrow.”

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
The prime of youth is youthful passion’s brother and companion;gray hair means desire’s dismissal and departure.
شرخ الشباب أخو الصبي وأليفهوالشيب تزجية الهوى وخفوفه

الصبي is understood as الصِّبا, ‘youthful passion’ or ‘youthful folly,’ rather than الصبيّ, ‘the boy’; the spelling may reflect a transcription error.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
I thought,when I could not bear separation, that those mute ruins could bear it.
خلتلما لم أطق حمل النوى أن تلك الدمن الصم مطيقه

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: the first hemistich likely ends at «النوى», rather than «خلت». The supplied division is retained.

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
I did not know,until they wasted away as I have, that they too were filled with longing.
لم أكن أعلمحتى نحلت كنحولي أنها مثلي مشوقه

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: the first hemistich likely ends at «نحلت», rather than «أعلم». The supplied division is retained.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
We passed the dwellings, which had exchangedtheir newness for decay and oblivion.
قد مررنا على الديار تبدأن دثورا، بجدة، وخمولا

The word split across the hemistichs as تبدأ / ن is unclear and appears corrupt. The translation tentatively reads تبدّلن ('exchanged'), taking بجدة to mean 'in place of newness.'

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
The world is only like a passing shadow.I praise God: thus He ordained it.
إنما الدنيا كظل زائلأحمد الله، كذا قدرها

أحمد الله is translated as ‘I praise God.’ If the initial hamza is a spelling error for احمد, the phrase would instead mean ‘Praise God.’

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
May God send rain—though they have departed; tell them so—upon the site of the tents and those black mountains.
سقى الإلهوإن بانوا، وقل لهم مبنى الخيام، وتلك الأجبل السودا

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: the first hemistich likely continues through «وإن بانوا، وقل لهم», with the second beginning «مبنى الخيام». The supplied division is preserved here. The phrase «وقل لهم» ('and tell them') is awkward in context; it is rendered as a parenthetical 'tell them so.'

On dwellings (diyār), line 5
As though you had never known the tribe there as neighbors,united in affection—bewildered, you cannot turn away.
كأنك لم تعهد بها الحي جيرةجميع الهوى، من حيرة ما تصرف

The syntax of جميع الهوى، من حيرة ما تصرف is unclear, and the text may be defective. The translation provisionally understands جميع الهوى as 'united in affection' and ما تصرف as 'you do not turn away,' with من حيرة meaning 'from bewilderment.'

On dwellings (diyār), line 5
What do my grief for you and my sorrow amount to?They are little, even if my heart is torn apart.
ما قدر ما أسفي عليك وحسرتيقلت، ولو أن الحشا يتقطع

I read قلت as qallat ('it is little; it falls short'), referring to the grief and sorrow, rather than qultu ('I said'). The construction ما قدر ما is awkward, and the wording may contain a textual error.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Stop, you two: hold back those mounts, and releasemy tears—after the loss of these homes, shall I conceal my grief?
قفا فاحبسا تلك الركاب وأطلقادموي، فهل بعد الديار أكاتم؟

دموي appears to be a misprint for دموعي, “my tears,” which is the reading translated.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
The dwellings stand empty of them and have becomeeffaced, as though they were mere markings.
أقفرت منهم الديار وأضحتدارسات كأنهم رقوم

The masculine plural pronoun in كأنهم ('as though they') apparently refers to the inhabitants, but the comparison with رقوم ('markings' or 'inscriptions') seems more naturally to describe the dwellings. The text may be corrupt; the translation leaves the reference open.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
And when you pass by them, say,quoting a verse:
فإذا مرتت بها فقلمتمثلا

مرتت appears to be a misprint for مررت, 'you pass.' The line appears incomplete, and متمثلا ('quoting a verse or saying') introduces a quotation that is not supplied.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
The land I love best is the land they [dwelt in],where once they had a settled home.
أحب الأرض أرض دموهاوكان لهم بها يوما قرار

دموها is unclear and appears corrupt. The bracketed 'dwelt in' is a conjectural rendering suggested by the following hemistich; the intended Arabic wording is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
The dwellings of her who nearly—while we were at Minā—undid us, had our mounts not sped away.
ديار التي كادتونحن على منى تحل بنا، لولا نجاء الركائب

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: ونحن على منى probably belongs with the first hemistich. تحل بنا literally suggests descending upon or alighting with us; ‘undid us’ interprets it as bringing ruin through love, but the intended sense is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
I saw her only three times, [at Minā?],and I remember her as a maiden with braided locks.
ولم أرها إلا ثلاثا على نمىوعهدي بها عذراء ذات ذوائب

على نمى is unclear and may be corrupted. The translation tentatively conjectures على منى, ‘at Minā,’ as in line 2. ثلاثا is taken as ‘three times,’ though ‘three nights’ is also grammatically possible.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
And your little tents at the bend of al-Liwā—they have worn away as no dwellings ever have.
وخيماتك اللاتي بمنعرج اللوىبلين بلى لم تبلهن ربوع

The wording بلى لم تبلهن ربوع is difficult, particularly the pronoun ending in تبلهن. The translation tentatively understands a comparison with the decay of other dwellings; the text may be corrupt.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
It was as though the daughter of al-Bakrī, the day I beheld her,ʿUbayda, were a kohl-eyed gazelle, its neck outstretched.
كأن ابنة البكري يوم اجتليتهاعبيدة مكحول الدامع مرشق

I take عبيدة (ʿUbayda) as the daughter's name, in apposition to ابنة البكري. الدامع looks like a corruption of المدامع, 'the eyes' or 'tear ducts.' The gazelle is implicit in the descriptive phrase مكحول ... مرشق, rendered 'kohl-eyed ... its neck outstretched.'

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
Has the hollow of Suwayqatayn departed from its place,or has al-Bardān settled there after our stay?
هل رام جو سويقتين مكانهأم حل بعد محلنا البردان

The second hemistich is unclear as transmitted. The translation takes حل as active ḥalla, ‘settled,’ with al-Bardān as its subject. A passive reading, ‘has al-Bardān been inhabited,’ is also possible; alternatively, حل may be a misprint for حال, ‘changed.’

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
You are the one who grieves in the wakeof those people; if you resolve to go their way, you will rise.
إنك أنت المخزون في أثر القوم فإن تنو نيهم تقم

المخزون ('stored away') appears to be a misprint for المحزون ('grief-stricken'), which is translated here. The phrase تنو نيهم تقم is also uncertain; نيهم is provisionally understood as their intended direction, and تقم as 'you will rise [to go].'

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
It is as though my eye, as al-Talīl flowed with them—and what neighbors they were, if only they were near!—
كأن عيني وقد سال التليل بهموعبرة ما هم، لو أنهم أمم

التليل is retained as the unidentified name al-Talīl. It may be a textual error for السليل, 'the valley.'

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
It is as though my eye, as al-Talīl flowed with them—and what neighbors they were, if only they were near!—
كأن عيني وقد سال التليل بهموعبرة ما هم، لو أنهم أمم

وعبرة ما هم is difficult to construe and appears corrupt. The translation assumes وجيرة ما هم, 'and what neighbors they were.' أُمَم is understood as 'near.'

On dwellings (diyār), line 5
were a great bucket on a pulley, or trembling pearlson a thread whose stringing has failed the women who own them.
غرب على بكرة، أو لؤلؤ قلقفي السلك جاربه رباته النظم

جاربه رباته النظم is obscure as printed. The translation tentatively reads جار به رباته النظم as describing stringing that has gone awry for the pearls' owners; the exact wording may be corrupt.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
Upon it pouredthe roaring winds with steady, copious rain, and its traces vanished.
جادت عليهافاضمحل رسومها هزج الرياح بديمة مدرار

The hemistich division appears displaced, probably belonging after رسومها. The wording هزج الرياح and its syntax are uncertain; the translation provisionally takes it as 'roaring winds,' the delayed subject of جادت.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
In a dwelling of Mayy’s that I recognized, I am notsteadfast, nor do my tears there refuse to flow.
وما أنا في دار لمى عرفتهابجلد، ولا دمعي بها بجماد

لمى is read as لمي, “of Mayy,” referring to the woman addressed in line 4; the final letter appears to be a typing or OCR variation.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
and by the Lord of the young sacrificial she-camels whose throats bleedat Makka, and of those who hasten about the sacred sites:
ورب القلاص البدني تدمي نحورهابمكة والساعين حول المناسك

البدني appears to be a misprint for البدن, referring to sacrificial camels; the translation follows that reading.

On dwellings (diyār), line 5
Their fragrance is musk, their faces goldcoins, and their fingertips red as ʿanam.
النشر مسك والوجوه دنانير، وأطراف الأكف عنهم

The source reads عنهم, which appears to be a misprint for عنم (ʿanam), a plant whose red blossoms, fruit, or branches are compared to dyed fingertips. Its precise botanical identity is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
I see him, in the folly of yearning, amid their landmarks,and in love’s earnestness amid their haunts of play.
فأراه جهل الشوق بين معالمفيها وجد الوجد بين ملاعب

The syntax of فأراه جهل الشوق ... فيها is unclear, and the wording may be corrupt. Tentatively, I take أراه as ‘I see him’ and جهل الشوق as ‘the folly of yearning.’ I read وجد الوجد as ‘and the earnestness of love,’ contrasting earnestness with the places of play.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
Dwellings that disowned us after knowing us, and grew desolate, bereft of our love, after intimacy.
منازل أنركتنا بعد معرفة وأوحشت من هوانا بعد إيناس

أنركتنا appears to be a typographical error for أنكرتنا, ‘disowned us’ or ‘no longer recognized us.’ The construction أوحشت من هوانا is somewhat unclear; ‘grew desolate, bereft of our love’ is a tentative rendering.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
I visited the dwellings at al-Baqīʿ and Thahmad,their traces effaced, now empty of Umm Maʿbad.
غشيت الديار بالبقيع فثهمددوارس قد أقوبن من أم معبد

أقوبن appears to be a misprint for أقوين, ‘became deserted’; the translation follows that reading.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Has it stirred your longingor not—a spring encampment at al-Sitārayn, and a desolate trace in the sandy tracts of al-Ghadīrayn?
أهاجكأم لا بالستارين مربع ورسم بأجراع الغديرين بلقع

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: the likely division is after مربع, with ورسم beginning the second hemistich. The translation preserves the supplied division.

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
A man desires to be granted his wishes,yet God permits nothing but what He wills.
يريد المرء أن يعطي مناهويأتي الله إلا ما يشاء

The translation assumes two likely textual errors: يعطي for يُعطى ('be granted'), and ويأتي ('and comes') for ويأبى ('but refuses'). The latter, with إلا ما يشاء, means that God allows only what He wills.

On dwellings (diyār), line 5
They press onward, lean as spear-shafts, scattering dust,bearing Qanān, al-Ḥamās, and Raʿbal.
تواغل جردا كالقنا حاثيةعليها قنان والحماس ورعبل

The construction «تواغل جردا كالقنا حاثية» is difficult and may contain a transcription error. The translation provisionally understands the horses as pressing onward and «حاثية» as scattering dust, although dust is not explicitly mentioned.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
An abode of Saʿdā, when Suʿād was likea gazelle fawn, downcast of eye and supple of limb.
دار لسعدى، إذ سعاد كأنهارشأ غضيض الطرف رخو المفصل

The text switches from Saʿdā to Suʿād within the same hemistich. These may be variant names for the same woman; a textual error is also possible.

On haunts (maghānī), line 1
Swallow sorrow: the lone sandy tract lies deserted,and let the eye be: longing wrings its tears from it.
تجرع أسى قد أقفر الجرع الفردودع جفه عين يحتلب ماءها الوجد

جفه is unclear and may be a misprint for جفن ('eyelid'). The second hemistich is translated tentatively, taking ودع as 'and leave be.'

On haunts (maghānī), line 2
If I were asked—with summer’s midday heat ablaze and a thirst in my breast flaring like fire—
لو قيل ليوهجير الصيف متقد وفي الحشا غلة كالنار تضطرم

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: وهجير الصيف متقد likely belongs with h1, leaving وفي الحشا غلة كالنار تضطرم as h2. The supplied division has been preserved.

On haunts (maghānī), line 2
Dwellings emptied of happiness and splendor,the dwellings of fair women, wealth, and all one could wish for.
مغان خلت من غبطة ونضارةمغاني الغواني، والغني والرغائب

الغني is understood as الغنى, “wealth,” rather than الغنيّ, “the wealthy man”; the final letter may reflect a typographical or transcription variation.

On haunts (maghānī), line 1
What a pasture for the eye, what a fresh valleytime has scraped bare at Malḥūb!
أي مرعى عين وواد قشيبلحيته الأيام في ملحوب

لحيته appears corrupt, probably an OCR error for لحبته, ‘scraped it bare’ or ‘wore it away,’ which is the reading followed here. Malḥūb is a place name; its precise location is uncertain.

On haunts (maghānī), line 1
Turn—may good be yours—the mounts toward hills that were once al-Rabāb’s abodes.
عرجلك الخير صدور الركاب على ربا كن مغاني الرباب

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: the first hemistich likely ends after الركاب, with the second beginning على ربا. The translation preserves the supplied division. صدور الركاب literally means ‘the breasts of the mounts,’ rendered idiomatically as ‘the mounts.’

On haunts (maghānī), line 1
The old dwelling sites are kinder to my heart than reproach,though they stir anguish and sighing.
المغاني أحفى بقلبي من العدل وإن هجن لوعة وزفيرا

العدل, split across the hemistichs, appears to be a misprint for العذل, here translated as ‘reproach.’ Without vowel marks, the corrected form could also mean ‘reproachers’ (العُذَّل).

On haunts (maghānī), line 6
relief for the distressed, support for an avenger,and a refuge for those whose homelands cast them out.
فرجا لمكروب، ونضرة ثائروملاذ من تنبو به أوطانه

The source reads نضرة ثائر, literally something like “freshness of an avenger,” which is unclear here. The translation tentatively assumes نصرة ثائر, “support for an avenger,” with نضرة a possible typing or OCR error. ثائر can also mean a rebel or insurgent.

On haunts (maghānī), line 2
We once dwelt there, when our life was pleasant,with fair, companionable maidens, like statues, with wide, dark eyes.
وقد نحل بها إذ عيشنا أنقبيض أوانس أمثال الدمى حور

The syntax is uncertain: نحل means ‘we dwell,’ but بيض (‘fair women’) appears grammatically disconnected from it. ‘With’ is supplied provisionally. نحل may be a misprint for تحل, which would make the sense ‘Fair, companionable maidens once dwelt there, when our life was pleasant.’

On haunts (maghānī), line 2
As though I were the first lover before whom appearedthe loved ones’ dwelling, so that his tears streamed forth.
كأنني أول العشاق طاللهمغنى الأحبة فارفضت مدامعه

The reading طالله is unclear and may be a transcription error. The translation provisionally understands it as طلّ له, ‘appeared to him.’

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
As though its dwelling-place had been wateredand altered by our tears, streaming down the day they departed.
كأنما جاد مغناهفغيره دموعنا يوم بانوا، وهي تنهمل

The hemistich division appears misplaced: فغيره (“and altered it”) likely belongs at the end of h1. I take دموعنا (“our tears”) as the delayed subject of both جاد (“watered”) and غيّر (“altered”).

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
My companion says, on the day at Sābiqat al-Naqā,while my eyes stream with overwhelming grief:
يقول زميلي يوم سابقة النقىوعيناي من فرط الأسى تكفان:

سابقة النقى is unclear. Provisionally treated as the place name Sābiqat al-Naqā, but I could not identify it; the wording may be corrupt.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
And one sign of my anguish—though gray hair gives the discerning self-command—is weeping over the ruins on the day of al-Rawākis.
ومن جزعيوالشيب إحكام ذي النهى بكاء على الأطلال يوم الرواكس

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: the likely division is after «ذي النهى». The translation preserves the supplied division.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Do you recognize today—or do you not recognize—the ruined campsite? Yes; it has stirred my sorrows and dread.
هل تعرف اليومأم لا تعرف الطللا بلى، فهيج لي الأحزان والوجلا

The hemistich division appears misplaced: the first hemistich likely ends with الطللا, and the second begins with بلى. The translation preserves the supplied division.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
The winds have scattered it since its inhabitants departed,for months and days and a full year.
أذاعت به الأرواح بعد أنيسهاشهورا وأياما وحولا محرما

محرما is unclear here and may be a misprint for مجرما, 'completed,' in the expression حولا مجرما, 'a full year.' The translation follows that probable reading.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 3
Are the young men's haunts swept away, while you have not meltedwith longing, nor lamented their bare ground?
أمواقف الفتيان تطوى لم تذبشوقا، ولم تندب لهن صعيدا؟

The construction «ولم تندب لهن صعيدا» is unclear. «صعيدا» ordinarily means bare or level ground; 'lamented their bare ground' is tentative. The wording may contain a transcription error.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
The ruins squander tears at every stopping place,and the dwellings still standing wreak havoc on tears.
تطل الطلول الدمع في كل موقفوتمثل بالدمع الديار المواثل

تمثل بالدمع is unusual and possibly misprinted. I have taken تمثل بـ to mean 'mutilate' or 'maltreat,' giving 'wreak havoc on tears'; the intended image is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
A familiar haunt, desolate of companions:Its fading traces stirred in me a grief that does not fade.
مألف موحش من الآلافهاج عافية لي جوي غير عاف

The second hemistich appears to contain transcription errors. I tentatively read «عافية» as «عافيه» ('its effaced traces') and «جوي» as «جوى» ('grief' or 'love-sorrow').

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 6
I stood questioning them, though they held nothingbut oryx and dusky male ostriches.
فوقفت أسألها وليس بهاإلا ألمها ونقانق ربد

ألمها appears to be a typing or OCR error for المها, ‘oryx,’ adopted in the translation.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Tell me, O ruined dwelling:those who dwelt in you—what became of them?
خبرني أيها الطللالألى حدوك ما فعلوا؟

حدوك appears to be a misprint for حلوك, ‘dwelt in you,’ which is the reading translated here.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
At the foot of the slope are traces, their outlines likea Yemeni cloth embroidered by Rayda and Saḥīl.
وبالسفح آيات كأن رسومهايمان وشته ريدة وسحيل

Saḥīl (سحيل) appears to be a place associated with Yemeni textiles, but its identification is uncertain. The spelling may be related to, or a corruption of, Saḥūl (سحول), a name associated with such cloth.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 4
Now I know nothing of them since I saw them; a ridge and hills have come between me and the company.
فأصبحت لا أدري لدن أن رأيتهم أتى حدب دون الجميع وقور

The syntax of لدن أن رأيتهم أتى حدب دون الجميع وقور is unclear, and the text may be defective. The translation tentatively takes أتى حدب ... وقور to mean that a ridge and hills intervened; ‘of them’ and ‘between me and’ are supplied to make the inferred sense readable.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 6
Indeed, we once lived in happiness when we camped,in the days when your people dwelt in those abodes.
ولقد نكون إذا يحل بغبطةأيام أهلك للديار حلول

إذا يحل ('when he settles') is awkward beside نكون ('we were/would be'). The translation provisionally reads إذا نحل ('when we settle'), a possible correction of a dotting or transcription error.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 3
It is as though the time the tribe spent at the sandy bend—the bend of Tarmadhāʾ—had never been.
كأن زمانا حله الحي باللوىلوى ترمذاء لم يكن بزمان

ترمذاء is unidentified, and its vocalization as Tarmadhāʾ is tentative. The spelling may be corrupted, possibly for ثرمداء (Tharmadāʾ).

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 5
Whenever I say, 'I shall put Asmāʾ from my mind,' love callsto my heart with its promptings, and my heart disobeys me.
إذا قلت: أنسى ذكر أسماء هيبتبقلبي دواعي حبها فعصاني

هيبت بقلبي is unusual. It is provisionally understood as 'called to my heart,' with دواعي حبها ('the promptings of her love') as its subject; the wording may be corrupt.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
As though my heart—broken anew by recognizing her campsite there—were a weakened leg abandoned by its splints.
كأن فؤاديهاض عرفان ربعها بها وهي ساق أسلمتها الجبائر

The syntax of هاض عرفان ربعها بها وهي ساق is unclear and may be corrupt. The translation tentatively understands recognition of the campsite as breaking the heart anew, followed by a comparison with an injured leg abandoned by its splints. The supplied hemistich division also appears misplaced.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 8
Whenever I look out, it is toward the quarterwhere you are, of all quarters, that I gaze.
وإني متى أشرف إلى الجانب الذيبه أنت من بين الجواب ناظر

الجواب appears to be a misprint for الجوانب, ‘quarters’ or ‘directions,’ which is the reading translated.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 9
No brief spell of dozing overtakes the ridersat night without a visitor from you returning to me.
وأن لا ينال الركب تهويم وقعةمن الليل إلا اعتادني منك زائر

The opening وأن لا is syntactically uncertain and may be misprinted. The unusual phrase تهويم وقعة has been rendered tentatively as ‘a brief spell of dozing.’

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
May God water Baljāʾ’s ruined dwellings at al-Ghaḍā,which decay and distance have clothed in matted layer upon layer.
سفى الله أطلالا لبلجاء بالغضاكساها البلى والنأي لبدا على لبد

The source reads سفى الله, probably a misprint for سقى الله, the conventional prayer ‘May God water …’; the translation follows that reading.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 3
Love for you makes me forget what is in my handand distracts me from everything I undertake.
وحبك ينسيني من الشيء في يديويذهلني عن كل شيء أزاوله

The construction من الشيء في يدي is awkward, particularly the function of من. I have understood it as referring to what the speaker holds in his hand; the wording may contain a textual error.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Halt the pale camels among Mayya’s ruins, and questionthe traces, like the tatters of a threadbare cloak.
قف العيش في أطلال مية فاسألرسوما كأخلاق الرداء المسلسل

العيش ('life') appears to be a misprint for العيس ('pale camels'), which is translated here. The precise textile sense of المسلسل is uncertain; 'threadbare' is provisional.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 7
The perennial waterholes parted with Mayya and took in her steadscattered herds of wide-eyed wild cows, lingering with their calves.
دعت مية الأعداد واستبدلت بهاخناطيل آجال من العين خذل

The opening دعت is unclear as transmitted. The translation takes الأعداد ('perennial waterholes') as the subject of both verbs and understands the first as releasing or parting with Mayya; a defective form or misprint involving ودعت may be involved.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Did you not halt, so the ruins might tell you,though they have decayed—if questioning could avail?
ألم تربع فتخبرك الطلولوقد ساءت لو نفع السؤول

وقد ساءت is awkward here. It is translated as referring to the ruins’ deterioration, but it may be a misprint for وقد سألت, ‘though you have asked.’

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
But how can one question worn-out tentsand an old encampment ditch, its newest trace a year old?
وكيف سؤال خيمات بوالونوى عهد أحدثه محيل؟

The second hemistich appears defective. The translation tentatively reads نوى as نؤي, an encampment’s drainage ditch, and أحدثه محيل as ‘its newest trace is a year old.’ The wording عهد and the construction as a whole remain uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
It avails nothing, my friend, to lingerat ruins; nor does questioning bring back what is gone.
ليس بجدي يا صاحبي وقوفبطلول ولا يرد سؤال

بجدي appears to be a misprint for يجدي ('avail'). I read يرد as 'bring back'; its object is unstated, so 'what is gone' is supplied.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
If it is a fire, it stands on a towering height;the wind scatters it and lashes it fiercely.
فإن تك نارا فهي في مشمخرةمن الربح تذروها وتصفقها صفقا

الربح ('profit') appears corrupt, probably for الريح ('wind'). The translation follows that reading, though the syntax of من الريح remains awkward. مشمخرة is understood as an elevated peak or height.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
The dwelling’s traces held me until there flowedmy tears, and until my companion reproached me again and again.
وما انفك رسم الدار حتى تهللتدموعي، وحتى أكثر اللوم صاحبي

The construction وما انفك رسم الدار is unclear as transmitted: انفك appears to lack a complement. It may be elliptical or corrupt. “The dwelling’s traces held me” is a contextual interpretation.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Stop at the effaced ruins, O ʿUlāth;the ropes of those who dwelt there have grown threadbare.
قف بالطلول الدارسات علاثاأضحى حبال قطينهن رثاثا

علاثا is uncertain. It is provisionally read as an address to ʿUlāth, possibly a shortened form of the name ʿUlātha; the person is unidentified, and textual corruption cannot be ruled out.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 3
The abodes of her—the fruit of her kissesis sweet, and her touch is soft.
ديار التي أما جنى رشفاتهافيحلوا، وأما مسها فيلين

فيحلوا appears to be a spelling or transcription error for فيحلو, 'it is sweet.'

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Have Saʿdā’s ruined dwellings stirred you this morning,at Dhū al-Ṭalḥ, [effaced] and weathered?
أهاجك من سعدى الغداة طلولبذي الطلح عامي ومحيل

عامي is unclear and may be corrupt. The bracketed 'effaced' tentatively assumes عافي, a word commonly used of vanished dwelling traces; the wording of this hemistich remains uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
Their people departed, and over them sweptthe summer winds and pouring rain.
تحمل أهلها وجرى عليهارياح الصيف والسرب الهطول

السرب الهطول is unusual. السرب can denote flowing water; 'pouring rain' is a contextual rendering. السرب may also be a textual error for السحب, 'clouds.'

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
A dwelling of Asmāʾ, where we once stayed;and you—in those days it had been your home.
دار لأسماء إذ كنا نحل بهاوأنت إذ ذاك قد كانت لكم وطنا

The opening وأنت (“and you,” singular) in the second hemistich is syntactically awkward and shifts to plural “you” in لكم. The text may be corrupt; the translation preserves its abrupt construction.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 13
whose bounty all may share, whose fire-stick readily sparks,illustrious, ever wearing the robes of glory.
مشترك النبل ورى الزندأغر لباسا ثياب المجد

The source has مشترك النبل, whose sense is uncertain. 'Whose bounty all may share' tentatively reads النيل ('bounty') for النبل, a possible dotting or OCR error. If النبل is retained, it may refer to nobility or generosity.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 6
The people's anguish avails nothing whencalamity befalls them, save a change.
ليس يغني جزع القوم إذاوقع الأمر بهم إلا الغيار

الغيار can denote change, but its precise meaning here, and the logic of 'save a change' after 'avails nothing,' are unclear. The text may be defective.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 7
Grieve over what has happened, or do not grieve:the roof has fallen in and the wall has collapsed.
فاجزعوا للأمر، أو لا تجزعواقد تداعى السقف وأنهار الجدار

أنهار appears to be a spelling or transcription error for انهار, 'collapsed,' which is the reading translated.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
Question the dwelling in its decay, you two, and say:“You have stirred a long yearning in us this morning.
سائلا الربع بالبلى وقولاهجت شوقا لنا الغداة طويلا

بالبلى is uncertain: rendered here as “in its decay,” but it may conceal a place-name or a textual error.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 4
Yet once I would see it, before the ravages of separation,delighting the beholder with its beauty.
وقد أراه قبل صرف النوىيعدب من بهجته الناظر

يعدب appears to be a misprint for يعجب, ‘delights’ or ‘pleases,’ which is the reading translated here.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
Stop, you two, at what you recognize of my dwellings,even if my tears have outrun my utmost fortitude.
قفا عند مما تعرفان ربوعيوإن سبقت فرط العزاء دموعي

The wording عند مما تعرفان ربوعي is syntactically irregular and may contain a copying or OCR error. The translation provisionally takes it to mean ‘at what you recognize of my dwellings.’

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
Fairer indeed to behold than the lowlands of al-Ruṣāfaand its parade ground, al-Rukh, al-Dūr, and the bridge,
لأحسن من بطن الرصافة منظراوميدانها فالرخ فالدور فالجسر

الرخ, provisionally transliterated al-Rukh, is an unidentified place-name here; it may be a misprint for الكرخ (Al-Karkh). The particular locality intended by al-Dūr is also uncertain.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 3
I dream of them at al-Raqmatayn, while their homeis in Wādī al-Ghaḍā—how far away is what I long for!
فمنيتهم بالرقمتين، ودارهمبوادي الغضا يا بعد ما أتمناه

فمنيتهم is unclear as printed and may be corrupt. “I dream of them” is a tentative contextual rendering, taking it to express a wish concerning their whereabouts.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
Is it for the campsite that your eye has kept shedding tearsin sprays, as strung pearls stream down?
أللربع ظلت يعنك الماء تهملرشاشا كما استن الجمان المفصل؟

يعنك appears to be a typographical error for عينك, ‘your eye.’ المفصل likely describes pearls separated by intervening beads or other ornaments; the precise arrangement is uncertain.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 4
I remember the tribe settled there in carefree ease,all together, with the signs of love still undiminished.
عهدت بها الحي الحلول بسلوةجميعا، وآيات الهوى ما تزيل

بسلوة is taken to mean ‘in carefree ease,’ though a place name, Salwa, is also possible. ما تزيل is understood as ‘do not disappear’; the transmitted verb form is unusual in this sense and may be corrupt.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 3
Ruins where I suckled at the teats of youth—if only that suckling had not been followed by weaning!
دمن رضعت بهن أخلاف الصبيلو لم يكن بعد الرضاع فطامه

الصبي (‘the boy’) appears to be a misprint for الصبا (‘youth’), which is the reading translated here.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 2
Revering your dwelling is the striving of one who falls short:when the sword has perished, let oblivion take the sheath.
وإجلال مغناك اجتهاد مقصرإذا السيف أودي فالعفاء على الجفن

أودي appears to stand for أودى, 'perished,' with a possible typing or OCR error in the final letter.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 5
The first assaults of calamity struck you and scatteredyour people, those maiden gazelles with budding breasts.
أصابتك أبكار الخطوب فشتتتنواك بأبكار الظباء الكواعب

The wording نواك بأبكار is unclear. نواك ordinarily suggests your destination, intended journey, or separation, rather than your inhabitants. The translation provisionally understands the phrase as referring to the dispersal of the women who occupied the site; the text may be corrupt.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 2
I well remember myself—and all that is new must decay—long happy and joyful in union with you.
فلقد أرانيوالجديد إلى بلى دهرا بوصلك ناعما مسرورا

The hemistich division appears misplaced: والجديد إلى بلى likely belongs at the end of the first hemistich, with the second beginning دهرا. The supplied division is preserved. The phrase about decay is read as a parenthesis.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
We stopped at the campsite of the withholding beloved, and forth rushedtears the eye had once begrudged.
وقفنا على ربع البخيلة فانبرتوسابق قد كانت بها العين تبخل

وسابق appears to be a misprint for سوابق, meaning things that race ahead—here, rushing tears. The translation follows this conjectural reading.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
Has the campsite saddened you, or its age,or ashes whose charred remnants have worn away?
أشجاك الربع م قدمهأم رماد دارس حممه

The isolated م in the first hemistich appears defective. I have read it as أم (‘or’); من (‘because of’), giving ‘Has the campsite saddened you because of its age?’, is also possible.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
My two friends, this is ʿAzza’s campsite: hobbleyour two young she-camels, then weep where she once dwelt.
خليلي هذا ربع عزة فاعقلافلوصيكما ثم ابكيا حيث حلت

فلوصيكما appears to be a misprint for قلوصيكما, ‘your two young she-camels,’ which is the reading translated.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 3
“I water it”: I pray that it receive rain.
أسقيه: أدعو له بالسقيا

This appears to be an explanatory prose gloss on أسقيه in line 2, rather than a verse.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 4
There is ordained for mefrom where I do not know, separation; and longing steals upon me from where I know.
تقيض ليمن حيث لا أعلم النوى ويسري إلي الشوق من حيث أعلم

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: the first hemistich would naturally end after النوى, with the second beginning ويسري. The translation preserves the supplied division.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
My two friends, turn aside—come now, you two—for a while with me at the campsite, that we may fulfill a need and bid farewell.
خليلي عوجاويكما ساعة معي على الربع نقضي حاجة ونودع

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: the expected division is after معي. The translation preserves the supplied division.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 4
In those days, suns dwelt in you that never rose before uswithout wrapping themselves in blood shed by their glances.
أيام فيك شموس ما انبعثن لناإلا التعثن دما بالحظ مسفوكا

التعثن is obscure; I tentatively understand it as 'wrapped themselves.' بالحظ ('by fortune') appears to be a misprint for باللحظ ('by a glance'), which the translation follows.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 2
O Lord of the Throne, I have sinned in forsaking her;whatever sin there may be, You are its forgiver.
فذ العرش قد أجرمت في أن هجرتهاوما يك من ذنب فإنك غافره

The opening فذ العرش appears defective, perhaps through loss of an alif in an invocation such as فذا العرش. The translation provisionally takes it as an address to God, 'O Lord of the Throne.'

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 2
A blustering wind with trailing skirts swept over it,with [unclear] and a fierce, gravel-scattering train.
جرت به ذات أذيال مزعزعةلها تقى، وذيل عارم حصب

I cannot make satisfactory sense of لها تقى in this description of a wind or storm. تقى may be a transcription error; its place is marked '[unclear]' in the translation.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 4
She said: “Had you forgotten us, then remembered us?It is the gazelle we thank, not the weeping tears.”
قالت: أكنت نسيتنا فذكرتناللظبي نشكر، لا للدمع الباكي

الدمع الباكي literally means “the weeping tears,” an unusual expression retained here. It may be personification or a textual error; الباكي also departs from the preceding rhyme endings.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 4
If he went down to Tihāma whenlonging climbed to Najd with me—
إن كن قد أتهم لماأنجد الوجد معي

كن appears defective, probably for كان. The translation assumes إن كان قد أتهم. أتهم and أنجد mean to enter Tihāma and Najd respectively, also contrasting descent to the lowlands with ascent to the uplands.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 6
I entrusted him with my heart, but he did nothonor the rights of the one who entrusted it.
أودعته قلبي قلميرع حقوق المودع

قلم appears to be a misprint for فلم, “but he did not.”

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 7
Though he has betrayed me and has nothonored my rights, may he be kept safe.
وإن يكن خان ولميرع حقوقي فرعي

فرعي is unclear. It is tentatively read as a passive blessing, فَرُعِيَ, “may he be cared for,” despite his betrayal; the wording or vocalization may be defective.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 2
I faced the caravan’s mounts until they coveredmy feet with dust; they treated me harshly and blamed me.
نحرت ركاب الركب حتى يغبروارجلى، لقد عنفوا علي ولاموا

The wording نحرت ركاب الركب حتى يغبروا رجلى is obscure and may be corrupted. The translation tentatively takes نحرت as “faced” and يغبروا رجلى as “covered my feet with dust,” but the connection between these actions remains unclear.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 1
Ruins, like the track of trailing reins,their tight strands unravelled.
دمن كمسحبة الأزمة مسحلا إمرارها

The wording كمسحبة الأزمة مسحلا إمرارها is difficult and may be corrupt. The translation provisionally takes مسحبة الأزمة as the track of dragged reins, and مسحلا إمرارها as tightly twisted strands being loosened or unravelled.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 2
Their realities have died,but their false semblance and borrowed guise endure.
ماتت حقائها وخلد زورها ومعارها

حقائها appears corrupt. The translation conjectures حقائقها, ‘their realities,’ in contrast with زورها ومعارها, ‘their false semblance and borrowed guise.’

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 4
On Laylā’s account I bear a grudge against some people,and on Laylā’s account grudges are borne against me.
وأحمل في ليلى لقوم ضغينةوتحمل في ليلى على الضغائن

على appears to be a typing or OCR error for عليّ, ‘against me.’ The translation also reads تحمل as passive تُحمل, ‘are borne.’

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 2
The dwelling—if we turn aside,bless you!—will its ruins and thumām-grass speak of what we seek?
هل الدار إن عجنالك الخير ناطق بحاجتنا أطلالها وثمامها؟

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: لك الخير ناطق probably belongs at the end of the first hemistich. The translation preserves the supplied division.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 4
Dwellings of Mayy at Wahbayn, wateredby heavy showers, their clouds drizzling, and their [itmihmām].
منازل من مي بوهبين جادهاأهاضيب طل دجنها واتمهامها

The wording طل دجنها واتمهامها is unclear and may be corrupted. 'Their clouds drizzling' tentatively takes طل as a verb. I cannot securely interpret اتمهامها and have left its central word provisionally transliterated in brackets.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 2
Hasten the three to the Fire, and the fourth—ʿAmr al-Ghawwāl—all bound together in one fetter.
عجل إلى النار بالثلاثة والرابع عمرو الغوال في قرن

The word الرابع (“the fourth”) is divided between the hemistichs; the translation places it wholly in h1. The singer’s epithet الغوال, rendered al-Ghawwāl, is uncertain and may be corrupt.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 1
Memories of youth and the gazelles’ springtime hauntshave brought my death before its appointed hour.
ذكر الصبي ومرابع الآرامجلبت حمامي قبل وقت حمامي

الصبي appears to be a misprint for الصبا, ‘youth,’ which is the reading translated here.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 4
Her dwelling stirred my sorrow, though it lay still;its traces renewed my longing, though they were worn away.
فحرك بثي ربعها، وهي ساكنوجدد وجدي رسمها وهو مخلق

The source reads وهي ساكن, with a feminine pronoun that could refer to the beloved: 'while she dwelt [there].' The parallel contrasts favor referring instead to the motionless dwelling, as translated; وهي may be a misprint for وهو.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 1
And my friend said—while weeping overwhelmed me—“Will weeping and longing be the death of this man?”
وقال خليليوالبكا لي غالب أقاض على هذا البكاو التشوق؟

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: والبكا لي غالب would normally complete the first hemistich. I read البكاو التشوق as البكا والتشوق, 'weeping and longing.' I understand أقاض على هذا as 'will [they] be the death of this man,' with 'this man' referring to the poet, though the wording is uncertain.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 1
People are carefree in their dwellings,while we are journeying, on the move.
الناس لا هون في أماكنهمونحن في رحلة وفي ظعن

Read لا هون as لاهون, ‘carefree’ or ‘amusing themselves’; the space appears erroneous.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 11
People live at leisure in their own places,while we are ever journeying and on the move.
الناس لا هون في أماكنهمونحن في رحلة وفي ظعن

لا هون is read as لاهون, “at leisure” or “amusing themselves,” with an erroneous space.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 18
I have joined together—alas!—a young man’s heart that reveals the cares of one both youthful and aged,
جمعتوالهفتاه قلب فتى يفتر عن هم شارخ يفن

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: the likely division is after قلب فتى rather than after جمعت. It has been preserved as supplied. The phrase هم شارخ يفن is also difficult: شارخ denotes someone youthful, while يفن denotes a decrepit old man. The translation tentatively takes هم as “cares” and retains the apparent contradiction.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 22
Would that, before death, I had alreadybeen hidden away in my grave and my shroud!
يا ليت أني قبل المنية قدغببت في حفرتي وفي كفني

غببت appears to be a typing or OCR error for غُيِّبت, “I was hidden away,” which is followed in the translation.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 2
If what you say is true, then fly awaywith my flesh to your two nests, and eat me.
فإن كان حقا ما تقولان فانهضابحلمي إلى وكريكما فكلاني

بحلمي (‘with my forbearance’ or ‘with my understanding’) appears corrupted. The translation assumes بلحمي, ‘with my flesh,’ which fits the ravens’ eating him.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 1
If you two wish to console me,then take me past the weathered ruins.
فإما شئتما أن تسعدانيفمرا بين على الدمن البوالي

بين in the second hemistich appears to be a misprint for بي: فمرا بي, “take me past.” The translation follows this reading.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 1
Ruins—when you ask your eye to confirm its memory of them,it returns to you with the gaze of one searching for signs.
دمن إذا اشتثبت عينك عهدهارجعت إليك بنظرة المتوسم

اشتثبت appears to be a misprint for استثبت. I understand the phrase as asking the eye to confirm its recollection of the ruins, though the syntax of عينك عهدها is uncertain.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 2
I lingered after them beside an ailing remnant,which knew decay and wasted as things waste.
وعكفت بعدهم على ضمنعرف البلى فبلى كما يبلى

ضمن is uncertain. I tentatively read it as ضَمِن, ‘ailing,’ describing the abandoned dwelling figuratively; it may instead be a textual error.

On traces (rasm), line 4
Their people packed up and departed from them,and the dwellings made me weep in dismay.
تحمل أهلها منها فبانوافأبكتني المنازل للرواع

للرواع is obscure here and may be corrupt. 'In dismay' tentatively connects it with روع, 'fright'; the intended sense is uncertain.

On traces (rasm), line 3
These are but traces of a company once united,scattered by their destinations after living side by side.
وما ذاك إلا من جميع تفرقتبهم نية بعد الجوار قسم

The final word قسم is unclear and may be corrupted; as printed, it also appears inconsistent with the other rhyme endings. The translation follows the apparent overall sense, taking نية as the destination or direction of departure.

On traces (rasm), line 1
As for the traces, they have recalled what is past;so do not let your two tear ducts cease to flow.
أما الرسوم فقد أذكرن ما سلفافلا تكفن عن شأنيك أن يقفا

شأنيك is understood as 'your two tear ducts.' The construction فلا تكفن عن شأنيك أن يقفا is unclear and may be corrupt; the translation follows the apparent injunction to continue weeping.

On traces (rasm), line 2
The forms of things have come between me and it,So my ignorance is no true ignorance, and my knowledge no true knowledge.
أنت صور الأشياء بيني وبينهفجهلي كلا جهل، وعلمي كلا علم

The opening أنت is unclear as printed and may be corrupt. The translation tentatively reads أتت, ‘have come’; this emendation is uncertain.

On traces (rasm), line 6
Rain watered them before me; then, when I watered themwith my tears, they saw how the later rain surpassed the first autumn showers.
سقاها الحيا قبلي فلما سقيتهادموي رأت فضل الولي على الوسمي

دموي appears to be a misprint for دموعي ('my tears'), which is the reading translated here.

On traces (rasm), line 4
My left eye wept; when I rebuked it for folly after forbearance, both eyes streamed together.
بكيت عيني اليسرى فلما زجرتها عن الجهل بعد الحلم أسبلتا معا

بكيت appears to be a misprint for بكت, 'wept,' which is the reading translated. As written, it could alternatively be vocalized بكّيت, 'I made [my eye] weep.'

On traces (rasm), line 2
Where are the people of the tents at al-Ajzaʿ al-Fard?They have departed—oh, where are the people of the tents!
أين أهل القباب بالأجزع الفرد، تولوا، لا أين أهل القباب!

Al-Ajzaʿ al-Fard is unidentified; it may be a descriptive expression rather than a place name. The spelling الأجزع may also be a misprint for الأجرع, a sandy tract. The word al-Fard is divided between the source hemistichs.

On traces (rasm), line 2
Where are the people of the tents at al-Ajzaʿ al-Fard?They have departed—oh, where are the people of the tents!
أين أهل القباب بالأجزع الفرد، تولوا، لا أين أهل القباب!

The wording لا أين is syntactically unusual and possibly corrupt. It is provisionally rendered as an emphatic repetition of the question: 'oh, where ...!'

On traces (rasm), line 4
Nights long ago, when the tribe were neighbors,when its grove was peopled and the place was lovely.
ليالي من دهر إذ الحي حيرةوإذ هو مأهول الخميلة مونق

'حيرة' is unclear here. The translation tentatively reads it as 'جيرة' ('neighbors'), a plausible copying or OCR error.

On traces (rasm), line 2
So you lingered there, on the verge of tears,as though, for all your experience of time, you knew nothing.
فظلت بها تفضي على حد عبرةكأنك من تجريبك الدهر جاهل

The expression تفضي على حد عبرة is unclear, particularly the verb تفضي in this construction. “On the verge of tears” is a tentative rendering; the verb may be misprinted.

On traces (rasm), line 3
Yet what time holds has offered a lesson to anyone with understanding,and counsel to anyone with judgment—will you understand?
وقد كان ما فيه لذي اللب عبرةورأى لذي رأي، فهل أنت عاقل؟

I read ورأى as ورأي, “and counsel/judgment,” parallel to عبرة, “a lesson.” The printed form appears to be a spelling or transcription error.

On traces (rasm), line 1
Have the worn-away traces of the encampments stirred youby the high, jutting sandhills of Ḥawḍā?
أهاجتك أطلال الرسوم الدوائربأدعاص حوضي المغنقات النوادر

المغنقات is unclear and may be a misprint for المعنقات, describing something rising high or projecting; 'high' follows that conjecture. النوادر is taken to describe projecting or isolated dunes. حوضي is read as the place-name Ḥawḍā (حوضى).

On traces (rasm), line 2
It said, “From here they journeyed,and from here they went west.”
وقال: من هنا طعن، وغربن من هنا

طعن, divided between the hemistichs, is taken in the sense of journeying. It may instead be a misprint for ظعن, “departed.”

On traces (rasm), line 7
Those who left at dawn left meno heart to harbor sorrow.
لم يترك الغادون ليقلبا نجن الحزنا

نجن appears corrupt. The translation tentatively reads يجن, “conceals” or “harbors,” with “heart” as its subject.

On traces (rasm), line 1
I bade my tears cease that day at Suwayqa,but an overpowering flood of tears refused [text unclear].
ولقد نهيت الدمع يوم سويقةفأبت غوالب عبرة ما تلب

The closing words ما تلب are unclear and may be corrupted; they are not translated. Suwayqa is a place name, but its precise location here is uncertain.

On traces (rasm), line 2
How did you find your way, without guidance, to a man worn down by love,through the night at ʿĀna, while the Pleiades veered south?
أني اهتديت، وما اهتديت لمعمدمن ليل عانة والثريا تجنب

The wording is uncertain. I take لمعمد to mean ‘to a man worn down,’ with love understood from context. وما اهتديت literally means ‘and you did not find your way’; ‘without guidance’ is a tentative contextual rendering. The text may be corrupt.

On traces (rasm), line 4
You remembered Suʿād there and foolishly turned asideto a trace, asking after Suʿād.
ذكرت بها سعاد فعجب جهلاعلى رسم تسائل عن سعاد

The source reads فعجب, which is difficult to construe here. The translation provisionally reads فعجت, ‘you turned aside,’ a likely copying or OCR error.

On traces (rasm), line 3
I knew Hind there, when Hind was innocent,unversed in lewdness, simple-hearted, much given to evening sleep.
عهدت بها هندا، وهند غريرةعن الفحش بلهاء العتي نئوم

العتي is unclear and may be an OCR error for العشي, ‘evening.’ The translation ‘evening sleep’ follows that conjecture; the wording and grammatical grouping remain uncertain.

On traces (rasm), line 2
Once Salmā would be there, telling me,like falling jewels, all that I wished and longed to hear.
وقد تكون بها سلمى تخدثنيتساقط الحلى حاجاتي وأوطاري

تخدثني appears to be a misprint for تحدثني, ‘speaking to me.’ The syntax of تساقط الحلى حاجاتي وأوطاري is uncertain; the translation tentatively takes her words as falling like jewels and expressing what he wishes to hear.

On traces (rasm), line 4
It was as though my heart, on the morning of parting, were divided,and scattered bands bore it away to different towns.
كأن قلبي غداة البيت منقسمطارت به عصب شتى لأمصار

البيت, ‘the house,’ appears to be a misprint for البين, ‘parting,’ which is adopted in the translation.

On traces (rasm), line 4
Saʿdā once dwelt there, requiting me with her love,on nights when keeping away from her was impossible.
وقد غنيت سعدى نثيب بودهاليالي لا يسطاع منها التجنب

The printed نثيب (‘we reward’) is difficult in context. The translation assumes تثيب (‘she rewards’), a likely dotting or OCR error, and reads غنيت as feminine غَنِيَتْ, ‘she dwelt.’

On traces (rasm), line 4
If you have sense, desist from youthful infatuation,and do not let your eyes follow a people scattered apart.
فإن كنت ذا عقل فأقصر عن الصبيولا تتبعن عينيك شعبا تبددا

الصبي is read as الصبا, 'youthful infatuation' or 'youthful folly,' rather than الصبي, 'the boy'; the spelling may be a transcription error.

On traces (rasm), line 3
If her destination lies far away, and if she is distant,separation can both part and reunite.
فإن تك قد شطت نواها، وأن نأتفإن النوى مما تشت وتجمع

The source's وأن نأت is read as وإن نأت ('and if she is distant'), a likely spelling or transcription error.

On traces (rasm), line 2
Do no violence in its courts, for lovelies cast upon those lifeless traces.
لا تبغني عرصاتها إن الهوىملقى على تلك الرسوم الهمد

The wording لا تبغني عرصاتها is unclear and may be corrupted. The translation provisionally reads لا تبغ في عرصاتها, ‘do no violence in its courts,’ continuing the address to the wind.

On traces (rasm), line 2
I questioned them when I was drawn to them, but they would not listenthen to the call of a lover asking for a halt.
وسألتها حين انجذبت فلم تصخفيه لدعوة عاشق مستوقف

حين انجذبت is unclear in context: literally, 'when I was drawn' (or 'when she/it was drawn'). 'To them' is supplied tentatively. The reference of فيه, rendered 'then,' is also uncertain; the wording may be corrupt.

On traces (rasm), line 1
I wept, but it was not the faded traces that made me weep,nor the campsite, its enclosing trench now effaced.
بكيت وما أبكاني الرسم إذ عفاولا الربع أضحى نويه وهو دائر

نويه probably represents نؤيه, ‘its trench’ (dug around a campsite to divert rainwater). The construction أضحى نويه وهو دائر is awkward and possibly corrupt; the translation takes دائر in the sense ‘effaced’ rather than ‘circular.’

On remains (āthār), line 2
I said—with anguish burning in my heart and tears streaming—
فقلتوالقلب به لوعة تحرقه، والدمع مدرار

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced. The likely division is «فقلت والقلب به لوعة / تحرقه والدمع مدرار». The translation retains the supplied division.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 3
They endured time’s vicissitudes, but [separation carried]Laylā far away from your people’s home.
أقامت على ريب الزمان وأعجتبليلى نوى عن دار أهلك شاطن

The form أعجت is unclear and may be corrupt. The bracketed rendering is conjectural, based on the following phrase بليلى نوى عن دار أهلك شاطن, which describes a departure or separation taking Laylā far from the addressee’s people.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 2
They lay desolate after their people left, save for dwellingsthat look newly made, though they are falling into ruin.
وأوحشن بعد الحي إلا مساكنايرين حديثات وهن دوائر

The exception إلا مساكنا, 'save for dwellings,' is awkward because the preceding subject is itself the dwellings. The wording may be defective; it is translated as transmitted.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 3
They were emptied of human gazelles, then took in their placegazelles, while my heart remains lovesick for those replaced.
خلت من طباء الإنس ثم تبدلتظباء، وقلبي بالمبدل هائم

طباء appears to be a misprint for ظباء, ‘gazelles,’ here used of beautiful people. المبدل is understood as those replaced, rather than their replacements.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 4
They try to turn me away from Sālim, and I turn them back;yet Sālim is the skin between my eye and nose.
يديروني عن سالم وأديرهوجلدة بين العين والأنف سالم

The first hemistich appears textually defective. The translation tentatively reads يديرونني for يديروني and وأديرهم (‘and I turn them’) for وأديره (‘and I turn him’). Sālim’s identity and the precise allusion are uncertain.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 3
Far away for one who seeks nothing,but near for one who has something to seek.
بعيد على من ليس يطلب حاجةوأما على ذي حاجة قفريب

قفريب appears to be a typographical or OCR error for فقريب, “then/but near,” which is followed here.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 4
As [unclear] scattered,after a twisted cord had clasped them tightly—the strewn pearls.
كما أرفض هلكيبعد ما ضم ضمة بحبل الفتيل اللؤلؤ المتناثر

هلكي is unintelligible in this context and appears corrupt. The hemistich division also seems misplaced. The translation is provisional: the recognizable wording apparently compares the tears to pearls scattering after a twisted cord had held them together.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 3
There I knew idols of beauty that knew mein my passion, as a worshipper of their ʿUzzā and their Manāt.
'هدت بها أصنام حسن عهدتنيهوى عبد عزاها، وعبد مناتها

The opening «'هدت» appears corrupted; I provisionally read عهدت, “I knew.” The grammatical role of هوى in the second hemistich is uncertain; “in my passion” is tentative.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 3
Shall I forget you? Shall I forsake you?Rarely do the thirsty forget water.
أسلوا عنكم أهجركمقلما يسلو عن الماء الصوادي

أسلوا appears to be an irregular spelling or transcription of أسلو, 'I forget' or 'I cease to long.' It is translated here as a rhetorical question, parallel to أهجركم, 'Shall I forsake you?'

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 2
They said, “If you turn aside, then weep enough for us—tears whose streaming never ceases.”
فقالوا: إن عرضت فأغن عنادموعا غير راقئة السجام

عرضت is uncertain in this context; it may be a misprint for عرجت, ‘you turn aside,’ which is the sense adopted here. فأغن عنا is understood as asking the speaker to do enough weeping on the others’ behalf.

On the land (arḍ), line 2
Through my passion for Lubnā, I have indeed encounteredan affliction that leaves me unable to swallow any drink.
لقد لافيت من كلفي بلبنيبلاء لا أسيغ له شرابا

لافيت appears to be a misprint for لاقيت (“encountered”). بلبني is read as بلبنى, referring to Lubnā.

On the land (arḍ), line 2
Do You not know, O Lord, how many a prayerI have offered You sincerely—if only He had answered it!
ألم تعلمن يا رب، أن رب دعوةدعوتك فيها مخلصا لو أجابها

The wording is uncertain: لو أجابها literally means ‘if he had answered it,’ shifting from addressing God to the third person and supplying no explicit consequence. I have provisionally read it as a wish, ‘if only He had answered it’; the text may be defective.

On the land (arḍ), line 3
I swear, if I could regard as kin to herthe wolves of the wild, those wolves would be dear to me.
فأقسم لو أني أرى نسبا لهاذئاب الفلا حبت إلى ذئابها

I read حبت إلى as حَبَّت إليَّ, ‘would be dear to me’; the printed إلى (‘to’) appears erroneous. The construction نسباً لها ذئاب الفلا is unusual; I understand it to mean regarding the wolves as kin to the beloved.

On the land (arḍ), line 3
I said: “It is time, from the land where I was born,to return; and time for separation’s vicissitudes to yield reunion.
فقلت: قد حان من أرض ولدت بهاأوب، وقد حان من صرف النوى قرن

The text says من أرض ولدت بها, “from the land where I was born,” although the context seems to require a return to that land. The wording may be corrupt. The second hemistich is also difficult: قرن is provisionally understood as “joining, reunion,” and صرف النوى as the vicissitudes of separation.

On the land (arḍ), line 2
If my fortunes were bound to Dūdān, I would not be assailed,whether I were guilty or innocent.
فإن تلتبس حلى بدودان لا أرملئن كنت ذا ذنب، وإن غير مذنب

حلى is unclear and may be corrupt. 'My fortunes' provisionally assumes حالي ('my condition'). لا أرم is read as لا أُرْمَ ('I would not be assailed'); another possible reading is لا أَرِمْ ('I would not depart'). The construction لئن كنت ... وإن غير مذنب is also awkward as transmitted; the translation takes it to mean 'whether guilty or innocent.'

On the land (arḍ), line 3
Surely a man's own people are better protectionthan the farthest stranger, even if they are not near.
ألا إن قوم المرء خير تفيةمن الأبعد الأقصى، وإن لم تقرب

تفية is unclear, probably a misprint for تقية ('protection'), adopted in the translation. The subject and vocalization of تقرب are uncertain: 'even if they are not near' is provisional; 'even if you are not welcomed' is another possible interpretation.

On the land (arḍ), line 3
I keep putting hunger off until I weary it,and turn my thoughts away from it until I forget.
أديم مطال الجرع حتى أملهوأضرب عنه الذكر صفحا فأذهل

الجرع ('swallowing') appears to be a misprint for الجوع ('hunger'), which is translated here. أمله is read as 'I weary it'; without vocalization, it could also mean 'I grow weary of it.'

On the land (arḍ), line 4
I swallow the earth’s dust, lest he think he hasa claim of favor over me—some bestower of favors.
واستف ترب الأرض كيلا يرى لهعلى من الطول امرؤ متطول

على appears to be a misprint for عليّ ('over me'), the reading used here.

On the land (arḍ), line 1
If you claim that the earth is spacious,with places where others may seek their living and travel,
إن كنت تزعم أن الأض واسعةفيها لغيرك مرتاد ومرتحل

الأض appears to be a misprint for الأرض, “the earth.”

On the land (arḍ), line 2
I reproach a friend just once for what displeases me;then farewell to him—I reproach him no more.
أعاتب الخل فيما ساء واحدةثم السلام علين، لا أعاتبه

علين appears to be a textual or OCR error for عليه, giving ثم السلام عليه, translated here as a farewell: “then farewell to him.”

On the land (arḍ), line 1
Then no chaste woman of Rabīʿa bore meif I side with desire in following her.
فما ولدتني حاضن ربعيةلئن أنا مالأت الهوى لا تباعها

The wording لا تباعها is unclear and may be misprinted. The translation tentatively reads it as لاتّباعها, ‘in following her’; the feminine pronoun’s referent is uncertain.

On the land (arḍ), line 2
Have you not seen that the earth is broad and spacious?Can any one of its regions thwart me?
أم تر أن الأرض رحب فسيحةفهل تعجزني بقعة من بقاعها؟

أم تر appears to be a misprint for ألم تر, ‘Have you not seen,’ which is the reading translated here.

On the land (arḍ), line 1
Bid farewell, man of resolve, to Miṣr—not Lamīs—and plungeon swift steeds into the depths of the desert wastes.
ودع أخا العزم مصرا، لا لميس، وخفضبالسابحات غمار المهمه البيد

The printed وخفض appears corrupt. Translated as وخض, 'and plunge,' which fits the following غمار, 'depths.'

On homelands (awṭān), line 3
I do not forget the one I bade farewell to by the riverbank at dawn,when the camel-drivers sang out and the caravan hastened.
وما أنس من ودعت بالشط سحرةوقد غرد الحادون واستعجل الركب

أنس appears where the negative construction would normally require أنسى, ‘I forget.’ The final letter may have been dropped in transcription; the translation follows the apparent sense, ‘I do not forget.’

On homelands (awṭān), line 6
My lingering in al-Shām brings mesorrows that tear my heart to shreds.
وتأنى بالشآم مفيديحسرات يقددن قلبي قدا

وتأنى is unclear. The translation provisionally reads it as وتأنّي, 'and my lingering,' but it may be corrupted from وتنائي, 'and my being far away.'

On homelands (awṭān), line 3
The heart’s sorrow was deepenedby a turtledove’s voice upon its branch.
ولقد زاد الفؤاد شجيصوت قمري على فننه

شجي is read as شجى, 'sorrow,' with an apparent spelling or transcription irregularity.

On homelands (awṭān), line 4
What wasted me wasted him, and he wept—each weeping over his own sorrow.
شفه ما شفني فبكىكل من يبكي على شجنه

كل من يبكي على شجنه literally reads 'everyone who weeps over his sorrow.' Its syntax here is awkward and may reflect a textual error; the translation takes the intended sense to be that the speaker and dove each weep over their own sorrow.

On homelands (awṭān), line 2
Whenever I wish, I can find the young she-camel, yet I seenone like my people, to whom my heart might warm.
إذا شئت لاقيت القلوص ولا أرىلقومي أشباها فيألفهم ودى

The phrase لاقيت القلوص literally means ‘I meet the young she-camel.’ Its connection with the following contrast is unclear; the wording may be corrupt, but it has been translated as supplied.

On homelands (awṭān), line 2
