When they lament a single sorrow,my sorrows multiply in number.
إذا تشكوا شجنا واحداتكاثرت ععدة أشجاني

ععدة appears to be a typographical or OCR error for عدة, meaning 'number' or 'count'; translated accordingly.

On homelands (awṭān), line 1
My two companions, may my life ransom yours!Turn the mules’ breasts toward the open road.
يا صاحبي فدت نفسي نفوسكماعوجا على صدور الأبغل السنن

The syntax of «عوجا على صدور الأبغل السنن» is unclear and may be corrupt. The translation is provisional, taking «الأبغل» as ‘mules’ and «السنن» as ‘the open or direct road’; the wording does not straightforwardly support the resulting construction.

On homelands (awṭān), line 1
I wish to return to you, but I am held back,whenever I try, by a heavy debt I bear.
أريد رجوعا نحوكم فيصدنيإذا رمته دين على ثقيل

Read على as عليّ (“upon me”), apparently a typing or OCR error.

On homelands (awṭān), line 9
From their right hands and their faces, Time hasthere blazes and white stockings that never fade.
وللدهر من أيمانهم ووجدوههمبها غرر ما تنقضي وحجول

وجدوههم appears to be a typographical or OCR error for وجوههم, 'their faces,' which is the reading translated.

On homelands (awṭān), line 1
We settled among Banū Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr,and among ʿAkk and ʿĀmir of ʿAwthabān.
حللنا في بني كعب بن عمرووفي عك وعامر عوثبان

The wording عامر عوثبان is uncertain. “ʿĀmir of ʿAwthabān” provisionally treats it as a genealogical designation, but the relationship between the names is unclear; the text may be defective. The vocalization of عوثبان is also uncertain.

On homelands (awṭān), line 2
And among Jurm, and among ʿAmr ibn Murr,and among Zayd and Ḥayy ibn al-ʿAdān.
وفي جرم، وفي عمرو بن مروفي زيد، وحي بن العدان

I could not identify حي بن العدان. It is provisionally rendered as the name Ḥayy ibn al-ʿAdān, with uncertain vocalization; حي might instead mean “clan,” and the wording may be corrupt.

On cities (mudun), line 1
Where are those who lived before us,men of might and high standing?
أين من كان قبلنامن ذويب البأس والخطر

ذويب appears to be a typographical error for ذوي, giving ذوي البأس والخطر, ‘men of might and high standing.’

On cities (mudun), line 2
Had they answered you, they would have said—knowing the ways of those who have passed away and those who remain—
فلو أجابتك قالتوهي عالمة بسيرة الذاهب الماضي ومن غبرا

The hemistich division appears misplaced: metrically, وهي عالمة likely belongs at the end of h1. The supplied division has been retained.

On countries (bilād), line 3
A land where my amulets were hung upon me,where childhood's days were fresh and full of ease.
بلاد بها نيطت على تمائميوكان بها عصر الصبي نضرا رغدا

The wording 'نيطت على تمائمي' appears to require 'نيطت عليّ تمائمي': 'my amulets were hung upon me.' Also, 'عصر الصبي' may be a misprint for 'عصر الصبا', 'the days of childhood'; the translation follows that sense.

On countries (bilād), line 2
May God water—for watering is His to grant—our lands at Ḥazm Qanāwayn with gentle morning rains:
سقى اللهوالسقيا إليه بلادنا بحزم قناوين الذهاب الغواديا

Ḥazm Qanāwayn is an unidentified place; the vocalization of قناوين is uncertain. The supplied hemistich division is unusual, but has been preserved.

On countries (bilād), line 1
Ah, pity the stranger in a distant land—what has he done to himself?
وارحمنا للغريب في البلد النازح ماذا بنفسه صنعا؟

The opening وارحمنا appears corrupt, probably for وارحمتا, an exclamation of pity; the translation follows that reading.

On countries (bilād), line 1
Suppose Miṣr were the gardens of eternity: whateverpleasures souls desire are to be found there.
هب أن مصر جنان الخلد ما اشتهتالنفوس فيها في اللذت موجود

اللذت appears to be a misprint for اللذات (‘pleasures’). The phrase في اللذت is awkward; the translation takes it to mean ‘of pleasures.’

On countries (bilād), line 2
In other lands, if you fear hostilityopenly declared, there is escape from wicked rulers.
وفي البلاد إذا ما خفت نائرةمشهورة عن ولاة السوء منتفد

منتفد is unclear and may be a typographical error for منتقد, meaning a place to withdraw to or a refuge. It is translated provisionally as ‘escape.’

On countries (bilād), line 3
toward the land of a people whose way is beyond reach;the way of other people is destruction.
لبلاد قوم لا يرام هديهموهدى قوم آخرين هو الردى

The sense of لا يرام هديهم is uncertain. Read literally as “whose way cannot be sought or attained,” it does not clearly explain the preference for this people. I have provisionally understood هديهم and هدى as “way” or “guidance.” The wording may be corrupt; the ending الردى also departs from the preceding lines’ rhyme.

On countries (bilād), line 3
Wādī Ushayy is in al-Madīnah.
وادي أشى بالمدينة

This appears to be a prose geographical gloss rather than a verse. Its placement of Wādī Ushayy in al-Madīnah is puzzling: the valley associated with these verses is generally identified with al-Yamāmah.

On countries (bilād), line 5
They feed others when a north wind blowsand a cutting blast of its cold visits the tribe at dawn.
والمعطمون إذا هبت شآميةوباكر الحي من صرادها صرم

المعطمون appears to be a misprint for المطعمون, 'those who feed others.' The wording من صرادها صرم is obscure and possibly corrupt; 'a cutting blast of its cold' is a tentative rendering.

On countries (bilād), line 2
For the chessboard’s pawn, though its lowliest piece,becomes a vizier when it advances.
فنيذق النطع وهو أحقر ما فيه إذا ساء صار فرزانا

فنيذق appears to be a corruption of فبيذق or فبيدق, ‘the pawn’; ساء (‘became bad’) is probably سار (‘traveled’ or ‘advanced’). The translation follows these likely corrections.

On countries (bilād), line 2
Indeed, a man whose house has not been left bare this yearand whose flesh has not been renewed is surely ignoble.
وإن امرأ لم يقفر العام بيتهولم يتجدد لحمه للئيم

يقفر بيته can mean that his house becomes deserted or that it is stripped of provisions. The sense of ولم يتجدد لحمه, translated literally as ‘whose flesh has not been renewed,’ is unclear in context; the wording may be corrupt.

On countries (bilād), line 1
A land where my well-wishers shunned me, and I weariedmy friend; those who visited me paid that no heed.
بلاد جفاني الناصحون وملنيصديقي، ولمن يحفل بذلك عودي

ولمن appears to be a misprint for ولم, 'and did not.' I tentatively read عودي as عُوَّدي, 'those who visit me when sick'; the wording and sense of this hemistich remain uncertain.

On countries (bilād), line 2
How often my head has drunk its fillthere—and wild goats from my pillow.
كم قد تروت هامتيفيها وعول من وسادي

The text appears corrupt. تروت هامتي literally suggests 'my head drank its fill,' while وعول من وسادي reads 'and wild goats from my pillow.' I cannot establish a coherent meaning for the line; the translation preserves the apparent wording.

On countries (bilād), line 1
While darkness lay with its neck laid low, there flasheda gleam between Ṣāḥa and al-ʿArān.
تألق والدحى ملقى الجرانبريق بين صاحة فالعران

الدحى appears to be a misprint for الدجى, “darkness,” adopted here. ملقى الجران evokes a camel resting its neck on the ground.

On countries (bilād), line 2
She gazed, her eye shedding tears,watchfully, looking with one eye.
ورنت والعين تذرىكالئا ترنو بعين

The wording كالئا ترنو بعين is obscure and may be corrupt. كالئا can mean ‘watchful’ or ‘guarding,’ but its masculine form does not clearly fit the female subject. The second hemistich is translated tentatively; ‘tears’ in the first is implicit rather than expressed.

On countries (bilād), line 2
How often my head has been drenchedthere, with ibex for my pillow.
كم قد تروت هامتيفيها وعول من وسادي

The wording is obscure and may be corrupt. تروت هامتي is read as ‘my head was drenched,’ and وعول as ‘ibex.’ The rendering ‘with ibex for my pillow’ is tentative: وعول من وسادي literally gives something like ‘and ibex from/of my pillow,’ whose syntax and intended meaning are unclear.

On countries (bilād), line 1
When the lovesick stranger sees my submissionand my sighs clothed in humility,
إذا الصب الغريب رأى خضوعيوأنفاسي تزين بالخشوع

The clause beginning with إذا ('when' or 'if') has no clear grammatical conclusion. Line 3 may supply it, but the connection is loose; the text may be defective.

On countries (bilād), line 5
Though I am not among its inhabitants,a person dear to me dwells there.
وإن لم أكن من ساكنيه فإنهيحل به شخص على كريم

Read على as عليّ ('to me') in شخص عليّ كريم, 'a person dear to me'; the supplied spelling appears to be a typing or OCR error.

On the house (dār), line 1
O dwelling, changed by passing time and decay,between al-Salīl and Maʾmī Akbād!
يا دار غيرها التقادم والبلىبين السليل ومأمي أكباد

The locations are unidentified. مأمي أكباد, provisionally transliterated Maʾmī Akbād, is unclear and may be corrupted; it could represent مآمي أكباد, 'the wastes of Akbād.'

On the house (dār), line 5
They have a love akin to ours that draws us near;my heart and liver have wasted away yearning for that nearness.
لهم هوى من هوانا ما يقربناماتت على قربه الأحشاء والكبد

The syntax of لهم هوى من هوانا ما يقربنا and the reference of قربه are unclear. The translation tentatively understands a shared love that brings the lovers near, and yearning for that nearness. The transmitted wording may be defective.

On the house (dār), line 4
Then death comes suddenly—what is a prudent, sensible man to do?
والموت يأتي بعد ذا بغتةماذا بفعل الحازم العاقل

The text reads بفعل, which appears to be a misprint for يفعل, ‘does’ or ‘will do’; the translation follows that correction.

On the house (dār), line 1
And an abode of honor, where you have sanctioned the humiliationof your prophet, though the guest is not dishonored.
ودار حفاظ قد حللتم مهانةبها نبيكم، والضيف غير مهان

The wording is uncertain and may be corrupt. The translation tentatively reads حللتم as ḥallaltum, 'you sanctioned,' and مهانة ... نبيكم as 'the humiliation of your prophet.' حللتم could instead mean 'you took up residence,' but the remaining wording then does not yield a clear construction. The prophet intended is unidentified.

On the house (dār), line 3
Is this longing for the traces of Rāma, afterthe east and north winds have come to know its landmarks?
أصبابة برسوم رامة بعدماعرفت معارفها الصبا والشمأل

عرفت معارفها is translated literally as “have come to know its landmarks,” with the winds as subject. The expression is unusual and may contain a textual error, possibly concealing a verb meaning that the winds effaced the landmarks.

On the house (dār), line 3
Then the land behind Jāsim, then the valleys of al-Ṣufr,the dwelling of tribes and white camels.
فقفا جاسم، فأودية الصفر مغى قبائل وهجان

مغى appears to be a misprint for مغنى, “dwelling.” هجان is taken here as white, thoroughbred camels, though the word can also denote purity of lineage. The reading of this hemistich is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 1
Death is a gate that everyone must enter;would that I knew: what dwelling lies beyond the gate?
الموت باب وكل الناس داخلهفليست شعري بعد الباب ما الدار؟

فليست شعري appears to be a misprint for فليت شعري, “would that I knew,” which is the reading translated here.

On the house (dār), line 1
Dwellings lie effaced in the villages of al-Khābūr, alteredafter their people left, by dust-laden winds and rain.
دور عفت بقرى الخابور غيرهابعد الأنيس سوا في الريح والمطر

The text’s «سوا في» appears to be an erroneous splitting of «سوافي», understood here as dust-laden or dust-driving winds.

On the house (dār), line 2
How did you find travelers who had journeyedthrough as much darkness and daylight as your people wished?
كيف اهتديت لراحلين ترودواما شاء قومك من دجى ونهار

ترودوا is uncertain here. I have understood it as تروّدوا, 'wandered' or 'journeyed.' It may instead be a misprint for تزودوا, 'took provisions,' which would make darkness and daylight their figurative provisions.

On the house (dār), line 5
Nothing remains of it but blazing anguishin the heart, whose fire remembrance feeds.
لم يبقى منه سوى جوى متسعرفي القلب يذكى ناره التذكار

لم يبقى appears to be a spelling or transcription error for لم يبق, the expected form after لم.

On the house (dār), line 7
I knew there wide-eyed oryx, before whose veilsstood lions of al-Sharā: whoever fought them met death.
عهدت بها عين ألمها دون حجبهاأسود الشرى يلقى الردى من تصاوله

عين ألمها appears to be a typing or OCR error for عين المها, 'wide-eyed oryx.' al-Sharā is apparently the place traditionally associated with lions; its precise location is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 1
O dwelling, you are the one where everyone once gathered,and within your grounds were boys and retainers.
يا دار أنت التي كانت الجميع بهاوكان في ربعك الولدان والحشم

The wording كانت الجميع بها has unexpected feminine agreement in كانت with الجميع. It may contain a textual error; the translation follows the apparent sense, 'where everyone once gathered.'

On the house (dār), line 4
The blows of fate destroyed them, leavingnothing of them but the memory of a dreamer’s dream.
أفناهم ريب المنون فلم يدعمنهم سوى ذكر لحلم الحالم

The phrase «ذكر لحلم الحالم» is uncertain. Translated literally here as a memory of a dreamer’s dream, it may contain a misprint for «ذكر كحلم الحالم», ‘a memory like a dreamer’s dream.’ Alternatively, حلم الحالم could mean ‘the forbearing man’s forbearance.’

On the house (dār), line 3
They said, “Come to your senses! Do you weep for the earth?” I said, “No,but I weep for those whom the earth has buried.”
وقالوا: أفق، للأرض تبكي؟ فقلت: لاولكنني أبكي لمن وارث الأرض

The source reads وارث الأرض, which appears corrupt. The translation assumes وارت الأرض, ‘the earth has covered/buried,’ with لمن referring to those buried.

On the house (dār), line 1
Indeed, a man whose home is now in Irbil,while his brothers and his heart’s attachments are in Shayzar,
وإن امرأ أضحت بإربل دارهوفي سيزر إخوانه وشجونه

The source’s سيزر appears to be a misprint for شيزر, Shayzar, the poet’s hometown.

On the house (dār), line 1
O dwelling whose people have gone far away,though against my will your inhabitants departed.
فيا أيها الدار التي شط أهلهاوبالرغم مني أن سكانها شطوا

The address أيها الدار is grammatically irregular: with the feminine الدار, أيتها الدار would normally be expected. It may be a textual error.

On the house (dār), line 4
O men, come to the aid of a captive held in bondage:his own gaze has brought affliction upon him.
يا للرجال لأسر مرتهنجلب البلاء عليه ناظره

لأسر مرتهن is uncertain as written. The translation assumes a captive is meant; لأسر may be a defective spelling of لأسير. Alternatively, أسر could mean 'captivity,' giving 'the captivity of one held in pledge.'

On the house (dār), line 2
An abode—I hold love too sacred to stop thereamong the riders unless my eye streams with tears for it.
دار أجل الهوى عن أن ألم بهافي الركب إلا ويعين من متائحها

ويعين من متائحها appears corrupt. The translation tentatively understands an eye pouring out tears for the dwelling, perhaps underlying وبعين or وعيني. The precise reading and the sense of متائحها remain uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 3
You two, pause there a little for me; I ask noless than a glance to take as provision.
قفا قليلا بها على فلاأقل من نظرة أزودها

على appears to stand for عليّ (‘for me’), with the final letter misprinted or misrecognized. أزودها is understood as taking the glance as provision for departure.

On the house (dār), line 3
The dwellings reminded me of love, though they were ruins;what then if they had not been ruins?
ذكرتني الهوى وهن رميمكيف لو لم يكن كن رميما؟

The feminine plural pronoun هن apparently refers to the dwellings or their remains. The sequence يكن كن in the second hemistich looks corrupted, perhaps through duplication; the translation assumes لم يكنّ رميماً, ‘had not been ruins.’

On the house (dār), line 2
Time has altered some of its familiar features since I left,and the wind as well; its dwelling sites lie buried there.
قد غير الدهر بعدي من معارفهاوالريح، فادفنت فيها مغانيها

فادفنت appears irregular or misprinted, possibly for فاندفنت, 'and became buried'; the translation follows that sense.

On the house (dār), line 2
I stood there, and my tears were held backthere by my eye—save those with which I checked my gaze.
وقفت بها، فاستوقفت ماء عبرتيبها العين، إلا ما كففت به طرفي

The wording is obscure and possibly corrupt. The translation follows فاستوقفت literally as “held back,” but فاستوكفت, suggesting the drawing forth of tears, may have been intended. The phrase إلا ما كففت به طرفي, rendered literally as “save those with which I checked my gaze,” is also unclear.

On the house (dār), line 3
It lay desolate, its people having departed;what destroyed Lubad has laid it waste.
أضحت قفارا وأضحى أهلها احتملواأخنني عليها الذي أخني على لبد

The forms أخنني and أخني appear to be transcription errors for أخنى ('destroyed' or 'laid waste'), the reading followed here.

On the house (dār), line 2
The tearful one, weeping from longing and anguish,or the other, who weeps over his sorrow and wanders distraught?
أمستعبرا تبكي من الشوق والجوىأم آخر يبكي شجوه ويهيم

The wording أمستعبرا تبكي is grammatically uncertain: masculine مستعبرا is followed by تبكي, which can mean 'she weeps' or 'you weep.' The context suggests a contrast between the weeping dwelling and the poet, followed in the translation, but the text may be corrupt.

On the house (dār), line 4
My heart refused all but love of Buthna; it wantedno other, yet my heart’s love for Buthna avails nothing.
أنى القلب إلا حب بثنة لم يردسواها، وحب القلب بثنة لا يجدي

أنى appears to be a misprint for أبى, “refused,” which is the reading translated here.

On the house (dār), line 7
By your life, on the day at Jarʿāʾ Mālik,I was weary with tears that overflowed and choked me.
لعمرك إني يوم جرعاء مالكلذو عبرة كل تفيض وتخنق

The wording كل تفيض is difficult. The translation tentatively reads كل as كَلٌّ, ‘weary,’ describing the speaker, with تفيض referring back to his tears. The construction is uncertain, and the text may be corrupt.

On the house (dār), line 2
At times my eyes are flooded with tears,and my sight grows dim; at times they clear, and I see.
فعيناني طورا تغرقان من البكافأعشى، وطورا يحسران فأبصر

«عيناني» is unusual where standard grammar would have «عيناي» (‘my two eyes’); it may reflect poetic license or a textual error. «يحسران» (‘they recede’) is understood as the tears subsiding and the eyes clearing.

On the house (dār), line 1
My two friends of Ghayṭ ibn Murra, conveymessages from me—I shall not burden you further.
خليلي من غيط بن مرة بلغارسائل مني، لا أزيد كما وقرا

The name غيط بن مرة (Ghayṭ ibn Murra) probably contains a misprint for غيظ بن مرة (Ghayẓ ibn Murra), the tribal ancestor. The translation retains the printed form.

On the house (dār), line 3
I draw out conversation for her sake,to hear some mention of her, though she is far away.
وإني لأستثني الحديث لأجلهالأسمع منها وهي نازحة ذكرا

أستثني الحديث is unclear: the usual meaning of أستثني, ‘I except/exclude,’ does not readily fit. ‘Draw out conversation’ is a tentative contextual rendering; the text may be corrupt.

On the house (dār), line 5
At evening I wrap my cloak about my breast,as though my breast beneath it were ablaze with embers.
عشية ألوي بالرداء على الحشاكأن الحشا من دونه مشعر جمرا

مشعر جمرا is grammatically and lexically uncertain as printed. The translation tentatively understands it as describing the breast or inward parts as kindled with embers; a textual error is possible.

On the house (dār), line 4
Extinguish your love for her, and in place of union with herand seeing her, set likenesses of those you do not live beside.
أمت حبها، واجعل مكان وصالهاورؤيتها أمثال من لا تجاور

The construction اجعل مكان وصالها ورؤيتها أمثال من لا تجاور is obscure. 'Set likenesses of those you do not live beside' closely follows the wording, but the intended substitution is unclear; the text may be defective.

On the house (dār), line 2
He is like a woman in labor, assailed by birth pangs:she grows still, but he can find no rest.
فهو كالماخض التي اعتادها الطلق، فقرت، وما يقر قزاره

The wording فقرت ... قزاره is uncertain. I take فقرت as ‘she grows still’ and provisionally read قزاره as قراره (‘his repose’), treating it as a typographical or OCR error.

On the house (dār), line 4
Or if you leave him to ruin—how,and why, should he perish while you are alive?
أو تدعه إلى البوار فأني؟ولماذا وأنت حي بواره؟

فأني is read as فأنّى (‘how?’), apparently a spelling or OCR error.

On the house (dār), line 2
But when I returned, you doubled my suffering and gave me still moretorment and rejection, though you were near.
فأضعفت ما بين حين أبت وزدتنيعذابا وإعراضا وأنت قريب

The wording ما بين حين أبت is unclear and appears corrupt. The translation tentatively reads ما بي حين أبت, ‘what I suffered when I returned,’ taking أبت as the first-person past tense of آب, ‘to return.’

On the house (dār), line 2
I love them both, and then give my wealth,and those who blame me have no cause for reproach.
أحبهما وأبذل بعد ماليوليس للائمي فيها عتاب

The wording «وأبذل بعد مالي» is awkward. The translation provisionally treats «بعد» as an adverb meaning 'then'; the word may be a misprint.

On the house (dār), line 1
Have you broken your pledge between us,while the diviners come to regret?
أقطعت عهدك بينناوالحازيات إلى ندامه

الحازيات is obscure in this context. It is tentatively understood as female diviners, but its connection with إلى ندامه, ‘to regret,’ is unclear; the text may be corrupt.

On the house (dār), line 4
You sold your cousin’s house,with which remorse is bought off from you.
دار ابن عمك بعتهاتشرى بها عنك الندامة

تشرى بها عنك الندامة is translated provisionally and literally as remorse being bought off. The wording is difficult to reconcile with the reproach and may be corrupt.

On the house (dār), line 4
O daughter of al-Ḍabbī,has not passed away?
يا ابنة الضبيلم يحل؟

The identity of 'the daughter of al-Ḍabbī' is unclear, and the wording may be corrupt. لم يحل is provisionally read as lam yaḥul, 'has not changed/passed away.'

On the house (dār), line 2
My bones have been worn awayby its faded traces, after love had wasted them, as a woodworker pares a shawḥaṭ shaft.
أبلى عظاميبعد الحب دارسها كما تتبع عود الشوحط الباري

The supplied hemistich division appears displaced, but is preserved. I take دارسها ('its faded traces') as the subject of أبلى and بعد الحب as 'after love [had wasted them]'; the wording is somewhat uncertain and may be corrupt.

On the house (dār), line 3
Will you forever keep dying of grief for Laylā,at a stopping place where you stood, or beside a dwelling?
ما تبرح الدهر من ليلى تموت جفافي موقف وقفته أو على دار؟

جفا is unclear in this construction. The translation provisionally assumes a misprint for جوى ('consuming grief'); a connection with جفاء ('estrangement') is also possible.

On the house (dār), line 2
Do you stem my tears for fear of tale-bearers,then pour them forth in streams when you are alone?
أتغيض من حذر الوساة مدامعيفإذا خلوت تفيضهن سجوما؟

الوساة appears to be a misprint for الوشاة, “tale-bearers” or “slanderers.”

On the house (dār), line 7
Her neck gleams, and her upper breast is bright,as though she were a gazelle brought into view by a sandy slope.
براقة الجيد، واللبات واضحةكأنها طبية أفضى بها لبب

طبية appears to be a misprint or OCR error for ظبية, 'gazelle.' لبب denotes a low or sloping stretch of sand; the precise spatial image in أفضى بها لبب is somewhat uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 2
And your little tents at the bend of al-Liwāhave suffered a decay no other encampments have known.
وخيماتك اللاني بمنعرج اللوىبلين بلى لم تبلهن ربوع

اللاني is probably a misprint for اللاتي, ‘which.’ The wording لم تبلهن ربوع is grammatically problematic; ‘no other encampments have known’ is a conjectural rendering. Al-Liwā may be a place-name or a description of winding sands.

On the house (dār), line 3
There was a time when people sought my intercession;is there anyone to intercede for me with Lubnā this morning?
مضى زمن والناس يستشفعون بينفهل لي إلى لبنى الغداة شفيع؟

بين appears to be a misprint for بي, ‘through me,’ giving ‘people sought my intercession.’

On the house (dār), line 4
Indeed, I have learned, despite all striving, thathearts suffer and fate prevails.
ولقد علمت على التكالف أنهتشقى القلوب وتغلب الأفدار

الأفدار appears to be a misprint for الأقدار, ‘fate’ or ‘decrees of fate.’ التكالف is also unusual and may be a corruption of التكلف, ‘striving’ or ‘taking pains’; ‘despite all striving’ is tentative.

On the house (dār), line 2
Let it be a detour that God will recompense you for in His keepingwith reward—or let a friend’s claim be fulfilled.
تكن عوجة بجزيكما الله عندهبها الأجر، أو تقضى ذمامة صاحب

بجزيكما appears to be a misprint for يجزيكما, “He recompenses you both.” تقضى is understood as passive, “be fulfilled.”

On the house (dār), line 4
My soul defied me there, ever turning back to passion;whenever passion called it, it offered no resistance.
عصتني بها نفس تريع إلى الهوىإذا مد دعاها دعوة لم تغالب

إذا مد appears to be corrupted; the translation assumes إذا ما, “whenever.” The unvocalized لم تغالب is ambiguous: it is rendered actively, “offered no resistance,” but a passive reading, “could not be restrained,” is also possible.

On the house (dār), line 1
Halt the pale camels: weariness has shortened their steps;And question Saʿdā’s dwelling, if questioning it can heal you.
قف العيسى قد أدنى خطاها كلالهاوسل دار سعدى إن شفاك سؤالها

العيسى appears to be a typographical or OCR error for العيس, “pale camels,” which is the reading translated here.

On the house (dār), line 2
O ruined campsite, whose beauty the wind has tugged at,spending the night now spreading it out, now folding it away.
يا دمنة جاذيتها الريح بهجتهاتبيت تنشرها طورا وتطويها

جاذيتها appears to be a misprint for جاذبتها, ‘contended with it for’ or ‘tugged at,’ which is the reading followed here.

On the house (dār), line 2
May rain bless your people—a tribe scatteredby the blows of fate and journeys in widely differing directions.
سقيا لأهلك من حي تقسهمريب المنون وطيات عباديد

تقسهم appears defective; I read it as تقسمهم, ‘scattered them.’ طيات can denote journeys, destinations, or directions taken on departure; the precise sense here is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 2
I recognized a dwelling of hers, and my companion noticedhow the look of my face had changed.
عرفت لها دارا، فأبصر صاحبيصيفة وجهي قد تغير حالها

صيفة is unclear and may be a misprint for صفة, “appearance” or “aspect,” which is the reading followed here.

On the house (dār), line 1
O lightning, al-Karkh is not my home; rather,fate cast me there some nights ago.
فيا برق ليس الكرخ داري وإنمارماني إليه لدهر منذ ليال

لدهر appears to be a typographical or OCR error for الدهر, ‘fate’ or ‘time,’ which I have translated.

On the house (dār), line 1
If a dwelling could tell of its people,I would ask Rāma about the gazelles of its covert.
لون دارا أخبرت عن ناسهالسألت رامة عن ظباء كناسها

The opening لون appears corrupted. The translation reads it as لو أن, ‘if a dwelling …’.

On the house (dār), line 5
From you I hold grants of land, old and new,on which I have lived part of my life beneath your shade.
ولي منك إقطاع قديم وحادثتقلبت منه تحت ظلك من عمري

The syntax of the second hemistich, particularly منه and من عمري, is awkward and possibly defective. The translation takes it to mean that the poet has spent part of his life supported by these land grants under the patron’s protection.

On the house (dār), line 7
But I seek to hold them as property in perpetuity,enduring as the verses that remain through time.
وكلنني أبغية ملكا مخلداخلود القوافي الباقيات على الدهر

وكلنني أبغية appears to contain typing or OCR errors for ولكنني أبغيه, ‘but I seek it,’ which is the reading translated.

On the house (dār), line 2
May a downpour heed your soil, deliberately seeking it,rather than being driven about by east or south winds.
وأطاع تربك وابل متعمدمن أن تزعزعه صبا وجنوب

The construction متعمد من أن is grammatically unclear and may be corrupt. The translation tentatively understands the rain as deliberately seeking the dwelling, rather than being carried there by winds.

On the house (dār), line 3
How lovely the water of al-Furāt—if only itcould quench the burning thirst of the drinker himself consumed.
يا حبذا ماء الفرات لو أنهيشفي غليل الشارب المشروب

المشروب literally means 'drunk' or 'drunk up.' Applied to the drinker, it may suggest someone consumed by longing, but this unusual epithet is uncertain; a textual error is also possible.

On the house (dār), line 3
In this abode, in this place, uponthis throne I saw glory—and it passed away.
في هذا الدار، في هذا المكان علىهذا السرير رأيت العز فانقرضا

هذا الدار has an unexpected masculine demonstrative with the normally feminine dār; هذه الدار would be expected, suggesting a possible textual error.

On the house (dār), line 2
God’s earth lies spread out for His creatures,and sustenance is apportioned in every place.
أرضى الإله لخلقه مبسوطةوالرزق مقسوم بكل مكان

أرضى الإله appears to be a misprint for أرض الإله, “God’s earth,” which is the reading translated here.

On the house (dār), line 2
Nothing remained of the dwelling when I came upon itbut the places where tent ropes and pegs had been set.
الدار لم يبق منها ريثما لقيتإلا مضارب أطناب وأوتاد

ريثما لقيت is syntactically awkward. The translation provisionally takes it as 'when I came upon it,' with an implied object; the transmitted wording may be defective.

On the house (bayt), line 4
Then Quraysh divided the Kaʿba among themselves. The side containing the door fell to Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Zuhra. The stretch between the Black Corner and the Yamānī Corner fell to Banū Makhzūm and those clans of Quraysh that joined them. The back of the Kaʿba fell to Banū Jumaḥ and Sahm, the two sons of ʿAmr ibn Huṣayṣ ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy. The side adjoining the Ḥijr fell to Banū ʿAbd al-Dār ibn Quṣayy, Banū Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Quṣayy, and Banū ʿAdī ibn Luʾayy; this is the Ḥaṭīm, the site of the idol. Then the people shrank from demolishing it and were afraid to do so. Al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra said, “I shall be the first of you to demolish it.” He took a pickaxe, then stood upon it, saying, “O God, be not alarmed, for we intend only good.” Then he demolished part of it on the side of the two corners. The people waited that night and said, “We shall see: if he is afflicted, we shall demolish nothing and shall restore it as it was. But if nothing befalls him, then God has approved what we have done, and we shall proceed with the demolition.” In the morning al-Walīd went early to his work and continued demolishing, and the people demolished with him, until they reached the foundations of Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him. They uncovered green stones like spearheads, interlocking with one another, [] .
ثم إن قريشا تجزأت الكعبة، فكان شق الباب لبني عبد مناف وزهرة، وكان ما بين الركن الأسود، والركن اليماني لبني مخزوم وقبائل من قريش انضموا إليهم، وكان ظهر الكعبة لبني جمح وسهم، ابني عمرو بن هصيص بن كعب بن لؤي، وكان شق الحجر لبني عبد الدار بن قصي، ولبني أسد بن عبد العزى بن قصي، ولبني عدي بن لؤي، وهو الحطيم موضع الصنم. ثم إن الناس هابوا هدمها، وفرقوا منه، فقال الوليد بن المغيرة: أنا أبدو كم في هدمها، فأخذ المعول، ثم قام عليها وهو يقول: اللهم لم ترع، فإنا لا نريد إلا الخير، ثم هدم من ناحية الركنين، فتربص الناس تلك الليلة، وقالوا: ننظر، إن أصيب لم نهدم شيئا، ورددناها كما كانت، وإن لم يصبه شيء فقد رضي الله بما صنعنا فهدمنا، فأصبح الوليد غاديا على عمله، وهدم وهدم الناس، حتى انتهى الهدم بهم إلى أساس إبراهيم عليه السلام، فأفضوا إلى حجارة خضر كالأسنة أخذ بعضها ببعض، [] .

أبدو كم appears to be a spacing or transcription error for أبدؤكم, “I shall begin before you / be the first of you.” The unusual invocation لم ترع is translated literally as “be not alarmed.”

On the house (bayt), line 4
Then Quraysh divided the Kaʿba among themselves. The side containing the door fell to Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Zuhra. The stretch between the Black Corner and the Yamānī Corner fell to Banū Makhzūm and those clans of Quraysh that joined them. The back of the Kaʿba fell to Banū Jumaḥ and Sahm, the two sons of ʿAmr ibn Huṣayṣ ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy. The side adjoining the Ḥijr fell to Banū ʿAbd al-Dār ibn Quṣayy, Banū Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Quṣayy, and Banū ʿAdī ibn Luʾayy; this is the Ḥaṭīm, the site of the idol. Then the people shrank from demolishing it and were afraid to do so. Al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra said, “I shall be the first of you to demolish it.” He took a pickaxe, then stood upon it, saying, “O God, be not alarmed, for we intend only good.” Then he demolished part of it on the side of the two corners. The people waited that night and said, “We shall see: if he is afflicted, we shall demolish nothing and shall restore it as it was. But if nothing befalls him, then God has approved what we have done, and we shall proceed with the demolition.” In the morning al-Walīd went early to his work and continued demolishing, and the people demolished with him, until they reached the foundations of Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him. They uncovered green stones like spearheads, interlocking with one another, [] .
ثم إن قريشا تجزأت الكعبة، فكان شق الباب لبني عبد مناف وزهرة، وكان ما بين الركن الأسود، والركن اليماني لبني مخزوم وقبائل من قريش انضموا إليهم، وكان ظهر الكعبة لبني جمح وسهم، ابني عمرو بن هصيص بن كعب بن لؤي، وكان شق الحجر لبني عبد الدار بن قصي، ولبني أسد بن عبد العزى بن قصي، ولبني عدي بن لؤي، وهو الحطيم موضع الصنم. ثم إن الناس هابوا هدمها، وفرقوا منه، فقال الوليد بن المغيرة: أنا أبدو كم في هدمها، فأخذ المعول، ثم قام عليها وهو يقول: اللهم لم ترع، فإنا لا نريد إلا الخير، ثم هدم من ناحية الركنين، فتربص الناس تلك الليلة، وقالوا: ننظر، إن أصيب لم نهدم شيئا، ورددناها كما كانت، وإن لم يصبه شيء فقد رضي الله بما صنعنا فهدمنا، فأصبح الوليد غاديا على عمله، وهدم وهدم الناس، حتى انتهى الهدم بهم إلى أساس إبراهيم عليه السلام، فأفضوا إلى حجارة خضر كالأسنة أخذ بعضها ببعض، [] .

كالأسنة means “like spearheads,” as translated. It may be a transcription error for كالأسنمة, “like camel humps,” the reading found in the familiar account of the Kaʿba’s rebuilding.

On the house (bayt), line 9
How many radiant stars of good fortune have fallen and shoneamong them—and how many peerless pearls of glory!
كم من درارى سعود قد هوت وزهتمنهم، ومن درر للمجد أفراد

The text reads «هوت وزهت», translated literally as “have fallen and shone.” «زهت» normally suggests shining, flourishing, or being splendid; its coordination with “fallen” is puzzling in this context and may reflect a textual error.

On the house (bayt), line 2
Separation is nothing but this: after sound health, we areas though we had never spent nights with Wāʾil or rested beside him at noon.
وما البعد إلا أننا بعد صحةكأن لم نبايت وائلا ونقايله

بعد صحة literally means 'after health.' Its connection to the rest of the sentence is awkward; the wording may be defective.

On the house (bayt), line 1
O house of ʿĀtika, which I shunfor fear of enemies, while my heart remains bound to it.
يا بيت عائكة التي أتعزلحذر العدى، وبه الفؤاد موكل

The source reads عائكة, apparently a misprint for عاتكة (ʿĀtika), adopted here. The feminine relative التي is also unexpected if it refers to بيت; الذي would fit the apparent sense.

On the house (bayt), line 2
I turn away from you, yet Iswear that, despite my turning away, I incline toward you.
إني لأمنحك الصدود وإننيقسما إيك مع الصدود لأميل

إيك appears to be a misprint for إليك, 'toward you,' adopted in the translation.

On the house (bayt), line 5
Though I turn away, you are—but for my fear of watchers—dearer than the houses I visit and enter.
ولئن صددت لأنتلولا رقبتي أهوى من اللائي أزور وأدخل

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: h1 is unusually short and h2 unusually long. It is preserved here. رقبتي is also uncertain; it may concern the speaker’s vigilance or those watching him. 'Houses' is supplied as the apparent referent of اللائي.

On the house (bayt), line 4
My visits, once accepted, are now disapproved of,and hearts have grown bitter against me because of them.
فقد أنكرت بعد اعتراف زيارتيوقد وغرت فيها على صدور

I read على as عليّ ('against me'), probably a typing or OCR error. The unvocalized أنكرت is taken as passive ('are disapproved of'); it could also mean 'she disapproved of my visits.'

On the house (bayt), line 4
Dwelling as neighbors, though not in a lasting home;their departure had indeed become pressing, yet they felt no regret.
متجاورين بغير دار إقامةول قد أجد رحيلهم لم يندموا

«ول قد» appears corrupted or incorrectly spaced. The translation provisionally reads «ولقد أجد رحيلهم», ‘their departure had indeed become pressing’; the intended wording and connection remain uncertain.

On the house (bayt), line 2
What a delightful house you are to me!Yet lovelier in my eyes than the house is its inhabitant.
لهنك من بيت إلى لمونقوآنق في عيني من البيت عامره

Read إلى as إليّ, “to me,” and لمونق as لمؤنق, “indeed delightful.” The transmitted spelling appears defective.

On the house (bayt), line 2
A word from you—if you would offer it—is the bees’ honey in the milk of newly calved she-camels nursing their young.
وإن حديثا منك لو تبدلينهجنى النحل في ألبان عوذ مطافل

The text has تبدلينه, normally meaning ‘you exchange/change it.’ I have provisionally read تبذلينه, ‘you offer it,’ which fits the context; the printed form may be a transcription error.

On the house (bayt), line 1
O house upon the heights, O house!But for my love of your people, I would not have come.
ألا يا بيت بالعلياء بيتولولا حب أهلك ما أتيت

The final بيت is syntactically unclear; it is rendered as a repeated address, though the text may be corrupt. العلياء may mean 'the heights' or be the place-name al-ʿAlyāʾ.

On the house (bayt), line 3
And may you dwell among folk with no neighborly contact between them,and no reunion unless the dead rise again.
وجاورت قوما لا تجاور بينهمولا وصل إلا أن يكون نشور

The wording لا تجاور بينهم is unusual; translated here as 'no neighborly contact between them.' تجاور may be a misprint for تزاور, 'mutual visiting.'

On the house (bayt), line 2
a house in whose courtyard your smith finishes his work,its seats filthy, its fare foul.
بيتا يتمم قينكم بفنائهدنس مقاعده خبيث المأكل

The reading يتمم is uncertain. Read literally as 'completes,' it lacks an explicit object; 'his work' is supplied tentatively. The text may be corrupt.

On the house (bayt), line 3
And may He greet Abū Nujayd with peace;and tell him: greetings and well-being.
وحيا بالسلام أبا نجيدوقل له التحية والسلامة

حيا is read here as a past-tense verb expressing a wish, continuing the prayer to God. The following قل, however, addresses the traveler directly; حيا may instead be a textual error for the imperative حيّ, ‘greet.’ Abū Nujayd has not been securely identified.

On the house (bayt), line 1
A house that rivals the clouds—indeed,its tears, when shed, are more abundant than theirs.
وبيت تساوى والغمام وإنهلآغزر منها دمعة حين تذرف

لآغزر appears to be a misprint for لأغزر, ‘more abundant.’

On the house (bayt), line 3
My robe—from the dripping of its black roofand its red earth—is a striped mantle.
فثؤبي من توكاف أسود سقفهوتربته الحمراء برد مفوف

فثؤبي appears to be a misprint for فثوبي, ‘so my robe.’

On the house (bayt), line 1
The spider has built a house, frail though it is,where it takes shelter; yet I have no home as it does.
العنكبوت بنت بيتا على وهوتأوى إليه ومالي مثلها وطن

على وهو appears corrupt, probably for على وهن, referring to the weakness of the spider’s house; the translation follows that reading.

On the house (bayt), line 3
I asked him, “How long has this mat been here,and how long have you gone without reciting the supplication upon it?”
فقلت له: كم لهذا الحصير، وكم لك لم تقر فيه القنوت؟

The form تقر appears to stand for تقرأ, “recite,” perhaps through poetic shortening or a textual error. القنوت is understood here as the supplication recited during prayer.

On the house (bayt), line 5
So take this house and conceal yourself within it;the grave conceals still better, if you will accept it.
فدنونك هذا البيت فاستتري بهوأستر منه إن رضيت به القبر

فدنونك appears to be a typing or OCR error for فدونك, ‘so take’ or ‘here is … for you.’

On the house (bayt), line 2
Estrangement has taken such hold of you that it is as thoughyou see death in the house you once frequented.
ولج بك الهجران حتى كأنماترى الموت في البيت الذي كنت تيلف

تيلف is understood as تألف, meaning to be familiar with or frequent a place. It may represent a dialectal pronunciation or a textual error.

On the house (bayt), line 2
I would give my life for the one I am barred from meeting,for him whose love weighs heavily upon me.
بنفسي من قد حيل دون لقائهومن حبه حب على ثقيل

على is read as عليّ, 'upon me,' likely a typing or OCR error. The second hemistich is understood literally as 'and him, love of whom is a love heavy upon me.'

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
Men who held the first fruits of glory; there was no fearfor their neighbor of the blows of fate or reversals.
رجالا له ربعية المجد لم يخفمجاورهم ريب الحوادث والزلل

The phrase له ربعية المجد is unclear and may be corrupt. The translation provisionally reads له as لهم, referring to the men, and takes ربعية المجد as an image of glory's early or first yield.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
They were like an archer's arrows in a quiver;then it was left without a single arrow.
وكانوا كنبل المرتمى في كنانةفأضحت وما فهيا من النبل أهزع

فهيا appears to be a typo for فيها, 'in it.' I take المرتمى to mean 'archer,' normally written المرتمي.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
So I shall surely shoot back at them,in defiance of them, forever, though bereft of young warriors.
فلأرمينهمبرغم أنوفهم أبدا على عدم من الفتيان

The hemistich division appears misplaced: برغم أنوفهم likely belongs with the first hemistich. The translation preserves the supplied division.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
A brother—I have no brother but him—yet I am like one watching a phantom, wandering without thought.
أخ لا أخا لي غيره، غير أنني كراعي الخيال يستطيف بلا فكر

The phrase كراعي الخيال يستطيف بلا فكر is obscure and may be corrupt. The rendering 'like one watching a phantom, wandering without thought' is tentative: the precise sense of يستطيف and whether its subject is the watcher or the phantom are uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
Defenders who protected their sacred charges and kept watchin the abode of death, with spears entangled.
محامين حاموا عن حريم، وحافظابدار المنايا، والقنا متشاجر

وحافظا is grammatically unclear after the plural حاموا and may be corrupted. It is translated provisionally as though وحافظوا ('and kept watch' or 'and guarded') were intended.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
Men—their father and Abū ʿAmr, andKaʿb—fair-faced and handsome.
من رجال أبوهم وأبو عمرو وكعب بيض الوجوه وسام

The wording من رجال أبوهم is syntactically unclear and may be corrupt. أبوهم is translated literally as 'their father,' but its referent is uncertain. The source divides كعب (Kaʿb) between the two hemistichs; the complete name is placed in h2.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
They weresons of a shelter, many in number; now they are sons of the earth, which has buried all but one.
وكانوابني كن كثرا فأصبحوا بني الأرض، قد وارتهم غير واحد

بني كن is obscure. I have provisionally read كن as kinn, 'shelter'; the text may instead contain a corrupted word or name. The division between hemistichs also appears misplaced, but has been preserved as supplied.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
Umayma said: “Why has your body grown so palesince you began neglecting yourself, when wealth like yours can help?
قالت أميمة: ما لجسمك شاحبامنذ ابتدلت ومثل مالك ينفع

The source has ابتدلت, probably a misprint for ابتذلت, the familiar reading of this verse. The translation takes this as neglecting one's appearance or treating oneself roughly; the precise implication is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
For you—truly, what a watcher's gaze you cast, with Waqf and Qabr between you and her!
فإنكحقا أي نظرة ناظر نظرت، و"وقف" دونها و"قبر"

The opening syntax and hemistich division appear disrupted: h1 contains only فإنك. Waqf and Qabr are treated as place names because the source marks them as such, but their identification and vocalization are uncertain. The referent of the feminine pronoun in دونها is also unclear.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
The dwellings of her who said—on the morning I met her, “You have fallen in love, Abū Dhīb, though you are old.
ديار التي قالتغداة لقيتها صبوت أبا ذيب وأنت كبير

The source has أبا ذيب, rendered Abū Dhīb, rather than the poet's usual name Abū Dhuʾayb (أبو ذؤيب). This may reflect textual corruption.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
Have you changed since I left, or has some calamity befallen youfrom time, or have bitter trials passed over you?”
تغيرت بعدي أو أصابك حادثمن الدهر، أم مرت عليك مرور

مرور is obscure here. “Bitter trials” is a tentative interpretation; the word may be corrupt.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
Where are the kings, and the life they once lived,and the age that was theirs, and all they amassed?
أين الملوك، وعيشهم فيما مضىوزمانهم فيهم وما قد جمعوا؟

The phrase وزمانهم فيهم, literally something like “and their time among them,” is awkward and may be corrupt. “The age that was theirs” is a tentative rendering.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 7
Rather, we have journeyed through them with unyielding souls,laden with what they cannot bear, yet bearing it.
ولكن رحلناها نفوسا أبيةتحمل ما لا تستطيع فتحمل

رحلناها is unclear in this construction. 'Journeyed through them' tentatively takes the pronoun as referring to the days. The text may be corrupt, possibly for حملناها, suggesting that proud souls were made to bear these hardships.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
It is as though death had no people other than them,though in dealing with them it is impartial, with no special attachment.
كأنهم لا ناس للموت غيرهموإن كان فيهم منصف غير معتقد

The second hemistich is uncertain, especially غير معتقد. I have taken death as the implicit subject of كان and tentatively understood غير معتقد as denying any special attachment or partiality. The wording may be corrupt.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
But today,since distance has parted me from them, I weep for those I love.
فالقيومإذ فرقت بيني وبينهم نوى بكيت على أهل المودات

فالقيوم appears to be a misprint for فاليوم ('but today'), which is the reading translated here. The hemistich division also appears misplaced; the translation preserves the supplied division.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
And no words to which you send an answerback to us, nor any request you would make?
ولا من كلام ترجعون جوابهإلينا، ولا من حاجة تلطبونها

تلطبونها appears to be a typographical error for تطلبونها, “you seek” or “you ask for,” which is the reading translated here.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
I called out to fortune—if only I had called to one who listened—but fortune is too busy with fools to attend to me.
أثبت بالحظ لو ناديت مستعماوالحظ عني بالجهال في شغل

The first hemistich appears corrupted: أثبت بالحظ is likely أهبت بالحظ, ‘I called out to fortune,’ and مستعما is likely مستمعا, ‘one who listens.’ The translation follows these readings.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 5
And Bayhas said—he was nicknamed Naʿāmah.
وقال بيهسويلقب نعامة

This appears to be an editorial attribution introducing another poet, rather than a verse by al-Ṭughrāʾī. It has been translated in the supplied divisions.

On weeping for family and brothers, whole poem

The attribution is inconsistent: the poet field gives السد بن سرك, while the introduction gives السيد بن برك الأسدي. At least one form appears corrupted.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
When it settles within my ribs, it casts darknessover the morning light, until my family console me.
إذا وقعت بين الحيازيم أسدفتعلى الضحى حتى يوسيني أهلي

يوسيني is understood as يواسيني, 'console me'; the spelling may be defective. The construction أسدفت على الضحى is also unusual; على may represent عليّ, giving 'it darkened the morning light for me.'

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
I say—when I console myself for brothers departed, neither weak in life nor unarmed—
أقولإذا آسيت نفسي بإخوة مضوا لا ضعاف في الحياة ولا عزل

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: h1 contains only أقول, while h2 contains the rest of the verse. The supplied division has been retained.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 6
As though we had never lived a day in happiness,all together, with my camp pitched beside theirs.
كأنك لم نعش يوما، ونحن بغبطةجميعا، وينزل عند رحلهم رحلي

كأنك لم نعش mixes 'you' with 'we' and appears corrupt. The translation follows the probable sense, 'as though we had not lived,' possibly intended as كأنّا لم نعش.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 8
For a generous gamester among them who played the stakes, and a horseman,when calamity rode upon withers and humps.
على يسر منهم يسير، وفارسإذا ارتدف الشيء الحوارك والذرى

الشيء literally means “the thing.” Its reference is unclear, and the text may be corrupt. “Calamity” is a tentative interpretation of the image of something mounting the animals’ withers and humps.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 5
Death shot them with arrows without heads,neither straying nor defective,
رمتها المنون بلا نصلولا طائشات ولا نكس

نكس apparently describes defective arrows, possibly broken arrows reversed and refitted with heads. The precise technical sense here is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 8
That is what has undone me—know this,and ask not about a man who takes consolation.
فذاك الذي غالني فأعلميولا تسأللي بامرئ مؤتس

تسأللي appears to be a misprint for تسألي. The construction بامرئ مؤتس is unclear: مؤتس probably means someone who takes consolation, but its relationship to the prohibition against asking is uncertain. The second hemistich is translated provisionally.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
Oh, my grief for one dead at Naʿmān—for the young man!And my grief for one dead at Qaws al-Maʿāqil!
فلهفي على ميت بنعمان للفتىولهفي على ميت بقوس المعاقل

The phrase للفتى, literally “for the young man,” is syntactically awkward here and may reflect a textual error. It has been retained rather than silently emended.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
I was a man steadfast in whatever befell me,and accepting the need for patience in calamity.
وكن امرأ جلدا على ما ينوبنيومعترفا بالصبر عند النوائب

وكن appears to be a misprint for وكنت ('and I was'), which fits the first-person context. The translation follows that reading.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
The carefree man slept, while I spent the night propped on my elbow,like one who turns aside, fearing blows to his flank.
نام الخلي، وبت الليل مرتفقاكما تزاور يخشى دفه النكب

The second hemistich is unclear and may be corrupted. The rendering is tentative: تزاور suggests turning or leaning aside, and دفه may mean 'his flank,' but I cannot confidently resolve النكب or the clause's syntax.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 8
I am left like a birdwith clipped plumage and feeble flight feathers.
فبقيت كالطير المقصض ريشه واهي القوادم

المقصض appears corrupt, probably for المقصص, ‘clipped,’ describing the bird’s plumage.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 11
Today I bow even to the lowly,to the hostile and the peaceable alike.
فاليوم أخضع للذليل وللمجارب والمسالم

المجارب may be a misprint for المحارب, ‘the hostile one’ or ‘one who wages war,’ contrasting with المسالم, ‘the peaceable one.’ The translation follows that conjecture.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
It destroyed my men, and they hastened away together;my heart is left distraught for them.
وأفنى رجالي، فبادروا معافأصبح قلبي لهم مستفزا

فبادروا معا literally means 'they hastened together,' apparently implying departure in death. It may be a misprint for فبادوا معا, 'they perished together,' which would also fit the meter better.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
One woman asks about Tawba ibn Muḍarris,caring little for what Time has inflicted on him.
وسائلة عن توبة بن مصرسوهان عليها ما أصاب به الدهر

The verse gives the father's name as مصرس, apparently a misprint for مضرس (Muḍarris), the name supplied in the attribution.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 4
No, by your worthy father, my brothers were notmen who held aloof, misers when the rain failed.
فلا وأبيك الخير، ما كان إخوتيمعازيل أبراما إذا جارد القطر

جارد القطر is unclear as printed and may be corrupt; 'when the rain failed' is a conjectural rendering. معازيل can describe men who keep apart from others or who hold back from fighting; its precise sense here is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
Upon my head are calamities—many, if you only knew—that I have suffered unjustly, and for which I seek redress alone.
برأسي خطوبلو علمت كثيرة أصبت بها ظلما، وأطلبها وحدي

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: the likely division is after كثيرة, with أصبت beginning the second hemistich. The translation preserves the supplied division. وأطلبها is understood as seeking redress or vengeance for the wrongs suffered.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
Calamities assail a man while he is powerless,and the vicissitudes of time toy with the resolute and steadfast.
تعرى المصيبات الفتى وهو عاجزويلعب ريب الدهر بالجازم الجلد

تعرى appears to be a misprint for تعرو, ‘assail’ or ‘befall,’ which is the reading followed here.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
Do you not know that I have no brother in Rāwand,nor any drinking companion in Jazāq besides you two?
أم تعلما مالي براوند من أخولا بجزاق من نديم سواكما

أم تعلما appears defective; the translation assumes ألم تعلما, 'Do you not know?'

On weeping for family and brothers, line 7
I poured some wine upon your graves;if you do not taste it, it will moisten your earth.
أصبت على قبريكما من مدامةفإلا تذوقاها ترو ثراكما

أصبت is probably a misprint for أصببت, 'I poured,' which is the reading adopted here.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
When we come to you, we seek no watering placebut you, and we slake the thirst of our wasted bones.
وإنا إذا جئناك لم نبغ مشراسواك، وروينا العظام البواليا

The printed مشرا appears defective, probably for مشربا, ‘a drinking place’ or ‘source of drink,’ which is the reading translated here.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 7
Calamities have taken their due from me,and left no further claim against me.
لقد أخذت مني النوائب حقهافما تركت حقا على النوائب

على appears to be a misprint for عليّ ('against me'). The translation takes النوائب ('calamities') as the delayed subject of تركت.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 8
Nor have they left me fearing Time any longer:its fang and claws have grown blunt against me.
ولا تركتني أرهب الدهر بعدلقد كل عني بابه والمخالف

The second hemistich appears corrupt. بابه ('its door') and المخالف ('the opponent') are provisionally read as نابه ('its fang') and المخالب ('claws'); the latter also restores the rhyme. بعد at the end of the first hemistich may be incomplete.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
Had it not been for what is owed to the earth, it would not have taken themwithout its grasp first being broken by swords.
ولولا الذي للأرض ما ذهبت بهمولما يفلل بالسيوف جذابها

The exact sense of جذابها is uncertain. Rendered provisionally as “its grasp,” it may refer to the earth’s pulling or to those who seize on its behalf; the reading may be corrupt.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
They called to one another and said, “The horsemen have felled a rider!”I said, “Is that fallen man ʿAbd Allah?”
تنادوا، فقالا: أردت الخيل فارسافقلت: أعبد الله ذلكم الردى؟

فقالا (“the two said”) appears to be a misprint for فقالوا (“they said”), matching تنادوا (“they called to one another”).

On weeping for family and brothers, line 13
They sought glory; when they had attained it,by decree, and when that appointed term had expired,
طلبوا المجد فلما أدركوالكتاب وانتهى ذاك الأجل

لكتاب, rendered tentatively as 'by decree,' is syntactically awkward. Its connection with أدركوا and the following clause is uncertain, and the text may be defective.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
Men of mature years, mighty-necked and stouthearted,who cut the bonds of captives laden with chains.
من كهول غلب ملاويث قطساعين قد الأسير ذي الأغلال

قط / ساعين appears corrupt. The translation conjectures قطّاعين قِدَّ الأسير, 'cutting the captive’s leather bonds,' with قطّاعين spanning the hemistich break.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
After my radiant sons, those noble lords,can I cherish any hope or expect any bounty from time?
أبعد بني الزهر الغطارفة الألىأرجى رجاء أو نوالا من الدهر؟

I read بني الزهر as 'my radiant sons.' The unvocalized text could also suggest a group name, Banū al-Zuhr. الألى is syntactically unclear: ordinarily meaning 'who,' it has no evident relative clause here and may be misprinted.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 5
The days have dealt him harm until they left him,through the long years gone by, bereft of children.
أضرت به الأيام حتى تركنهبطول الذي عفين وهو رقوب

بطول الذي عفين is obscure and may be corrupt. 'Through the long years gone by' is tentative. رقوب denotes someone whose children have died or who has no surviving child.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 5
When they descend into al-Adawāt, with the sea between us,think how far apart we shall be till the end of time!
إذا هبطوا الأدوات، والبحر دوننافقل في تناء بيننا آخر الدهر

الأدوات is treated as a place-name, al-Adawāt, but I could not identify it; the reading may be corrupt.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 4
Had the swords whose edgesstruck you known what they were doing,
لو أن السيوف الذي حدهايصيبك تعلم ما تصنع

الذي does not agree grammatically with السيوف ('swords'); it may be a misprint for التي. The translation follows that reading.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 5
they would have glanced off you, or elseceased to cut, in awe and fear of your onslaught.
نبت عنك، أو جعلتهيبة وخوفا لصولك لا تقطع

The line appears metrically uneven as supplied, possibly because of a misplaced hemistich division or textual corruption. I take جعلت ... لا تقطع to mean that the swords would stop cutting.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
With it I would water the grave of him I mean—and how dearthat grave is to me, though no ransomer redeemed him!
أسقي به قبر من أعني، وحب بهقبرا إلي، وغن لم يفده فاد

The printed وغن appears to be a typographical or OCR error for وإن, 'though.'

On weeping for family and brothers, line 4
Let every army weep for al-Mughīra,whose battlefields run with surging blood.
ويبك على المغرة كل جيشتمور لدى معاركه الدماء

المغرة appears to be a typographical or OCR error for المغيرة, al-Mughīra.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
I remembered my upright kinsfolk, whenour mounts had passed Ḥamal, then Aʿfar.
تذكرت أهلي الصالحين وقد أتىعلى حمل منا الركاب فأعفرا

Ḥamal and Aʿfar appear to be place-names, but their locations are uncertain. The wording منا الركاب is awkward and may be corrupt; “our mounts” is a tentative rendering.

The meaning is unclear

The translator could not settle what the words mean or how they fit together.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
Or why do you weep in a dwelling where you once knewa familiar life, now changed—or at which of them will you stop?
أم ما بكاؤك في دار عهدت بهاعهدا، فأخلف، أم في أيها تقف؟

The construction «عهدت بها عهداً فأخلف» is uncertain. I take it to mean a remembered way of life that has changed; «عهد» can also mean a pledge, with «أخلف» indicating its failure.

On encampments (manāzil), line 6
Eyes weep for them out of grief for others;and if anyone weeps for them, they themselves have known anguish.
تبكي لهم أعين من شجو غيرهموإن بكى لهم باك فقد لهفوا

«من شجو غيرهم» literally appears to mean 'out of grief for others,' though its connection to weeping for these people is unclear. Another possible reading takes «غيرهم» as «غِيَرهم», referring to their changes of fortune.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Stop, you two: let us offer the dwellings tears from eyeswhose depths overflow with longing.
قفا نعط المنازل من جفونلها في الشوق أحشاء غزار

أحشاء غزار, literally 'copious innards,' is an unusual and uncertain description of the eyes. I have understood it as depths overflowing with tears in longing; 'tears' is implicit rather than explicit in the Arabic.

On encampments (manāzil), line 6
Troubles have moved into your courtyard, though for so longthe daughters of Time had kept away from you,
خلفت بعقوتك الشؤون وطالماكانت بنات الدهر عنك خلوفا

I read خلفت as meaning that troubles have succeeded the former occupants, and الشؤون as adverse events. The unvocalized wording leaves the precise reading uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
By my father, these dwellings are sorrows indeed,and they plainly reveal longing.
وأبى المنازل إنها لشجونوعلى الصبابة إنها لتبين

I read «وأبى» as «وأبي», the oath ‘by my father.’ The construction «وعلى الصبابة إنها لتبين» is unclear, particularly the preposition «على»; the translation tentatively takes the dwellings as revealing or expressing longing.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Can a ruined dwelling answerthe questions of one who has no helper?
هل منزل دارس يبينسؤال من ما له معين؟

The construction يبين سؤال is unclear. The translation takes it as answering a question; understanding or making the question clear may instead be intended.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
O dwelling at al-Dayr, now deserted,where north and west winds play!
أيا منزلا بالدير أصبح خالياتلاعب فيه شمال ودبور

Al-Dayr literally means 'the monastery'; it is unclear whether this is a place-name or a reference to a particular monastery. The location is unidentified.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
To God I complain of what I see from my clan,though in days gone by I never asked more of them.
إلى الله أشكو ما أرى من عشيرتيوما كنت فيما قد مضى استزيدها

استزيدها can mean asking more of the clan, with the implication of finding their conduct wanting or reproaching them. The precise sense intended here is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
Though its people have departed,it was indeed once inhabited.
فلئن بان أهلهلبما كان يؤهل

The construction لبما is unclear to me. It is rendered as an emphatic recollection, 'indeed once,' contrasting the dwelling's former habitation with its present abandonment.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
Once I would see the whole tribe living happilythere—but separation severs ties.
بما قد أرى الحي الجميع بغبطةبها، والنوى قطاعة للوسائل

The opening بما is syntactically unclear. The translation takes the line as recalling the tribe's former happiness in these dwellings.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Has the trace of the age-old dwelling made you weep,at Amrāsh, deserted by the dwellers of al-Akhārim?
أأبكاك رسم المنزل المتقادمبأمراش أقوى من حلول الأخارم

Amrāsh and al-Akhārim are unidentified; their vocalization is uncertain. I take حلول as ‘dwellers,’ but whether al-Akhārim names a place or a group is unclear.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
So your eyes, when you recognized it, overflowed therewith streaming tears, rushing like two strings of pearls.
فأمرت به عيناك لما عرفتهابمبتدر نظم الفريدين ساجم

The construction مبتدر نظم الفريدين is uncertain. The translation takes it as an image of tears rushing like strung pearls; مبتدر may more specifically mean ‘outpacing,’ and the precise reference of the dual الفريدين is unclear.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
I am enthralled by a time the dwellings recalled—yet how can one forget good sense when gray hair has spread?
شعفت بعهد ذكرته المنازلوكيف تناسى الحلم والشيب شامل

The syntax of وكيف تناسى الحلم is uncertain. The translation takes الحلم as 'good sense' and تناسى as forgetting or disregarding it; a second-person reading would require understanding تناسى as shortened from تتناسى.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
We send greetings from Milḥ to the people of al-Ghawr;how far from Milḥ, in al-Ghawr, lies our greeting’s destination!
نهدي السلام لأهل الغور من ملحهيهات من ملح بالغور مهدانا

The identification and vocalization of ملح, provisionally transliterated Milḥ, are uncertain. Al-Ghawr means the lowlands; the particular region intended is unclear.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
We send greetings from Milḥ to the people of al-Ghawr;how far from Milḥ, in al-Ghawr, lies our greeting’s destination!
نهدي السلام لأهل الغور من ملحهيهات من ملح بالغور مهدانا

مهدانا is ambiguous here. 'Our greeting’s destination' is a tentative interpretation; it may instead refer to the greeting being sent.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
A dwelling at one of al-Rijlatayn, as thougheffaced for years, though not yet settled anew.
دار بإحدى الرجلتين كأنهاقد عفيت حججا، ولما تحلل

ولما تحلل is unclear in context. The translation tentatively reads تُحلَل, ‘be inhabited,’ taking the phrase to mean that the dwelling has not yet been inhabited anew.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
Nothing remains at your dwelling but motionless hearthstones,soot-darkened, and ash clumped like a huddled chick.
ما إن بمثواك غير راكدةسفع وهاب كالفرخ ملتبد

The word هاب is uncertain. I tentatively understand it as referring to ash, from هبا, used of dust or ash rising or scattering. 'Hearthstones' is inferred from راكدة سفع, literally 'motionless, darkened [things].'

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Whose dwellings are these, effaced over the years,Left desolate after their freshness, and worn away?
لمن المنازل قد عفون سنيناأقفرن بعد تحدد وبلينا

تحدد is unclear here. The translation provisionally assumes تجدد, ‘renewal’ or ‘freshness,’ with a possible dotting error in the source.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
Abodes of the clans of Dhuʾayb ibn Māzin,Ghayẓ, and Kaʿb, before they scattered—
منازل من حيي ذؤيب بن مازنوغيظ وكعب قبل أن يتفرقوا

حيي appears to be the construct dual, 'the two clans,' but three names follow. The grouping or wording is unclear; the translation uses 'clans.'

On encampments (manāzil), line 4
Homes of a people whose spearsare strongholds in battle and take the lead in avenging blood.
ديار من الحي الذين رماحهممعاقل في الهيجا وبالوتر تسبق

The compressed phrase بالوتر تسبق is understood as taking precedence in exacting blood vengeance; its precise construction is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
O Barq Ḥumma, how have you fared amid decay?May the clouds ever attend you, unerring in their course.
يا برق حمة ما فعلت على البلىلا زلت يصحبك الغمام سديدا

برق حمة is taken as a place designation, Barq Ḥumma; برق may refer to rocky ground rather than lightning. The precise sense of سديدا is also uncertain; it is rendered as describing clouds that do not miss their destination.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
I stood at the dwelling, unable to recognize itsave through memory, like the dim recollection of a dream.
وقفت بالدار ما أبينهاإلا إدكارا، توهم الحلم

The compressed phrase توهم الحلم is understood as comparing recognition of the dwelling to the indistinct recollection of a dream; its exact grammatical relation to إدكارا is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
I weep toward [the east], though your dwellings layon the western side—for fear of gossip.
أبكى إلى الشوق أن كانت منازلكمبجانب الغرب خوف القيل والقال

The opening أبكى إلى الشوق is obscure as written. I tentatively read إلى الشرق ('toward the east') instead of إلى الشوق ('toward longing'), giving a contrast with الغرب ('the west') and suggesting that the speaker conceals the direction of the beloved’s dwelling.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
O dwelling, the hands of decay have played with youas doubts play, though once you stood beyond doubt.
يا منزلا لعبت به أيدي البلىلعب الشكوك، وقد بدا بتيقن

The construction «لعب الشكوك، وقد بدا بتيقن» is compressed and somewhat unclear. I take it to contrast the dwelling’s former unmistakable presence with the uncertainty produced by its decay.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
and that you will be stripped of patience and consolationwhen your dwellings lie far from the one you love.
وأنك مسلوب التصبر والأسىإذا بعدت ممن تحب المنازل

الأسى is taken here as al-usā, 'consolations' (plural of uswa). The unvocalized text can also mean 'grief'; the intended sense is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
Why did you not stay, even if on embers of ghaḍā woodyou were tossed—or on the edge of a keen sword?
ألا أقمت ولو على جمر الغضاقلبت، أوحد الحسام الصارم؟

The translation tentatively reads قلبت as قُلِّبْتَ, 'you were tossed/turned about,' and separates أوحد into أو حدّ, 'or the edge of.' The printed spacing and punctuation appear faulty.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
May you never perish; may a downpour drench your grounds,its floodwaters soaking your soil and providing pasture.
لا تبعدن وجاد ربعك وابليروى ثراك أتيه ويسيم

The intended sense and construction of ويسيم are uncertain. It ordinarily means ‘lets graze’; ‘providing pasture’ interprets it here as the rain enabling grazing.

On encampments (manāzil), line 6
If you see men much envied, the days scarcelygive them respite before they become objects of pity.
وإذا رأيت محسدين فقلماترجيهم الأيام حتى يرحموا

The reading ترجيهم is uncertain. I take it as an unhamzated form of ترجئهم, meaning ‘give them respite’ or ‘leave them be’: those now envied are soon reduced to being pitied.

On encampments (manāzil), line 4
She said, “An old man?” I said, “Middle-aged.” She lowered her eyesand said, “Before gray hair comes a bowman’s warning.
وقالت: أشيخ؟ قلت: كهل، فأطرقتوقالت: أمام الشيب إنذار منبض

منبض is tentatively read as مُنْبِض, someone twanging a bowstring, making middle age a warning before gray hair strikes. The exact sense of this compressed image is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
A distant quest, and the shifting turns of separation,whenever a horseman comes from this side of Wajra.
طلاب بعيد، واختلاف من النوىإذا ما أتى من دون وجرة فارس

The syntax of «طلاب بعيد، واختلاف من النوى» and its connection to the following clause are unclear. «طلاب بعيد» could also mean ‘a quest for someone far away.’ The translation preserves the apparent fragmentary construction.

On encampments (manāzil), line 4
The dwellings stand empty of gazelles; yet he hasOf each compliant beauty a phantom that fails him.
تخلو الديار من الظباء؛ وعندهمن كل تابعة خيال خاذل

تابعة literally means 'following' or 'compliant.' I take it to describe a woman formerly responsive to the lover, contrasted with her phantom, which now fails him; the precise sense is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
Hind’s abode! Will the days with Hindreturn, with love and tranquil surroundings?
دار هند، وهل زمان بهندعائد بالهوى وصفو الجناب؟

The sense of ṣafw al-janāb, rendered as “tranquil surroundings,” is uncertain: it may refer more broadly to the untroubled happiness of life near Hind.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
The winds lingered there until it seemedthey were passing its topsoil to one another through sieves.
أربت بها الأرواح حتى كأنماتهادين أعلى تربها بالمناخل

The image in تهادين أعلى تربها بالمناخل is somewhat uncertain: تهادين suggests exchanging gifts, here understood as the winds passing the surface soil among themselves as though through sieves.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
The year she stayed there—its summer and spring—has passed,and another year, and yet another following the last.
أتى عام حلت صيفه وربيعهوعام وعام يتبع العام قابل

The syntax of عام حلت صيفه وربيعه is uncertain: “its summer and spring” may specify the seasons she spent there or the portions of that year that have passed. قابل describes a following or forthcoming year.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
Ah, Mayy, would that we knewwhen we shall meet you on some fleeting visit.
ألا يا ليتنا يا مي ندريمتى نلقاك في عرج اللمام

The expression «في عرج اللمام» is uncertain; it is understood here as referring to brief, occasional visits or stops along the way.

On encampments (manāzil), line 4
Yes—a choking grief, at recognizing a dwellingof Mayya, nearly slew me, had it not set my tears flowing.
أجل عبرة كادت لعرفان منزللمية لو لم تسهل الماء تذبح

The syntax is compressed and somewhat uncertain. I read أجل as ‘yes,’ عبرة as choking grief seeking release in tears, and تسهل الماء as ‘let the tears flow.’

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
Recognizing it brought the old bond back to me,until it almost returned my words in answer.
أدى إلى العهد من عرفانهاحتى لكاد يرد رجع جوابي

The first hemistich is syntactically unclear as printed. The translation provisionally reads إلى as إليّ, ‘to me.’ The referent of the feminine pronoun in عرفانها (‘recognizing her/it’) is also uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
Separation took notice of its inhabitant, andwatchful Time's slumber lifted from its people.
أبهت لساكنها النوى وتكشفتعن أهلها سنة الزمان الناظر

I read أبهت as أَبِهَتْ, 'took notice,' with النوى ('separation') as its subject. The unvocalized wording leaves some uncertainty.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
I looked toward Zaynab’s departing caravan in the morningand lamented over it—if only lamenting could avail.
نظت إلى أظعان زينب بالضحىفأعولتها لو أن إعوالها يغني

أعولتها is rendered as ‘lamented over it,’ taking the pronoun to refer to the departing caravan (أظعان). The verb’s transitive construction here is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
I ask every caravan I meet about her,but I have had no news of her since our stay.
أسأئل عنها كل ركب لقيتهوما لي بها من بعد مكتنا علم

أسأئل appears to be a misspelling of أسائل, ‘I ask.’ مكتنا is unclear; ‘since our stay’ tentatively assumes مكثنا (‘our stay’) was intended.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Dwellings—we found no fault with the days of our sojournin them, nor was their time with us ever faulted.
منازل لم نذمم عهد معرسنافيها، ولا ذم يوما عهدها فينا

The grammar of ولا ذم يوما عهدها فينا is uncertain. I read ذم as passive, dhumma, with عهدها as its subject: ‘nor was their time with us ever faulted.’

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Take your share of my weeping at the dwellings, or leave it;set about reproaching me for them, or desist.
خذا من بكائي في المنازل أودعاوروحا على لومي بهن أو أربعا

خذا من بكائي is uncertain: it may mean “share in my weeping” or “lessen my weeping.” I read أودعا as أو دعا, “or leave it,” addressed to two companions.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
At al-Ghawr is a dwelling of those who have forgotten their bond with me;have mercy on one who stayed there through winter and summer!
وبالغور للناسين عهدي منزلحنانيك من شات أقام وصائف

شاتٍ and صائف mean someone who winters and summers somewhere. The construction حنانيك من and the identity of that person are uncertain; the translation takes this as a plea for mercy on the speaker.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
I feign ignorance of it out of wariness, not lack of knowledge,and ask about it, though its features are plain.
أغالط فيه رقبة لا جهالةوأسأل عنه وهو باد [ي] المعارف

رقبة is taken to mean apprehension or wariness, perhaps of being watched; its precise sense here is uncertain. The printed باد [ي] المعارف is read as بادي المعارف, 'with plainly visible features.'

On encampments (manāzil), line 5
And from clouds of tears its soil brought forthverdure whose scout brought seekers of pasture glad tidings of plenty.
وأنبت من سحب الدموع ترابهحيا بشر النجاع بالخصب رائده

Ḥayā usually denotes life-giving rain, but here appears to mean the vegetation or fertility it produces, since it is what the soil brings forth. The reference of 'its scout' is somewhat uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Is it longing, now that the dwellings have stirred you,where the thickets of Bayshatayn meet?
أللشوق لما هيجتك المنازلبحيث التقت من بيشتين الغياطل

The opening question, «أللشوق», is syntactically elliptical; its precise connection with «تذكرت» in line 2 is uncertain. The translation retains the shift from addressing “you” to speaking of “my eye.”

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
How often they have quenched thirst with tears of bloodshed within them, yet left reprover and reproved athirst.
فلربما أروت دموعا من دمفيها، وأظمت لائما وملوما

The construction أروت دموعا من دم is difficult: literally, it seems to mean 'gave tears of blood to drink,' with the recipient unstated. The translation takes the dwellings as the subject and preserves the contrast between quenching thirst and causing thirst.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
And pour down between them until you soothe themwith a streaming downpour of autumn rain?
وصبت بينهما حتى تسليهمابمستهل من الوسمى منسجم

تسليهما is rendered as ‘soothe them.’ The reading is uncertain; it may be a transposition of تسيلهما, ‘make them flow [with rainwater].’

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
My eye imagined her, and her cheek came to beara mark where my gaze’s imagining had fallen.
توهمها طرفي فأصبح خدهاوفيه مكان الوهم من نظري أثر

توهمها طرفي may mean that the eye barely perceived her rather than literally imagined her. The compressed phrase مكان الوهم من نظري is likewise uncertain; it appears to describe even an imagined glance leaving a mark on her cheek.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
Except for eyes that lament love through their lids,and broken sighs over a blazing fire.
سوى أعين تشكو الهوى بجفونهاوتقطيع أنفاس على النار تضرم

The syntax of على النار تضرم is uncertain. I have taken تضرم as describing the fire blazing; it may instead refer to the sighs being kindled upon the fire.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
Dwellings where Sulaymā once would stay,slender-waisted, her sash hanging loose.
ديار قد تحل بها سليمىهضيم الكشح، جاثلة الوشاح؟

جاثلة الوشاح is obscure as printed. The translation tentatively reads جائلة الوشاح, ‘with a loose-hanging sash,’ a conventional description of a slender waist.

On encampments (manāzil), line 4
In your betrayal of me you stumbled—the stumble of one who has no escape.
عثرت في غدرك بيعثرة من لا وألا

The construction من لا وألا is uncertain; 'one who has no escape' takes وألا as related to وأل, seeking refuge or escaping. The unvocalized عثرت could also mean 'I stumbled' rather than 'you stumbled.'

On dwellings (diyār), line 7
May the man who relayed the news for a morsel [unclear],or live blind from failing sight, unable to hear.
صار الذي أثر الحديث بطعمةأو عاش أعمى من عشا لا يسمع

صار الذي أثر الحديث بطعمة does not yield a clear construction. أثر الحديث can mean “relayed the report,” and بطعمة could mean “for a morsel,” but their connection with صار is unresolved. The translation tentatively treats the line as a curse, suggested by “or live blind … unable to hear”; the missing sense has not been supplied.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
She is the very likeness of Umm Ḥakīm when we were lovers,and the bond with her was strong, unbroken.
أشباه أم حكيم إذ تواصلناوالحبل منها متين غير منجذم

أشباه literally means 'likenesses'; its plural form and grammatical connection are unclear here. I have understood it as comparing the woman to Umm Ḥakīm, whom I cannot identify from the supplied context.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Ḥarām has departed from the land; never again will you seethe faces of Ḥarām there, to the end of time.
رحلت حرام عن البلاد فلن ترىأخرى المنون بها وجوه حرام

Ḥarām appears to be the name of a tribe or clan, whose identity is uncertain. The unusual expression أخرى المنون is tentatively understood as a temporal phrase, 'to the end of time.'

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
For loyalty belongs to al-Shām; elsewhere there isloyalty in speech, treachery in intent.
فللشام الوفاء، وإن سواهتوافي منطقا غدر اعتقادا

توافي is grammatically unclear as printed. I have provisionally taken it as a noun expressing mutual fidelity, contrasted with غدر, ‘treachery.’

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
