What harm would it have done those abodes, when they settled in their precincts,if no dwelling of ʿAlwa were seen there?
ما ضرها إذ ينزلون ربوعهاألا يرى "فيها لعلوة منزل

The wording is obscure: the subject of ينزلون (‘they settle’) is not identified, and the rhetorical question is difficult to interpret in context. The translation takes ألا as أن لا (‘that … not’). The stray quotation mark before فيها appears accidental.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
A tribe’s abode—long has the time elapsedsince it was peopled; it fell to ruin, and they perished.
دار حي تقادم العهد منهابعد حضارها، فبارت وباروا

The reading of حضارها is uncertain. I have taken the phrase to mean 'since it was peopled'; حُضّارها could instead mean 'its inhabitants,' giving the sense 'after its inhabitants were gone.'

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
If you will not endure what was bound to come,then, if you have a protest to make, protest.
فإن أنت لم تصبر لما كان جائيافإن كان تنكير لديك فأنكر

تنكير is unusual here. It is rendered as 'protest,' in the sense of rejection or repudiation, but its precise force is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
We wear away, but the rising stars do not;the dwellings and edifices remain after us.
بلينا وما تبلى النجوم الطوالعوتبقى الديار بعدنا والمصانع

«المصانع», translated as “edifices,” can also denote waterworks or cisterns; the precise structures intended are uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
The winds wove over their surface, untilthe bare ground showed through all the traces.
نسجت ظهرها الرياحات حتىيرى القاع من جميع الرسوم

The relation expressed by من in يرى القاع من جميع الرسوم is unclear. The sense may instead be that only bare ground remains where all the traces once were.

On dwellings (diyār), line 9
A neighbor used to live at ease among them,neither threatened nor wronged.
ولقد كان يخفض الجار فيهمغير مستشرف ولا مظلوم

The precise sense of مستشرف is uncertain. 'Threatened' takes it to mean exposed to hostile or covetous attention.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
The prime of youth is youthful passion’s brother and companion;gray hair means desire’s dismissal and departure.
شرخ الشباب أخو الصبي وأليفهوالشيب تزجية الهوى وخفوفه

تزجية الهوى is uncertain. I take it as driving desire away, paired with خفوفه, ‘its departure’; تزجية can also suggest eking something out.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
How often I have stood there, questioning someone who might knowabout its people—or a departing traveler, or a sympathetic soul.
كم قد وقفت بها أسائل مخبراعن أهلها أو صادرا أو مشفقا

Ṣādiran (صادراً), rendered as “a departing traveler,” denotes someone departing or returning, often from a watering place. Its specific reference here is unclear.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Do you recognize the traces of dwellings at al-Sitārayn?A bitter, doubly fierce north wind has effaced them.
أرسم ديار بالستارين تعرفعفتها شمال ذات نيرين حرجف

ذات نيرين, rendered 'doubly fierce,' is obscure here. It apparently likens the wind's strength to doubled threads or a double-woven fabric, but the precise force of the expression is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 6
When people were truly people, and the land was in its bloom,and you were there, loving your companion, bound in affection.
إذ الناس ناس، والبلاد بغرةوأنت بها صب القرينة مؤلف

صب القرينة مؤلف is compressed and somewhat uncertain. القرينة is taken as a female companion or wife, and مؤلف as describing a bond of affection.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
Can reunion draw near after separation?Can the ease of our former life return?
فهل شعب يداني بعد شعبوهل لليان عيشتنا انكرار

شعب can denote either gathering or separation. I take its two occurrences as a contrast, ‘reunion after separation,’ but the unvocalized wording also permits a reference to groups of people, and the precise sense is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Who has dwelt in these abodes—even with ample raiment about him—and endured?
من على هذه الديار أقامالو ضفا ملبس عليه فداما

The syntax of لو ضفا ملبس عليه فداما is uncertain. I take لو concessively ('even if') and 'endured' as referring to the inhabitant, though it could refer to the garment. The 'ample raiment' may figuratively signify prosperity.

On dwellings (diyār), line 5
A captive in the hand of wishes: whenever heattained a desire he pursued, he aimed at another goal.
علقا في يد المنى كلما نال هوى يبتغيه رام مراما

The precise sense of علقا is uncertain. I understand it as something caught or held fast, hence 'a captive' in the hand of wishes.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Standing among the dwellings is no act of pious restraint;so let your tear ducts overflow: these are the old encampments.
ما في وقوفك في الديار تورعفأفض شؤون العين فهي الأربع

The intended sense of تورع ('pious scrupulousness' or 'restraint') in this context is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
How dear to me the long winter night I spend awake,thinking of you while tears stream down.
أحبب إلي بليل التم أسهرهتفكرا فيكم، والدمع ينهمل

ليل التم is understood here as the long night of midwinter, though the precise form and intended sense are uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
If your dwellings stand empty of you, and they have lostthe radiance of majesty, and their canopies have fallen,
دياركم إن خلت منكم وفارقهانور المهابة وانحطت بها الكلل

الكلل is taken as the plural of كلة, a curtain or canopy. It is unclear whether انحطت describes these being lowered or falling into disrepair.

On dwellings (diyār), line 6
May God grant no joy to anyone whose eyes found joy in parting.
لا أقر الله من قرت له بالبين عينا

The grammatical form of the final عينا is unclear as written. The translation follows the apparent sense of the idiom قرت العين, meaning that the eye is gladdened or content.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
They have fallen into ruin, keeping faith with them, and grown forlornafter their departure; the landmarks have been effaced.
درست محافظة لهم، وتوحشتمن بعدهم، وتعفت الأعلام

The unusual phrase محافظة لهم is rendered as 'keeping faith with them'; its precise force here is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Dwellings that drank deep of oppression as it was dealt out;death summoned the folk within them and made itself heard.
ديار كرعن الضيم وهو مصرفونادى بهن الموت أهلا فأسمعا

مصرف is uncertain here; provisionally read as مُصَرَّف, ‘dealt out’ or ‘dispensed.’

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
Who will take my side against wayward Time,which has defied my efforts to set it straight?
من عذيري من الزمان أخي عوجاء أعيا علي أن يستقيما

أخي عوجاء is elliptical: literally, 'brother of a crooked [thing or course].' I take it to characterize Time as wayward, though the implied noun is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
And that the turtle-dove should coo within them when there appearsto riders there a gray rim of the sun;
وأن يسجع القمري فيها إذا بدالركبانها قرن من الشمس أورق

أورق usually means gray or ash-colored; its precise force here as a description of the sun’s rim is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Salute the dwellings of the days when life was truly life,when al-Simāk was our emissary and was granted aid.
حي الديار إذ الزمان زمانوإذ السماك جري لنا ومعان

The phrase «السماك جري لنا ومعان» is uncertain. I provisionally read جري as جَرِيّ, ‘emissary’ or ‘agent,’ and معان as مُعان, ‘aided.’ al-Simāk is a star name, but the precise celestial allusion and the sense of ‘aided’ here are unclear; the text may be faulty.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Do you recognize traces like the coursing of streams,ʿAmra’s, desolate save where a rider stops?
أتعرف رسما كاطراد المذاهبلعمرة وحشا غير موقف راكب

المذاهب is tentatively understood as streams or watercourses; the precise sense of the comparison is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Tell me: if there linger over Najd’s peopleand its upper lava plain the rumbling rainclouds,
أريتك إن نجدا ألظ بأهلهوحرته العليا الغيوث الرواجس

I read إن as conditional ('if'), with the question in line 3 completing the sense. The construction إن نجداً ألظ بأهله ... الغيوث is syntactically awkward as transmitted, so this reading is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
You ask it about the old days, though it is as you knew it;those who dwelt there have gathered together, but it has not moved.
تسأله العهد وهو عهدك واستجمع من حله، ولم يرم

The wording is difficult. وهو عهدك is taken as 'it is as you knew it.' واستجمع من حله literally appears to say that those who inhabited it gathered together; whether this implies their departure is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 8
Ever since Ḥabība left me this legacy—and evil comes upon the hilltops.
من عهد ما أورثت حبيبةوالشر يوافي مطالع الأكم

The syntax of من عهد ما أورثت حبيبة and its connection to the preceding line are unclear. The translation provisionally understands a legacy of love or sickness left by Ḥabība. حبيبة could instead mean 'a beloved woman'; the person's identity and any particular allusion in the second hemistich are uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
The absence of its people has not changed the dwelling;nor is the dwelling deaf—if only it could speak to one in need.
لا الدار غيرها بعد الأنيس ولابالدار لو كلمت ذا حاجة صمم

The syntax and sense are uncertain. The translation takes لا as negation and بعد الأنيس as بُعد الأنيس, 'the absence of its people.' Initial لا could instead be corrective: 'No—it is the absence of its people that changed the dwelling.' The force of لو كلمت ذا حاجة is also unclear.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
We stopped at the dwellings; among the riderswas one despoiled by passion, and another rich.
قد وقفنا على الديار وفي الركب حريب من الغرام ومثري

Ḥarīb means someone despoiled of possessions, contrasted here with muthrī, 'wealthy.' It is uncertain whether the latter means enriched by love or spared its ravages.

On dwellings (diyār), line 7
Yet once the kin would all be gathered there, and Iwould delight in Ṣafrāʾ, radiant to behold.
فقد يكون بها الأهل الجميع وقدألهو بصفراء ذات المنظر الواري

The precise sense of al-wārī, rendered as 'radiant' in the description of her appearance, is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
Though Salmā has gone far from you today,every bond of companionship is destined to break.
فإن تك قد نأتك اليوم سلمىفكل قوى قرين لانقطاع

The compressed phrase قوى قرين is uncertain. I understand قوى as rope-strands, used figuratively for the bonds joining companions.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
and three enduring hearthstones like doves,and weathered ash, cold and caked.
وغير ثلاث كالحمام خوالدوهاب محيل هامد متلبد

هاب is understood as هابٍ, referring to fine ash or dust. ‘Ash’ fits the hearthstones, but the word’s precise sense here is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 6
The talebearers tapped the staff for you concerning herlong ago, as it used to be tapped for the man of discernment.
وقد قرع الواشون فيها لك العصاقديما، كما كانت لذي الحلم تقرع

Tapping the staff alludes to a proverbial warning or reminder given to a discerning man. The proverb is commonly associated with the judge ʿĀmir ibn al-Ẓarib, but whether he is specifically intended here is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
Would that I knew! Every abode scatters us;is there no dwelling that draws our company close and reunites it?
ألا ليت شعري كل دار مشتةألا منزل يدنو بشمل فيجمع؟

I take مشتة to describe an abode that disperses its people, though the unvocalized form leaves some uncertainty about its precise sense.

On dwellings (diyār), line 9
They said, “After Salmā’s ransom, you will beneither rich through what you possess nor poor.”
وقالوا: لست بعد فداء سلمىبمغن ما لديك ولا فقير

بمغن ما لديك is grammatically awkward. The translation tentatively understands it as ‘rich through what you possess’; the exact construction and sense remain uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
The dwellings of her whose coquetry ensnared my heart,and who tempted it on the day of separation, as we departed.
ديار التي صاد الفؤاد دلالهاوأغرت به يوم النوى حين نرحل

«وأغرت به» is ambiguous without vowels, and its implied object or referent is unclear. 'Who tempted it' provisionally takes the woman as the subject and the heart as the referent.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
Their landmarks have vanished; what remains of their tracesis worn, like the heading of a faded letter.
درست معالمها فباقي رسمهاخلق كعنوان الكتاب المحول

المحول, rendered as “faded,” is uncertain: it may describe writing that has been altered or effaced, or a document that has aged a year.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
So I said to my companion, “Turn aside a little;let us remind our longing of the worn, deserted ruins.”
فقلت لصاحبي: عرج قليلانذكر شوقنا الدرس القفارا

I read نذكر as nudhakkir, “remind.” The relationship between its objects is uncertain: the phrase could instead mean “let us remind the worn, deserted ruins of our longing.”

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Is there among the dwellings, despite my reproach and my excuses,a plea for redress against my longing and remembrance?
هل بالديار على لومي ومعذرتيعدوى تقام على وجدي وتذكاري

The construction is uncertain. I take عدوى in its sense of a plea for assistance or redress, rather than contagion. على لومي ومعذرتي is also ambiguous: لومي may mean either reproach I utter or reproach directed at me, while معذرتي may mean my excuse or the justification offered for me.

On haunts (maghānī), line 3
The ruins of a campsite are no replacement for you;they have grown unrecognizable, taking the sand-bearing winds in your place.
وما خلف منكم بأطلال دمنةتنكرن فاستبدلن منك السوافيا

The first hemistich is syntactically uncertain. I read خلف as khalaf, ‘a replacement,’ rather than as a verb. السوافي can denote sand-bearing winds or the sand and dust they carry.

On haunts (maghānī), line 3
For once I would see those dwellings and their people,with their inhabitants gathered together, flourishing.
بما قد أرى تلك الديار وأهلهاوهن جميعات الأنيس عوامر

The opening بما قد أرى is syntactically uncertain. I take it as recalling the dwellings’ former condition and explaining why they awaken longing.

On haunts (maghānī), line 3
A time of pleasure whose haunts were never found wantingfor a single day, that it should be forgotten; its beginnings have not grown old.
عهد من اللهو لم تذمم معاهدهيوما فينسى ولم تقدم بواديه

بواديه is taken as “its beginnings” or “its earliest manifestations,” and لم تقدم as “have not grown old.” The wording is unusual, and this reading is uncertain.

On haunts (maghānī), line 3
By my life, you have worn out the freshness of weeping,as you wore me out, and made my faded longing new again.
لعمري لقد أبليتم جدة البكابلاى، وجددتم على بلى الوجد

The form «بلاى» is uncertain. I take it as «بِلايَ», ‘my wearing away,’ with an implied comparison: ‘as you wore me out.’ I read «على» here as «عليّ», ‘upon me.’

On haunts (maghānī), line 2
Then my tears overflowed with longing,and among them was a young beauty, like an oryx, demure.
ففاضت دموعي عند ذاك صبابةوفيهن خود كالمهاة غضيض

The referent of فيهن (“among them”) is uncertain; it may mean “in those dwelling places.” غضيض, rendered “demure,” may suggest downcast eyes or softness and delicacy.

On haunts (maghānī), line 1
O dwellings of al-Ḥimā, may you be watered! Yet whatgood does it do me if rain lavishes its drops on you?
يا مغاني الحمى سقيت، وما ينفعني الغيث أن يجودك قطرا

Al-Ḥimā can mean a protected pasture or reserved grazing ground; it is unclear whether a particular named locality is intended here.

On haunts (maghānī), line 2
What evil eye struck the dwelling after I left? May Godfill its lids with grit and do it harm!
أي عين أصابت الدار أقذى الله بعدي أجفانها وأضرا

The placement of بعدي ('after I left') makes its attachment uncertain. It is taken here with the eye’s striking the dwelling, rather than with the ensuing curse.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
What is there to greet in courtyards that have exchanged usfor the sundering paths of separation, and now lie desolate?
وماذا نحيي من عراص تبدلتشعوب النوى عنا فهن قواء

شعوب النوى is uncertain. The translation takes شعوب as branching or sundering paths, figuratively belonging to separation; شعوب can also denote death, which would suggest a personification of separation as death.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 3
Parting behaved rashly toward you on the day they left,though often I have found it forbearing toward you.
سفه الفراق عليك يوم رحيلهموبما أراه عنك وهو حليم

The construction «وبما أراه عنك» is uncertain. I take «بما» in the sense of «ربما», ‘often,’ and understand «عنك» as completing «حليم», ‘forbearing toward you.’

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
What greeting can a dwelling offer once it has been effaced,but familiar traces that stir my distracted grief?
وما تحية دار بعد ما درستإلا معارف رسم هاج من خبلي

The construction «إلا معارف رسم هاج من خبلي» is compressed and uncertain. I take the recognizable traces as the dwelling’s answering greeting; «خبلي» can mean my madness, mental disturbance, or distraction.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Turn aside, you two, to the timeworn ruins, that we mayweep for the dwellings as Ibn Khidhām wept.
عوجا على الطلل المحيل لعلنانبكي الديار كما بكى ابن خذام

The identity of Ibn Khidhām, invoked as a predecessor in weeping over abandoned dwellings, is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
Time has worn away the freshness of their site,and they seem a threadbare cloth,
درس الجديد جديد معهدهاوكأنما هي ريطة جرد

الجديد is understood here as time renewing itself, which wears away the site's former freshness; the precise sense of the singular expression is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 5
A wind from al-Shām meets one from al-Yaman;the two weave with the ruins’ swirling dust.
تلقى شآمية يمانيةلهما بمور ترابها سرد

شآمية and يمانية are understood as winds from al-Shām and al-Yaman. سرد appears to describe their weaving or interlacing the moving dust, but its exact sense here is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 6
My heart is left to sorrows after separation,and you to drifting sand and fine, sifting rain.
قلبي للأحزان بعد النوىوأنت للسافي وللناخل

I take al-sāfī as wind-driven sand and al-nākhil as fine, sifting rain. The latter is uncertain here; it may instead describe a wind that sifts or scatters dust.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 4
As though its days had not been lived in utmost happiness,with our two clans gathered together in harmony.
ولم تغن في أيامه أحسن الغنىوشعبا جميع الشمل متفقان

The subject of تغن ('you/she dwelt or lived') is unclear; the translation leaves it implicit. The compressed phrase وشعبا جميع الشمل متفقان is taken provisionally to describe two clans gathered in unity.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 3
That evening Masʿūd said—as there streamed
عشية مسعود يقولوقد جرى

Lines 3–4 appear to constitute a single bayt divided incorrectly in the supplied text; their supplied divisions have been retained. Masʿūd’s identity is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 7
O Mayy, is my weeping answered with the likeby you, while my breaths are sighs for you?
فيامي هل يجزي بكائي بمثلهإليك، وأنفاسي عليك زوافر

The construction يجزي بكائي بمثله إليك is awkward. The translation tentatively understands a question about whether Mayy reciprocates the speaker’s tears; إليك literally means ‘toward you,’ rather than ‘by you.’

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
May God water Baljāʾ’s ruined dwellings at al-Ghaḍā,which decay and distance have clothed in matted layer upon layer.
سفى الله أطلالا لبلجاء بالغضاكساها البلى والنأي لبدا على لبد

لبدا على لبد literally suggests felt or matted coverings piled one upon another; the precise material or image intended is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
On its sandy flat is a place where the tribe made merry at night,and a tethering-place for horses, like an anthill.
بجرعائها من سامر الحي ملعبوآرى أفراس كجرثومة النمل

I read آرى as آريّ, a tethering-place or stall for horses; the intended spelling and form are uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 3
As though the tribe had never dwelt there—though once you werethere, your yearnings stilled, your loved ones gathered together.
كأن لم يكنها الحي إذ أنت مرةبها ميت الأهواء مجتمع الشمل

ميت الأهواء literally means 'dead in desires/passions.' I have interpreted this unusual expression as yearnings stilled through fulfillment, but its precise force is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 4
was not the first time a deserted site stirred your yearningamong sandy flats where people often halted and stayed.
بأول ما هاجت لك الشوق دمنةبأجراع محلال مرب محلل

The closely grouped epithets محلال مرب محلل appear to describe a frequently occupied stopping place; their precise individual senses are uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 5
It has faded, save for a tethering stake and the posts of a prayer enclosure,and blackened stones, kneeling mounts that bore a cooking pot.
عفت غير آري وأعضاد مسجدوسفع مناخات رواحل مرجل

I take سفع مناخات رواحل مرجل as blackened hearthstones likened to kneeling riding beasts supporting a cooking pot. The compressed construction is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
Successive rains have effaced its traces,and it has changed from what you used to know.
درست عهاد الغيث منه فحال عما كنت تعهد

The syntax of درست عهاد الغيث منه is compressed and somewhat uncertain. I take the successive rains as the agent effacing the dwelling’s traces. The word منه is split across the two hemistichs.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 6
The dwelling stirred in you what you will never forgetof your longings—unless you forget despite remembrance.
فهاجت عليك الدار ما لست ناسيامن الحاج إلا أن تنسى على ذكر

The qualification إلا أن تنسى على ذكر is obscure. Translated literally as “unless you forget despite remembrance,” it may refer to forgetting despite reminders or to deliberately suppressing recollection.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
They have weathered away; you would think their traces,after two years have passed, a faded parchment.
بلين وتحسب آياتهمعن فرط حولين رقا محيلا

عن فرط حولين is understood as ‘after two years have passed’; the exact force of فرط here is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Between al-Akhshabayn lie the traces of ʿAmra’s dwellings;some have weathered a month, others a year.
لعمرة بين الأخشبين طلولتقادم منها مشهر ومحيل

I take mushhir (مشهر) and muḥīl (محيل) to describe traces over which a month and a year, respectively, have passed; the exact temporal sense is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Between al-Akhshabayn lie the traces of ʿAmra’s dwellings;some have weathered a month, others a year.
لعمرة بين الأخشبين طلولتقادم منها مشهر ومحيل

Al-Akhshabayn means “the two rugged mountains”; whether the familiar pair near Mecca is intended here is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 3
Her dwelling said nothing to us, except that itbrought back passing thoughts born of recurring madness.
فما كلمتنا دارها غير أنهاثنت هاجسات من خبال مراجع

The phrase ثنت هاجسات من خبال مراجع is obscure. I take ثنت as “brought back,” هاجسات as passing inward thoughts, and مراجع as “recurring,” qualifying خبال, “madness” or mental confusion.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 5
A bond with her—may that bond be blessed!—she breaks a promise or keeps one.
عهدا لها سقيا له من عهدتخلف وعدا أو تفى بوعد

The construction عهدا لها is unclear. عهد may mean a bond or pledge, as translated, or a former time of acquaintance with her.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 10
I bore in a patch of my own skin,expecting from him the likes of a recurring fever,
حملته في رقعة من جلديأرقب منه مثل حمى الورد

حمى الورد appears to designate a recurrent fever; the precise periodicity intended is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 12
May you be safe and long-lived, Abū al-Mukhallad,key to compassion’s bolted door,
واسلم وحييت أبا الملدمفتاح باب الحدب المنسد

The source reads أبا الملد, an unclear name or epithet. The translation tentatively restores أبا المخلد, Abū al-Mukhallad, with a possibly omitted خ; this restoration is uncertain.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
O once-fresh abode of theirs, I see you worn away,and your guests’ fare is anguish and lingering pain.
أقشيب ربعهم أراك دريساوقرى ضيوفك لوعة ورسيسا

رسيس can mean a lingering trace or an abiding feeling, especially of love or pain. Its precise sense here is uncertain; it is rendered as “lingering pain.”

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 3
while I have no means to ward harm off from you;for here I am not addressing Suʿād.
ولا أدرأ الضراء عنك بحيلةفما أنا فيها قائل لسعاد

The reference to Suʿād is uncertain, possibly contrasting this lament with conventional love poetry. The second hemistich could also be read as a question: 'What, then, am I to say to Suʿād about it?'

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 2
What sense has a man faced with his fate,who seeks refuge in grief when a dwelling saddens him?
أي لب لامرئ في قدرهعائذ بالحزن إذ تشجيه دار

في قدره is ambiguous. I have provisionally understood قدر as 'fate'; it could instead concern the man's standing or worth. Its grammatical connection to the rest of the line is uncertain.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 3
He weeps only for those who dwelt there,then withdrew far from him, once their abode lay distant.
إنما يبكي الألى كانوا بهافانتأوه بعد ما شط المزار

فانتأوه is an unusual form with an attached object pronoun. I have provisionally understood it as 'withdrew far from him,' referring to the grieving man, but the construction and the pronoun's referent are uncertain.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 4
Time destroys and builds tirelessly,and Time's destruction of a dwelling is its rebuilding.
يخرب الدهر ويبني جاهداوخراب الدهر للدار عمار

The second hemistich literally identifies Time's destruction of a dwelling with its flourishing or rebuilding. The intended sense of this apparent reversal is unclear; the translation preserves it.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
O dwelling grounds, faced with whatI see of you, I have no strength to endure.
يا ربوع الديار إني على ماقد أراه منكن غير جلدي

The transmitted غير جلدي is unclear and likely contains a transposition for غير جليد, meaning 'not steadfast' or 'unable to endure.' The translation follows that reading.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 2
are meadows that never clothe themselves, when the breeze is gentle,in dust, nor turn muddy beneath torrential rain.
ربائع لا يلبسن والريح ريدةقتاما ولا يلثقن للوابل الهمر

ربائع is taken as a plural meaning meadows or spring pastures; its precise sense here is uncertain.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
I love the soil of the valley whose people have departed,and yearn for the campsite whose traces have worn away.
أحب ثرى الوادي الذي بان أهلهوأصبوا إلى الربع الذي مح مغناه

The unvocalized مح is uncertain; I have understood it as indicating that the campsite has become worn or effaced.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 3
At first my eye failed to recognize it; then it was made plainby black stones standing upright that this was the dwelling.
نبت نبوة عيني بها ثم بينتيحاميم سود أنها الدار مثل

يحاميم سود is understood as black stones, probably blackened hearthstones marking the abandoned dwelling. The precise objects intended are uncertain; مثل is read as مُثَّل, ‘standing upright.’

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 2
Weep there on my behalf, you two, if I am betrayedby my eyelid, and its cloud sheds no rain upon me.
واستعبرا عني به إن خاننيجفني، ولم يمطر على غمامه

The phrase على غمامه is unclear as printed. The translation reads على as عليّ, ‘upon me,’ with غمامه (‘its cloud’) referring to the eyelid’s tears.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 3
If you knew who called to you, you would answer him,and then weep blood over him from burning grief.
لو كنت تدري من دعاك أجبتهوبكيت من حرق عليه إذا دما

I take إذا دما as إذًا دمًا, 'then [weep] blood'; the unvocalized wording permits uncertainty.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 2
after they had grown unrecognizable, their traces alteredby rain and a wind with trailing skirts?
من بعد ما نكرت وغير آيهاقطر ومسبلة الذيول خريع؟

خريع is understood here as an epithet of the wind, but its precise descriptive sense is uncertain and is not separately rendered.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 3
Your tears flowed swiftly in the company’s wake, ever sincethe branches and dunes departed from the dunes.
خفت دموعك في إثر الخليط لدنخفت من الكثب القضبان والكثب

The 'branches and dunes' apparently represent the departing women, suggesting slender figures and rounded hips. Both occurrences of الكثب are read as al-kuthub, 'dunes'; the unvocalized text leaves some uncertainty.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 3
He is lost in memories of lovely women; his concernis to pursue youthful passion in his wavering folly.
يهيم بذكر الغانيات، وهمهطلاب الصبى في غيه المتمايل

The expression في غيه المتمايل, rendered closely as “in his wavering folly,” is unusual; the precise force of المتمايل is uncertain.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 2
I recognized it when I stood within its bounds,its remnants like a foreigner’s drawings.
تعرفته لما وقفت بربعهكأن بقاياه تماثيل أعجما

تماثيل أعجما is interpreted as ‘a foreigner’s drawings.’ أعجم can also mean someone unable to speak intelligibly, so the precise force of the comparison is uncertain.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 4
Ah, I see no disease like love for bringing to ruina noble man, nor any like love whose sufferer is blamed.
ألا لا أرى مثل الهوى داء مسلمكريم، ولا مثل الهوى ليم صاحبه

I take مسلم as musْlim, meaning ‘giving over to ruin,’ with كريم as its object, and ليم as līma, ‘was blamed.’ The unvocalized wording leaves some uncertainty about the construction.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
Tears flowed, paying at the campsite the debt owedto its people, but eased no anguish—how could they?
دمع جرى فقضى في الربع ما وجبالأهله وشفى أنى ولا كربا

The syntax of «وشفى أنى ولا كربا» is abrupt and uncertain. I take «أنى» as an incredulous question ('how could they?'), interrupting and retracting the claim that the tears brought relief.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
I owe the dwelling of al-ʿĀmiriyya a pause;longing dictates to me, and tears are the scribe.
علي لربع العامرية وقفةيمل علي الشوق والدمع كاتب

Al-ʿĀmiriyya apparently designates a woman of the tribe of ʿĀmir; her identity is uncertain.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 2
No, by the father of lovers, I am no loverif the haunts of play do not toy with my patience.
فلا وأبي العشاق ما أنا عاشقإذا أنا لم تلعب بصبري الملاعب

It is unclear whether the oath 'by the father of lovers' refers to a particular figure.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 5
I dwelt beside her through Rajab, in the days at Dhū Salam;then she went away, and Rajab stood between us.
جاورتها رجبا أيام ذي سلمثم استمرت ولاقى دونها رجب

The second occurrence of رجب and the construction لاقى دونها are unclear. The translation provisionally treats Rajab as something intervening between the speaker and the woman; I cannot establish whether it denotes the month again, a person, or a place.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
I seek the wind’s aid against Sulaymā,as it passes over her desolate dwelling.
استنجد الريح من سليمىمرا على ربعها المحيل

I read استنجد as أستنجد, “I seek aid.” The syntax of مرا is uncertain; the translation takes it as describing the wind’s passage, though it could describe the speaker’s passage or be a dual imperative, “pass, you two.”

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 2
Before this, I had not thought my curelay in the languid breath of the east wind.
ولم أخل قبلها شفائيعند نسيم الصبا العليل

The pronoun in قبلها, rendered “before this,” has an uncertain antecedent: it may refer to Sulaymā or to the wind and the experience described in line 1.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 3
Ask their east wind, if it blows,about the gleaming gazelle.
وسل صباها إن سرتعن الغزال الألمع

The precise sense of الألمع, translated as “gleaming,” is uncertain; applied to a gazelle, it may refer to contrasting patches in its coat.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 3
It left only a few of their recognizable traces,speechless when questioned.
فأبقى من معارفها قليلاعيبا حين يسأل بالسؤال

The printed عيبا does not yield a clear sense here. The translation tentatively reads عييا, meaning unable to speak or answer, describing the surviving traces.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 2
Whenever a new dwelling is taken, one grows attached to itthrough familiarity, until it seems one's homeland.
إذا استجدت دارا تعلقهابالإلف حتى كأنها وطنه

The subjects and pronouns are unclear. Unvocalized استجدت permits several readings, including 'I/you took a new dwelling,' whereas تعلقها and وطنه appear to refer to an unidentified third-person subject ('he grows attached to it'; 'his homeland'). The impersonal translation is provisional; the text may be faulty.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 5
I once beheld you; shall I behold you in your early splendor,with life still fresh and time a youth?
ولقد أراك فهل أراك بغرةوالعيش غض والزمان غلام

The sense of بغرة is uncertain: it may refer to early splendor or freshness, as translated, or to an unguarded moment.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 3
I stopped there at midday, asking the dwellingabout Nuʿm’s folk, on a trusty she-camel hardened by journeys.
وقفت فيها سراة اليوم أسألهاعن آل نعم أمونا عبر أسفار

«أمونًا عبر أسفار» appears to describe a dependable she-camel, strong or seasoned in travel. The exact construction and the sense of «عبر أسفار» are uncertain; «أمونًا» may be the delayed object of «وقفت», meaning that the speaker halted his camel.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 2
Yes—tears that kept flowing: whenever I checked themwith my self-command, fresh surges refused restraint and rushed forth.
أجل عبرة ظلت إذا ما وزعتهابحلمي أبت منها عوارض تسرع

I take عوارض to mean recurrent or sudden surges of tears; the compressed phrasing أبت منها عوارض تسرع leaves the precise construction uncertain.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 3
Longing does not bring back the time that has passed,nor is a dwelling’s ruin a place for a man to despair.
وما يرجع الوجد الزمان الذي مضىوما للفتى في دمنة الدار مجزع

I take مجزع as a place or occasion for despair; its precise force here is uncertain.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 3
A raging wind lingered there, drawing the east wind after it,scattering, blowing dust about, and gathering it in heaps.
أربت به هوجاء تستدرج الصبامفرقة تذرى التراب جموع

تستدرج الصبا is rendered 'drawing the east wind after it,' but the precise image of the two winds interacting is uncertain.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 2
by the rainclouds of al-Thurayyā at the close of every night,drenching them generously, bringing downpour after downpour.
نجاء الثريا كل آخر ليلةتجودهما جودا وتردفهما وبلا

نجاء الثريا is understood as rainclouds associated with al-Thurayyā (the Pleiades), though the precise sense of نجاء here is uncertain.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 2
Down over the breast and tunic, until it is drenchedWith streaming tears, though you have not crossed over toward the dwelling.
على النحر والسربال حتى تبلهسجوم، ولم تجزع إلى الدار مجزعا

The construction ولم تجزع إلى الدار مجزعا is uncertain. I have taken تجزع in the sense of crossing or making one’s way, with an implied 'you'; a sense connected with grief is also possible.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 1
May Ṣafrāʾ’s deserted campsite, where she used to dwell, be wateredby the Pleiades’ rain-clouds, their drizzle and gentle showers.
سقى دمنة صفراء كانت تحلهانجاء الثريا طلها وذهابها

نجاء is understood as rain-clouds and ذهابها as gentle showers; the precise meteorological senses are uncertain.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 3
And ever a lover is led to the campsite,captive to longings, worn out by cares.
وما زال مدلولا على الربع عاشقأسير لبانات، طليح هموم

مدلولاً على الربع is taken as 'led to the campsite'; the precise force of this unusual expression is uncertain.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 2
As though we were among the love-stricken of the pure-blooded Arabs,who love to linger by the traces of abandoned camps.
كأننا من متيمي العرب العرباء تهوى المعاج بالدمن

The subject of تهوى (‘loves’) is uncertain. The translation takes it as referring collectively to العرب (‘the Arabs’). If ‘we’ is intended, نهوى (‘we love’) would be expected. المعاج is understood as stopping or lingering.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 5
eager at heart for what fosters renunciation,content in my rough way of life,
راغب نفس فيما يزهدنيناعم بال بعيشي الخشن

The precise sense of فيما يزهدني is uncertain. Literally it suggests “in what makes me renounce,” without specifying what is renounced; the translation takes it as referring to an austere, independent life.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 10
Nor have my faithful friends shunned me, norhave I drunk the milk of affection mixed with rancor.
ولا جفاني أهل الصفاء ولاشربت در الصفاء بالضفن

بالضفن is unclear in this context. The translation conjecturally reads بالضغن, “with rancor,” giving affection’s milk mixed with resentment.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 12
As though we were among the love-stricken Arabs—Arabs of pure stock, longing to stop at abandoned camps.
كأننا من متيمي العرب العرباء تهوى المعاج بالدمن

The grammatical attachment of تهوى, “loves/desires,” is uncertain; it may refer collectively to العرب. المعاج is understood as turning aside or stopping at the abandoned camps.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 20
I have died, though my soul remains within me;I have been brought low, though the guardians guard me.
مت ونفسي على باقيةوضعت والحافظات تحفظني

ونفسي على باقية is problematic; على may represent عليّ, but the construction remains uncertain. The translation gives the probable contrast between being dead and still having one’s soul. وضعت is read as “I was brought low.” The identity of الحافظات, “the guardians,” is unclear.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 3
And when she herself was skilledin dalliance, yet kept herself from passion.
وإذ هي أما نفسها فأريبةللهو، وأما عن صبي فتذودها

The reading صبي is unclear. ‘Passion’ provisionally takes it as a form of ṣibā, youthful infatuation or folly, possibly with a final-letter error. The pronoun in فتذودها is taken to refer back to نفسها: she restrains herself.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 2
I lingered after them beside an ailing remnant,which knew decay and wasted as things waste.
وعكفت بعدهم على ضمنعرف البلى فبلى كما يبلى

The syntax of فبلى كما يبلى is unclear. The following جسدي (‘my body’) may supply the subject of يبلى, giving ‘wasted as my body wastes,’ but it also appears to begin the paired subject ‘my body and the ruined dwelling’ in line 3.

On traces (rasm), line 1
Here are the traces—if standing over traces could avail;that is prudence—were you not so long estranged from prudence.
هو الرسم لو أغنى الوقوف على الرسمهو الحزم لولا بعد عهدك بالحزم

The referent of هو in هو الحزم ('that is prudence') is unclear; it may refer to standing at the traces.

On traces (rasm), line 2
I used to see it with its people dwelling there,band after band—what fine bands they were!
ولقد أراها والحلول بهامن بعد صرم أيما صرم

The syntax of “من بعد صرم أيما صرم” is uncertain. The translation takes ṣirm as a band of people and understands the phrase as praising successive groups of inhabitants.

On traces (rasm), line 1
My two friends, turn aside today—or leave it be—let us greet the desolate traces at al-Qubayba.
خليلي عوجا منكما اليوم أو دعانحيي رسوما بالقبيبة بلقعا

The object of أو دعا, literally 'or leave [it],' is unstated; the precise force of this alternative is uncertain.

On traces (rasm), line 1
Can it be that the eye does not see you sheddingcarnelian whenever al-ʿAqīq comes into view?
أجدك لا تراك العين تذرىعقيقا كلما لاح العقيق

The precise place intended by al-ʿAqīq is uncertain.

On traces (rasm), line 4
O king in whom hopes are placed,the world's winged perils hover over you.
ألا يأيها الملك المرجىعليك نواهض الدنيا تحوم

نواهض الدنيا evokes birds rising into flight. I have rendered it as a metaphor for looming worldly perils, but the precise reference is uncertain.

On traces (rasm), line 1
I called Salmā to mind—for one who longs remembers—and an unfulfilled desire is a sickness that takes hold.
تذكرت من سلمى وذو الشوق ذاكروحاجة من لم تقض داء مخامر

The construction وحاجة من لم تقض is grammatically unclear as printed. I have provisionally understood it as an unfulfilled desire; the wording may be incomplete or miscopied.

On traces (rasm), line 5
If a dwelling stands empty of Maylāʾ, there is no lack,in the offspring of desire, of my long-standing love for her.
فإن يخل من ميلاء ربع فما خلابنات الهوى من حبها المتقدم

بنات الهوى literally means “daughters of desire.” Its precise referent and the syntax of فما خلا بنات الهوى are uncertain; the translation takes it as feelings or thoughts born of love that still retain the speaker’s old attachment.

On traces (rasm), line 6
Those of my peers who dallied in youthful love have sobered; but love for heris death’s companion, mingled with flesh and blood.
صحا من تصابي من لداتي وحبهاشريك المنايا خيض في اللحم والدم

تصابي is read as تصابى, “acted youthfully” or “dallied in youthful love.” خيض is taken in the sense “mixed” or “mingled.” The precise force of شريك المنايا, literally “a partner of deaths,” is uncertain; it may suggest that this love will remain until death.

On traces (rasm), line 3
Then a far-off destination carried Salmā away,and a swift journey that severed the bonds of companionship.
ثم استمر بسلمى نية قذفوسير منقضب الأقران مغيار

The phrase منقضب الأقران مغيار is difficult. I tentatively understand الأقران as bonds or ties and مغيار as describing swift travel.

On traces (rasm), line 2
That is the dwelling, desolate, though once there lodgedand lived someone dear to me.
هي الدار وحشا غير أن قد يحلهاويغني بها شخص علي كريم

I read يغني as يغنى, ‘dwells,’ rather than ‘sings.’ The temporal force of قد يحلها is uncertain: the translation takes it as recalling a former inhabitant, but it could mean ‘may lodge there.’

On traces (rasm), line 4
The years pass by, yet I do not seetheir ruins disappear from the open ground of al-Shaba.
تمر السنون الماضيات ولا أرىبصحن الشبا أطلالهن تريم

The antecedent of ‘their’ in أطلالهن is unclear in this quotation. Al-Shaba is treated as a place name, but its precise identification and vocalization are uncertain. تريم literally means ‘move away’ or ‘depart,’ rendered here as ‘disappear.’

On traces (rasm), line 3
Mayy’s people departed from there, bidding farewellthere to its inhabitants, not waiting for those who trailed behind.
تحمل منها أهل مي فودعوابها أهلها لا ينظرون التواليا

The referent of أهلها ('its inhabitants') is unclear after the mention of Mayy’s departing people. لا ينظرون التواليا may mean 'not looking toward those behind' rather than 'not waiting for those who trailed behind.'

On traces (rasm), line 4
In those days with Mayy, when the tribe lived as neighbors,despite her withholding, I was dead at heart and heedless.
وقد كنت من مي إذ الحي جيرةعلى البخل منها ميت القلب ساهيا

The emotional force of ميت القلب ساهيا (literally, 'dead-hearted, heedless') in describing his relationship with Mayy is uncertain. Her 'withholding' presumably concerns affection or favor, though this is not explicit.

On remains (āthār), line 1
Was it firelight that appeared to your eyes, or was there kindledat Dhū al-Athl a fire of Salāma’s?
ضوء نار بدا لعينيك أم شببت بذي الأثل من سلامة نار

I read شب / بت, split across the hemistichs, as شُبِّبَت, 'was kindled.' The contrast between the opening firelight and Salāma’s fire is unclear.

On remains (āthār), line 1
Whom can I ask? There is neither vestige nor trace.You departed, while tears and sleeplessness remained.
لمن أسائل لا رسم ولا أثررحلتم وأقام الدمع والسهر

The opening لمن أسائل is syntactically unusual: the preposition in لمن does not fit the straightforward sense 'Whom can I ask?' adopted here. The intended construction is uncertain.

On remains (āthār), line 3
Tell him who forbids what is lawful and permitted: tomorrowyou will, by your honor, be paid in full what you now borrow.
فقل لمن يمنع الحل المباح غداتوفى وحقك ما أصبحت تقترض

الحل المباح is uncertain: it may mean simply 'what is lawful and permitted,' or refer more specifically to permitted lodging or access to the site.

On remains (āthār), line 2
The prayer of one whom separation has made contentwith traces and a landmark in place of direct sight.
دعاء من أقنعه البين بعد العين بالآثار والمعلم

بعد العين literally means 'after direct sight' or 'after the thing itself.' It is unclear whether the lost sight or presence is that of the beloved or her dwelling.

On remains (āthār), line 3
Tears that streamed, their string come undone,the morning we lingered with our sorrows at the dwelling.
دموعا جرت جريا تحلل عقدهغداة ربعنا بالهموم على الربع

The construction جرياً تحلل عقده is uncertain: literally, 'a flowing whose knot/string came undone.' I understand an image of tears streaming like beads from an unfastened string, but the pronoun's reference is unclear.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 1
By my life, if every dwelling makes you weep—of Shammāʾ, or a phantom that visits you whenever evening falls—
لعمري لئن أبكتك كل محلةلشماء أو طيف متى تمس يطرق

Shammāʾ appears to be a woman's name; her identity is unclear.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 1
May the clouds water your dwelling, and may there always beabundant rain there, and deep-red blossoms.
أسقى محلتك الغمام، ولا يزالنوء بها خضل، ونور جاسد

جاسد is an uncommon epithet for blossoms; translated as “deep-red,” though the precise color intended is uncertain.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 4
A ruin where I hold back tears eloquentwith burning grief, and read a script that cannot speak.
طللا أكفكف فيه دمعا معربابجوى، وأقرأ فيه خطا أعجما

طللا appears to be the accusative singular ṭalalan, “a ruin,” but its grammatical connection to the preceding address to two abodes is unclear.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 1
Look, you two: Buthna’s landmarks have come into view,as though their summits were turbaned with horsehair.
ألا تلكما أعلام بثنة قد بدتكأن ذراها عممت بسبيب

Sabīb (سبيب), rendered as “horsehair,” can also mean a strip of cloth. The precise image intended by the turbaned summits is uncertain.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 2
We are like a gathering of tears in our dispersal,like the secret of farewell in our wasting away.
فكأننا شمل الدموع تفرقاوكأننا سر الوداع نحولا

سر الوداع literally means 'the secret of farewell.' The precise image linking this to نحولا ('wasting away' or 'emaciation') is unclear.

On residences, stopping places, haunts, landmarks, waymarks and courtyards, line 2
We have hobbled the pale camels in their home grounds,yet they move between a gentle trot and a long-striding pace.
قد عقلنا العيس في أوطانهاوهي ما بين ذميل ووخاد

The camels are described as hobbled, yet also as moving at two different gaits. The intended relation between these descriptions is unclear; 'yet' makes the apparent contrast explicit.

On the land (arḍ), line 4
Perhaps your wanderings will one day bring you back; fora foreign land draws near, until home draws near.”
عل النوى بك يوما أن تريع، فقدتدنو الغريبة حتى يدنو الوطن

The referent of الغريبة is not explicit; “a foreign land” assumes an omitted أرض. The precise sense of its drawing near before the homeland does remains uncertain.

On the land (arḍ), line 1
Depart in the morning from the ailing land,and accept no treatment for an intractable disease but excision.
تحمل عن الأرض المريضة غادياولا ترض للداء العياء سوى الحسم

الحسم can mean cutting off or decisive termination, and can also refer to cauterization. 'Excision' preserves the force of cutting away, though the precise treatment intended is uncertain.

On the land (arḍ), whole poem

The name حبال is unvocalized; its rendering as Ḥibāl is uncertain.

On the land (arḍ), line 1
Were it not for Ḥibāl, my mount would never have knelt with mein a land of fevers, recurring and fierce.
ولولا حبال لم تنخ بي مطيتيبأرض بها الحمى بورد وصالب

ورد and صالب appear to designate types of fever. They are rendered as “recurring” and “fierce,” though the precise medical distinction is uncertain.

On the land (arḍ), line 3
Seek your earnings in lands where they may be found,where seeking them is honorable, until your allotted span runs out.
وابغ المكاسب من أرض مطالبهامن حيث يجمل حتى ينفد الأجل

The construction من أرض مطالبها / من حيث يجمل is compressed and somewhat unclear. I take it to mean seeking earnings where they are obtainable and where doing so is fitting or honorable.

On the land (arḍ), line 1
How can I stay in a land where I cannot saddlemy travel-worn mount when a surge of anger seizes me?
كيف المقام بأرض لا أشد بهانضوى إذا ما اعترتني سورة الغضب؟

أشدّ نضوي is taken here as saddling or making ready a travel-worn mount; the verb literally means to bind or fasten, so the precise action intended is uncertain.

On the land (arḍ), line 4
For I am parted from one—I left my life flourishingbeside him, and my honor finding refuge on his heights.
لفرقة من خليت دنياي غضةلديه، وعزى معصما في يفاعه

I read خليت as khallaytu, ‘I left,’ and معصما as muʿṣiman, ‘seeking or finding refuge.’ The wording is compressed, and the precise relationship between leaving the person and leaving one’s flourishing life with him is uncertain.

On the land (arḍ), line 1
I say to my companion, as he wanders distraught with longingfor a distant flash of lightning he cannot clearly make out:
أقول لصاحبي إذ هام وجداببرق ليس يثبته نزوحا

The construction ليس يثبته نزوحا is uncertain. I take يثبته to mean ‘make out distinctly’ and نزوحا (‘far distant’) to describe the lightning.

On the land (arḍ), line 3
Everything there has fallen ill except the east wind,and grown soft—except manners, water, and wine.
قد اعتل فيها كل شيء سوى الصباورق سوى الأخلاق والماء والخمر

رقّ can mean “grew thin,” “delicate,” or “soft.” Its precise force here is uncertain; the exceptions may suggest coarse manners, hard water, and harsh wine.

On the land (arḍ), line 1
Bid farewell, man of resolve, to Miṣr—not Lamīs—and plungeon swift steeds into the depths of the desert wastes.
ودع أخا العزم مصرا، لا لميس، وخفضبالسابحات غمار المهمه البيد

لميس is understood as the woman's name Lamīs; her identity or the specific allusion is unclear.

On homelands (awṭān), line 2
I love it—by Him who set its foundations firm—with a love that lies hidden when its signs appear.
أحبه والذي أرسى قواعدهحبا إذا ظهرت آياته بطنا

The wording «إذا ظهرت آياته بطنا» is puzzling: literally, the love becomes hidden when its signs appear. It may mean that its full depth remains concealed despite its outward signs.

On homelands (awṭān), line 4
Water it with a night cloud bearing the rain of nearness,for it lies ruined, its very site effaced.
وسقه من حيا التقريب ساريةفإنه دائر قد مح موضعه

The wording دائر قد مح موضعه is uncertain. I take it as describing an effaced or ruined dwelling, reading مح as مُحَّ, 'was worn away or effaced.'

On homelands (awṭān), line 2
and son of lords who trodthe broad way and ruled Ghawr and Najd:
وابن أرباب واطئ السبب الأرحب والمالكين غورا ونجدا

واطئ is singular as printed, although the surrounding construction seems to require plural واطئي, 'those who tread.' السبب الأرحب is tentatively rendered 'the broad way'; its precise reference is unclear.

On homelands (awṭān), line 2
A time whose lingering memory shakes me,though it is past and does not return.
زمن راعني تذكره الثاوي وإن كان ماضيا لا يريع

الثاوي ('abiding' or 'lingering'), divided between the hemistichs, is taken as modifying 'memory'; its grammatical attachment is uncertain.

On homelands (awṭān), line 3
and gives me freedom now,and my friends let me go,
وأخلى ذرعي الآن، وخلاني خلاني

أخلى ذرعي is uncertain; ‘gives me freedom’ is tentative. خلاني خلاني is read as خَلّاني خِلّاني, ‘my friends let me go,’ though the intended sense is not entirely clear.

On homelands (awṭān), line 5
And if I return to it one day,may my jailer shroud me.
فإن عدت لها يومافسجاني سجاني

فسجاني سجاني is read as فَسَجّاني سَجّاني: ‘may my jailer shroud me,’ taking the first word from سجّى, ‘cover or shroud,’ and the second as سجّان, ‘jailer.’ The unvocalized wordplay leaves some uncertainty.

On homelands (awṭān), line 4
O tamarisks of the plain, my heart is boundto you, but there is little hope of reaching you.
ويا أثلات القاع قلبي موكلبكن وجدوى نيلكن قليل

The expression «جدوى نيلكن قليل» is compressed and uncertain: literally something like “the benefit of attaining you is little.” It is rendered here as little hope of reaching the trees again.

On homelands (awṭān), line 2
It is as though the earth were displeased with me:I have neither a homeland upon it nor a wish fulfilled.
كأنما الأرض عني غير راضيةفليس لي وطن فيها ولا وطر

Waṭar can mean a need, aim, or object of desire. Its sense here is uncertain; 'a wish fulfilled' takes it to mean the attainment of what one desires.

On homelands (awṭān), line 5
So excuse your brother, Ibn Zinbāʿ, for he has,in times of adversity, evasions of many kinds.
فاعذر أخاك ابن زنباع فإن لهفي الحادثات هنات ذات ألوان

The precise force of هنات is uncertain: it can mean minor matters, faults, or peculiarities. “Evasions” follows the next line’s description of changing his claimed ancestry.

On homelands (awṭān), line 4
So desist as Rawḥ desisted: I am a maneither of pure lineage or a puffball of the plain.
فاكفف كما كف روح إنني رجلإما صويح وإما فقعة القاع

The supplied صويح is unclear. I tentatively read صريح, 'of pure lineage,' in contrast to فقعة القاع, a puffball growing on open ground, suggesting someone without recognized ancestry.

On homelands (awṭān), line 2
I lodged among a people—may God keep them united—who have no stock to press but glory.
نزلت بقوم يجمع الله شملهموليس لهم عود سوى المجد يعتصر

The image in عود سوى المجد يعتصر is unusual: literally, “no stem/wood except glory that is pressed.” The translation preserves the apparent metaphor of extracting glory from their stock, but its precise force is uncertain.

On homelands (awṭān), line 1
A house I dwelt in unwillingly; never didmy soul find comfort in any companion there, or any attachment.
دار سكنت بها كرها وما سكنتنفسي إلى سكن فيها ولا شجن

The pairing سكن ولا شجن is uncertain. سكن can mean a companion or someone who affords comfort; شجن usually means sorrow or concern, but may also denote a desire or attachment, the sense adopted here.

On homelands (awṭān), line 4
My soul rejects that: it cannot be boundby staying put, nor can desires rule it.
أبى ذاك نفس لا يداني عقالهاثواء، ولا تقضي عليها المطامع

The compressed expression «لا يداني عقالها ثواء», literally something like ‘settled residence does not approach its tether,’ is uncertain. I understand it to mean that remaining in one place cannot bind the speaker’s soul.

On homelands (awṭān), line 2
From a night-roamer whose ambition is like the night’s star,stouthearted, casting no backward glance toward any homeland.
عن ابن ليل كنجم الليل همتهمشيع القلب لا يلوي على وطن

ابن ليل, literally “son of night,” is taken here as a night-roamer or night-traveler; the epithet’s precise implication is uncertain.

On homelands (awṭān), line 1
My homes are among the homelands laid waste;two lifetimes of mine have passed among thriving dwellings.
من الخراب من الأوطان أوطانيوقد مضى لي في العمران عمران

I read عمران as the dual of عُمر, “two lifetimes,” in wordplay with العمران, “inhabited or flourishing places”; the intended force of the dual is uncertain.

On cities (mudun), line 2
Ask the cities about them,and seek tidings from the thickets.
سائلوا عنهم المدائن واستخبروا الخمر

الخمر is uncertain. I read it as al-khamar, ‘thickets’ or ‘coverts,’ which fits the rhyme in -ar, rather than al-khamr, ‘wine.’

On cities (mudun), line 3
I nearly agreed, then remembered our milch-camels at nightat Liwā ʿUnayzah or Quff Bassām,
فهممت ثم ذكرت ليل لقاحنابلوى عنيزة أو بقف بسام

Liwā ʿUnayzah and Quff Bassām are unidentified here; the vocalization of Bassām is uncertain. The phrase ليل لقاحنا, literally “the night of our milch-camels,” is compressed and somewhat obscure.

On cities (mudun), line 2
I see one who pins his hopes on al-ʿIrāq and its peopleas a man thirsty in the midday heat, hoping for a mirage.
وأرى المرجى للعراق وأهلهظمآن هاجرة يؤمل آلا

I read المرجى as المرجِّي, “one who hopes.” The printed spelling could suggest a passive form, “one hoped for,” which is difficult to construe here.

On countries (bilād), line 3
There we were free of bewildering care and its draught,and its joy brought bliss round to us.
فقدنا بها الهم المضل وشربهودار علينا بالنعيم سرورها

وشربه is unclear. 'And its draught' is tentative; شربه could also refer to drinking companions. The intended expression, or the integrity of the text, is uncertain.

On countries (bilād), line 2
And the two sacred sites, and a mosqueat al-Khayf, frequented every year,
والمشعرين ومسجدبالخيف يشهد كل عام

The precise places intended by al-mashʿarayn, “the two sacred sites,” are uncertain.

On countries (bilād), line 3
And from clinging to the two sacred sites,and from prayer at the Maqām,
وعن التزام المشعرين وعن صلاة بالمقام

Iltizām means embracing or clinging to; its application here to “the two sacred sites” is unusual, and the intended ritual action is unclear.

On countries (bilād), line 1
O my two friends, whom I regardas my trusted confidants above all who show me care,
ألا يا خليلي اللذين أراهماذوي ثقتي من دون من كان حافيا

حافيا is uncertain here. I have tentatively understood it as someone showing care or solicitude; its more familiar meaning, “barefoot,” does not readily fit the context.

On countries (bilād), line 1
I speak, having passed Naqamā, while my she-camelyearns at dawn for the two banks of Fulayj.
أقول وقد جاوزت نقمي وناقتيتحن إلى جنبي فليج مع الفجر

The vocalization of نقمي, rendered Naqamā, is uncertain. I take جنبي فليج as the two banks or sides of the place Fulayj; its precise geographical reference is unclear.

On countries (bilād), line 2
May God water, O she-camel, the lands whereyour heart lies, though the roads to that region lie far from us.
سقى الله يا ناق البلاد التي بهاهواك وإن عنا نأت سبل القطر

I read القطر as quṭr, ‘region,’ and understand سبل القطر as the roads to that region. The unvocalized word can also mean ‘rain’ (Qaṭr), but the phrase would then be unclear.

On countries (bilād), line 3
One who sees her only on a brief visit is not the sameas another who dwells beside her and never leaves her.
وما يستوي من لا يرى غير لمةوآخر ثاو عندها لا يريمها

I take «لمة» to mean a brief visit or encounter, with Laylā understood as the object of «يرى» (‘sees’); the unvocalized wording is uncertain.

On countries (bilād), line 1
Sulaymā said, “You once lived as a young man;but today you neither kill outright nor mortally wound.
قالت سليمى قد غنيت فتىفاليوم لا تصمى ولا تنمى

I read تصمى and تنمى as tuṣmī and tunmī: hunting terms for killing game on the spot and wounding it so that it dies after disappearing from sight. Whether the hunting language is literal or figurative here is uncertain.

On countries (bilād), line 4
A land where a star loses its way,and its darkness turns its phantom back from visiting.
بلاد يضل النجم فيها سبيلهويثنى دجاها طيفها عن لمامه

I read «يثنى» as «يثني» ('turns back'), with «دجاها» ('its darkness') as the subject. Whose apparition is meant by «طيفها» ('its phantom') is unclear; the translation retains the literal possessive.

On countries (bilād), line 1
God bless the fiercely proud man! He was deniedhis honor amid humiliation, and so withdrew.
لله مر الأباء أعوزهمن جانب الذل عزه فنبا

I read الأباء as الإباء ('proud refusal'). The construction أعوزه ... عزه is uncertain; I take it to mean that he could find no honor in a setting of humiliation.

On countries (bilād), line 2
Perhaps its rainfall will bring our camp nearer,despite the obstacles, to Rumaym’s distant home.
لعل مصابها يدنى نواناعلى عدوائه لنوى رميم

Rumaym is apparently a personal name, probably a woman’s; its vocalization is uncertain. نوانا and نوى رميم can denote our separation or destination and Rumaym’s; the rendering as separate dwelling places is interpretive. The antecedent of the pronoun in على عدوائه ('despite its difficulties') is unclear.

On countries (bilād), line 2
Its flickering was like the flashing of a hand—a woman’s, speaking with terror in her heart.
كأن وميضه لمعان كفمخاطبة على هول الجنان

على هول الجنان is obscure. The translation tentatively takes الجنان as “heart” and the phrase as describing the speaking woman’s terror.

On countries (bilād), line 2
Among maidens who have stolen their glancesfrom the fawns of the sandy tract.
في جوار قد سلبن اللحظ أطلاء الصريم

I take الصريم to mean a tract of sand cut off from the surrounding sands; its precise sense here is uncertain.

On countries (bilād), line 2
And what a wretched exchange—the phantom of sleeplessness in place of sleep.
ولبئسما متبدلطيف السهاد من الرقاد

The syntax of متبدل is uncertain, and طيف السهاد literally means “the phantom of sleeplessness.” I understand the line as lamenting the replacement of sleep by this wakeful vision.

On countries (bilād), line 3
If they keep you from him, he will be visitedby your phantom, brought by the night visitations of his sleep.
إن يحجبوك تزره طيفك طارقات منامه

I tentatively read تزره as تُزِرْهُ, a causative form meaning 'bring ... to visit him,' with طارقات منامه ('the night visitations of his sleep') as its subject. The construction is uncertain, and the shift from 'my blood' to third-person 'him' is unexplained.

On countries (bilād), line 1
May the land where Sulaymā now dwells be wateredwith rain enough to quench its thirst and provide pasture.
سقى بلدا أمست سليمى تحلهمن المزن ما يروى به ويسيم

The verb يسيم normally means to put livestock out to graze. Its subject and implied object are unclear here; 'provide pasture' renders the probable sense.

On countries (bilād), line 1
The dearest of God's lands is the country between Manʿijand Salmā, to me—may its clouds pour down rain.
أحب بلاد الله ما بين منعجإلي، وسلمى، أن يصوب سحابها

The syntax of أن يصوب سحابها is uncertain; it is rendered here as a wish for rain.

On countries (bilād), line 4
May the land where Sulaymā now dwells be wateredwith rain from the clouds to quench its thirst and provide pasture.
سقى بلدا أمست سليمى تحلهمن المزن ما يروى به ويسيم

The exact construction and sense of ويسيم are uncertain. It appears to refer to grazing or providing pasture; the translation follows the latter sense.

On the house (dār), line 3
When your intimates have left you for their destination,along with those who kept you company, you are the first to go.
وإذا مضى الآلاف عنك لطيةوالمؤنسون، فأنت أول ذاهب

لطية means toward a destination or on a journey; death may be intended here. The force of «فأنت أول ذاهب» ('you are the first to go'), after the companions have departed, is unclear.

On the house (dār), line 3
Once there were people dwelling in it,owners of herds, horses, and domed tents.
وبما قد كان فيها ساكنأهل أنعام وخيل وقباب

The construction وبما قد is uncertain; it is taken here as introducing a recollection of the abode’s former inhabitants.

On the house (dār), line 2
The people who once lived there have departed;its outline has faded and become like sheath-linings.
ظعن الحي الألى كانوا بهاوعفا رسم وأضحى كالخلل

The comparison كالخلل is uncertain. 'Sheath-linings' provisionally takes الخلل as khilal, the plural of a word for the lining of a sword sheath.

On the house (dār), line 4
For I have feared that no abode would bring us together,nor time itself—save in the wishes we renew.
فقد خفت ألا تجمع الدار بينناولا الدهر إلا أن نجد الأمانيا

I provisionally read نجد as nujiddu, ‘we renew,’ from أجَدّ. The unvocalized wording and the relation of the final exception to the preceding statement are uncertain; the translation takes it to mean that reunion survives only in renewed wishes.

On the house (dār), line 1
O dwelling, deserted since its people left,nothing remains within it but its fastenings.
يا دار أقوت من بعد حاضرهالم يبق فيها سوى أواصرها

أواصر usually means bonds or ties. Its physical referent here is uncertain; “fastenings” provisionally takes it as the cords or attachments of the former encampment.

On the house (dār), line 3
Hail, ruined campsite, for what the wide-eyed cows, tender toward their calves, have left in you.
حييت من دمنة بما خلفت عين عطوف على جآذرها

The construction بما خلفت عين is unclear. The translation provisionally reads خلفت as “left behind” and عين as “wide-eyed wild cows,” whose young are جآذر. It may instead describe wild cattle replacing the former inhabitants, but the wording does not make that reading secure.

On the house (dār), line 2
They went forth like Indian swords, entering the thickof death; their entry into it allowed no return.
غدوا كسيوف الهند وراد حومةمن الموت أعيا وردهن المصادر

The compressed phrase أعيا وردهن المصادر uses the imagery of approaching and leaving a watering place. I understand it to mean that entering the fray left no possibility of return. The feminine pronoun in وردهن apparently refers to the swords to which the warriors are compared, but the construction is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 5
May their mother be bereaved of them—and bereaved she was, the day they settled at Ḥārith al-Jawlān.
نكلت أمهموقد ثكلتهم يوم حلوا بحارث الجولان

نكلت أمهم is unclear as printed. The translation assumes ثكلت أمهم, “May their mother be bereaved of them,” supported by وقد ثكلتهم, “and she was indeed bereaved of them,” immediately afterward.

On the house (dār), line 3
Ask the days about their kings:what milk the milch camel has withheld from them!
سائل الأيام عن أملاكهاأي در قطعت عنها اللبون

أملاكها is read as ‘their kings,’ though it can also mean ‘their possessions.’ The syntax of the second hemistich is uncertain, particularly the antecedent of عنها (‘from them/it’). The translation tentatively takes the milch camel’s withholding of milk as an image of bounty withdrawn from the kings.

On the house (dār), line 1
This is no stopping-place forthe grief-stricken; it stands deserted, a remnant of devastating time.
ما إن هذا موقفالجازع أقوى، وسؤر الزمن الفاجع

The text appears metrically disturbed, and the supplied hemistich break splits موقف الجازع ('the stopping-place of the grief-stricken'). The connection of أقوى وسؤر is uncertain; I take أقوى as 'stands deserted' and سؤر as 'remnant.'

On the house (dār), line 3
In those days I never approached a dwelling of your peopleexcept warily, under cover of darkness.
أيام لا أغشى لأهلك منزلاإلا مراقبة، على ظلام

The construction إلا مراقبة، على ظلام is somewhat uncertain: مراقبة may mean keeping watch rather than proceeding warily; على ظلام is taken as 'under cover of darkness.'

On the house (dār), line 8
My friend said—while weeping overcame me—“Will this grief and longing prove fatal?”
وقال خليليوالبكالي غالب أقاض على هذا الأسى والتشوق؟

البكالي appears to represent البكا لي, “weeping … over me.” The wording أقاض على is uncertain: it may represent أقاضٍ عليَّ, “will … finish me off?” The translation leaves the affected person unspecified because the pronoun and the boundaries of the friend's speech are unclear.

On the house (dār), line 2
And from him whom Time brought low in death,and whose armies disowned him?
وبمن أذل الدهر مصرعهوتبرأت منه عساكره

The grammar of أذل الدهر مصرعه is uncertain without vowel marks. The translation takes Time as the agent of humiliation at death; another possible reading is ‘whose downfall humbled Time.’

On the house (dār), line 1
Where are the generations that neglected their own good,until their cupbearer gave them drink from the cup of death?
أين القرون التي عن حظها غفلتحتى سقاها بكأس الموت ساقيها

Ḥaẓẓ (حظ), rendered as “their own good,” can also mean one's share or lot; its precise sense here is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 2
In it we are stricken by what is not sweet,and choke on what it gives us—not clear water.
نفجع فيها بغير اللذيذ ونشرق منها بغير الزلال

The wording نفجع فيها بغير اللذيذ is unusual. I understand it literally as being afflicted by something that is not sweet; the precise force of نفجع here is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 1
Janūb has forsaken me—yet how dear is she who shuns me!Adversities have barred my way to your nearness, driving us apart.
هجرت جنوب وحب من يتجنبوعدت عواد دون وليك تشعب

I take حب as an exclamation of affection, “how dear”; its precise grammatical construction is uncertain in the unvowelled text.

On the house (dār), line 3
Though you stand empty, this is not the first calamitythat has left the covert empty of gazelles.
ولئن خلوت فليس أول حادثخلت الكناس له من الغزلان

الكناس is understood as the gazelles’ covert, but its agreement with the feminine verb خلت is unclear as printed.

On the house (dār), line 2
Time’s vicissitudes have indeed wronged you,assailing you with every grievous calamity.
لقد جارت عليك صروف دهررمتك بكل داهية ناد

ناد is obscure as printed; I take it as نآد, ‘grievous’ or ‘overwhelming,’ qualifying ‘calamity.’

On the house (dār), line 1
My companions say: “You have kept us standing longat the dwelling, bereft of solace and self-command.
يقول صحابي: قد أطلت وقوفناعلى الدار مسلوب الأسى والتماسك

الأسى is taken here as al-usā, ‘solace’ or ‘consolation.’ The more usual reading al-asā means ‘grief,’ which would be awkward after مسلوب, ‘bereft of’; the intended reading is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 1
Ah, my loneliness in the abode, now bereft of wide-eyed gazelles!
وا وحشتي في الدار لما أصبحت موشحة من الظباء العين

The text reads موشحة (‘adorned’ or ‘girdled’), which is difficult to reconcile with من الظباء and the ensuing description of abandonment. The translation tentatively reads موحشة (‘desolate’), taking the phrase to mean deserted by the wide-eyed gazelles.

On the house (dār), line 3
After this day, no meeting can be hoped for,unless the darkness of night and its daylight meet.
ما بعد يومك من لقاء يرتجىأو يلتقي جنح الدجى ونهاره

The force of أو before يلتقي is uncertain: it can introduce an 'until' or 'unless' condition. Here it is taken as 'unless,' apparently making reunion depend on night and day meeting.

On the house (dār), line 5
The days lent them, then took them back;every miser keeps a tight hold on his gifts.
أعارتهم الأيام وارتجعتهموكل بخيل في مواهبه ضبط

The precise reading of ضبط is uncertain. It appears to describe someone who keeps a firm hold on things; the translation follows that sense.

On the house (dār), line 3
A heart—whenever I say it is coming to its senses,you two bring love and longing upon it, time and again.
فؤاد إذا ما قلت يصحو جلبتماعليه الهوى والشوق كل أوان

The opening فؤاد ('a heart') has an uncertain syntactic connection to the rest of the sentence. The dual جلبتما ('you two bring') apparently addresses the speaker’s two eyes.

On the house (dār), line 1
O dwelling, what ails the riders, now that I have halted them?Not even a drop of tears has watered you.
يا دار ما للكرب حين وقفتهمما إن سقاك من الدموع لماظ

The text reads الكرب ('anguish'), which is difficult to construe here. The translation tentatively reads الركب ('the riders'), a likely transposition of letters, consistent with the plural pronouns that follow.

On the house (dār), line 2
Yearning for it and writhing with heartache,as though you were a woman among the tribe in difficult labor.
حنينا إليها والتواء من الجوىكأنك في الحي الولود المطرق

I understand الولود المطرق as a woman undergoing difficult childbirth, though the precise sense of المطرق here is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 3
I revere the soil of the land where they once dwelt,and passing over it fills me with anguish and fear.
أجل تراب الأرض كانوا حلولهاوأجزع من مرى عليها وأشفق

مرى is unclear as printed. I have read it as مرّي, ‘my passing,’ giving ‘passing over it’ in the translation.

On the house (dār), line 1
O dwelling, may gentle showers of dew pour upon you,and may your meadow stir in the moist earth and sway.
يا دار در عليك أرهام الندىواهتز روضك في الثرى فترأدا

أرهام is uncertain as printed; it may represent إرهام, meaning light rainfall. The translation takes أرهام الندى as gentle showers of dew.

On the house (dār), line 3
I recognized nothing there in which to take comfortexcept the thumām grass and the place where the fire was lit.
فما عرفت بها شيئا أعيج بهإلا الثمام، وإلا موقد النار

The precise sense of أعيج به is uncertain here: it can suggest taking heed of something or finding benefit in it. It is rendered contextually as “in which to take comfort.”

On the house (dār), line 3
The wind swept over it with fiercely gusting skirts,until its faded remains were like a threadbare cloak.
جرت عليها بأذيال لها عصففأصبحت مثل سحق البرد عافيها

I take عافيها to refer to the dwelling's faded remains, but its precise grammatical role in the transmitted wording is unclear.

On the house (dār), line 3
Whenever I wish, I am moved to tears at Jarʿāʾ Mālikas far as al-Daḥl, by Mayy's desert camp and settled dwelling.
إذا شئت أبكاني بجرعاء مالكإلى الدحل مستبدي لمي ومحضر

مستبدي is understood as مستبدى, a place of dwelling in the open desert, contrasted with محضر, a settled dwelling or encampment at a watering place. The precise seasonal distinction, if intended, is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 7
Misfortunes kept me from you, Mayy, for a time;one may be diverted from the beloved and so stay away.
عدتني العوادي عنك يا مي برهةوقد يلتوى دون الحبيب فيهجر

يلتوى دون الحبيب فيهجر has no explicit subject, and its unvocalized verbs allow uncertainty about agency. The translation takes it to mean that someone is diverted from reaching the beloved and consequently remains apart.

On the house (dār), line 4
Mayy has departed: there stands her dwelling,where dark birds and ring-necked doves strut.
ألا ظعنت مي فهاتيك دارهابها السحم تردي والحمام المطوق

السحم means dark or black creatures, probably ravens here; the precise referent is uncertain. تردي describes their gait, possibly hopping rather than strutting.

On the house (dār), line 3
If one day his hardship falls into your hands,in your hands lie both his hardship and his ease.
إن يحر عسره بكفيك يومافبكفيك عسره ويساره

إن يحر عسره بكفيك is unclear. The translation tentatively takes يحر from حار يحور (‘return’), understanding the phrase as his hardship coming into the patron’s hands.

On the house (dār), line 2
Why did you not recall those nights of lifewhen oaths were sworn?
ألا ذكرت ليالي العيشالتي فيها القسامه

القسامة is interpreted as oath-taking, in keeping with the surrounding references to a covenant. The word can also denote beauty; the intended sense is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 6
And may you be repaid for it, besides your breach—of kinship and foulest conduct—with humiliation.
وجزيت فيها إلى العقوق وأسوإ الخلق الرغامة

The syntax is difficult. This translation reads جزيت as a passive imprecation, الرغامة as ‘humiliation,’ and إلى as ‘in addition to.’ The source divides العقوق, ‘breach of kinship,’ between the two hemistichs.

On the house (dār), line 8
Your covenant was not like the oneIbn ʿAmr made with Ibn Māmah.
ما كان عقدك مثل ماعقد ابن عمرو لابن مامه

The identities of Ibn ʿAmr and Ibn Māmah, and the particular covenant invoked, are uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 2
of all God's lands, most wish the tract between Munʿijand Salmā to have its clouds pour down rain?
أحب بلاد الله ما بين منعجإلي وسلمى أن يصوب سحابها

The syntax is compressed and uncertain, particularly the connection of ‘an yaṣūba saḥābuhā’ (‘that its clouds pour down rain’) with ‘aḥabb … ilayya’ (‘dearest to me’). I understand the speaker to wish rain upon this tract above all other lands.

On the house (dār), line 2
After those who knew it last were there, it is likethe written sheets of the Persians, or the embroidered patterns of robes.
كأنها بعد عهد العاهدين بهامهارق العجم أو مشية الحلل

مشية الحلل literally suggests 'the gait of robes,' which is obscure. The translation provisionally assumes وشية الحلل, 'the embroidered patterns of robes.'

On the house (dār), line 3
A dwelling where we lived awhile—and what prosperityfrom its people—
دار غنينا بها حينا، وأي غنىعن أهله

Lines 3–4 appear to contain one verse broken into irregular fragments. غنى is ambiguous here: 'prosperity' is provisional, but the preceding غنينا ('we dwelt') may suggest dwelling or residence instead. The translation tentatively links the fragments as 'what prosperity … has not passed away from its people?'

On the house (dār), line 3
ease the longing of a soul that defied you, and whosecares now pull it in different directions, not as one?
يريح هوى نفس عصتك وأصبحتتنازع شتى لا جميعا شجونها

The syntax of تنازع شتى لا جميعا شجونها is uncertain. I take it to describe the soul’s cares pulling it in conflicting directions.

On the house (dār), line 2
There was our time with al-Mālikiyya, and it ended;so it is with fair women: their pledges do not last.
بها كان عهد المالكية فانقضىكذاك الغواني لا تدوم عهودها

Al-Mālikiyya apparently designates a woman by tribal affiliation; her identity is unclear. عهد may mean a period of acquaintance or a pledge, and the translation reflects both senses across the two hemistichs.

On the house (dār), line 2
May its courtyard be watered by clouds with low-hanging skirts,far-reaching, their rain-bearing train close at hand—
جيدت بداني الأكناف ساحتهانائي المدى داني الحيا سربه

The wording «داني الحيا سربه» is difficult. I tentatively understand «سربه» as the clouds’ flock or train, with «داني الحيا» describing the nearness of their rain; the precise syntax and sense remain uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 2
May the sky shower you with rain under al-Saʿd, that you may prosper,and al-Ghafr—perhaps your people's sins will be forgiven.
بالسعد جادتك السماء لتسعديوالغفر، عل ذنوب أهلك تغفر

Al-Saʿd and al-Ghafr appear to name stars or lunar mansions associated with rain; the precise referent of al-Saʿd is uncertain. Their names echo the words for prospering (Tasʿadī) and being forgiven (tughfar).

On the house (dār), line 1
Were I in the dwelling at the foot of al-Ṣafā,I would fall ill—but the one who tends me is away.
ولو كنت في الدار التي مسقط الصفامرضت، ولكن غاب عني معللي

The phrase التي مسقط الصفا is grammatically incomplete or unusually elliptical as printed. The rendering 'at the foot of al-Ṣafā' is tentative; it is unclear whether al-Ṣafā denotes the hill in Mecca or another location.

On the house (dār), line 2
Or is it an old campsite, from which the east wind has swept dusky sand,as writings are spread out after being folded?
أم دمنة نسفت عنها الصبا سفعاكما تنشر بعد الطية الكتب

The referent of سفعا, literally 'dusky/dark-colored things,' is uncertain. The translation supplies 'sand' as material swept from the campsite, exposing its traces.

On the house (dār), line 6
Radiant, she gives still greater delight when she unveils,yet the eye is constrained when she wears her veil.
غراء تزداد إبهاجا إذا سفرتوتحرج العين فيها حين تنتقب

The precise force of تحرج العين فيها is uncertain. 'The eye is constrained' takes تحرج in the sense of experiencing restriction or difficulty, apparently because the veil limits the view of her beauty.

On the house (dār), line 2
What has enslaved my heart is that longing never abates,and that fever marks whoever dwells in the protected precinct.
وتيمني أن الجوى غير مقصروأن الحمى وصف لمن حل بالحمى

The connection of وتيمني ('and it enslaved me in love') with the following clauses is somewhat obscure. I read the two occurrences of الحمى as ḥummā ('fever') and ḥimā ('protected pasture or precinct'), respectively; whether the latter denotes a particular place is unclear.

On the house (dār), line 1
May the traces of the dwelling where you are be wateredby dark clouds pouring rain in summer and spring.
سقى طلل الدار التي أنتم بهاحناتم وبل، صيف وربيع
