Ḥanātim (حناتم) is obscure here; it is provisionally understood as dark rain clouds. The construction حناتم وبل، صيف وربيع is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 3
With pealing thunder, flashing fiercely as it rumblesin the rain-season of al-Thurayyā, or of Nathrat al-Asad.
مجلجل الرعد عراصا إذا ارتجستنوء الثريا به، أو نثرة الأسد

The syntax of إذا ارتجست نوء الثريا به is unclear as printed. I understand the two stellar rain-seasons as specifying when the cloud thunders, but the grammatical connection is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 6
Mayy once dwelt there; now she has been castaway from us by a journey toward a far-off destination.
كانت تحل بها مي، فقد قذفتعنا بها نية من طية قدد

نية and طية can both denote an intended destination or direction of travel; their exact relationship here is uncertain. I take قدد as describing a distant destination.

On the house (dār), line 1
O ruins of al-ʿĀmiriyyah’s dwelling at al-Liwā,May the seasonal rains water your grounds! What has become of Hind?
أأطلال دار العامرية باللوىسقت ربعك الأنواء ما فعلت هند؟

Al-ʿĀmiriyyah means 'the woman of ʿĀmir,' a tribal designation; she presumably is Hind, but her identity is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 3
She stayed there until the stalk withered in the soil,and dawn wrapped al-Thurayyā in its mantle.
أقامت به حتى ذوي العود في الثرىولف الثريا في ملاءته الفجر

The feminine subject of أقامت ('stayed') is uncertain: it may be Mayy or the summer clouds mentioned in line 2. The translation takes it as Mayy.

On the house (dār), line 3
I spoke to my soul, directing my shametoward it, while tears had wet my eyelids:
وقلت لنفسي في حياء رددتهإلهيا وقد بل الجفون بلالها

إلهيا appears to be a transposition error for إليها, “toward it,” referring to the soul. The phrase في حياء رددته إليها, literally “in shame that I turned back toward it,” is awkward, and its precise sense remains uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 4
“Is it for a dwelling whose people separation scatteredlike the people of Sabaʾ after I left, and over which long years have passed,
أمن أجل دار طير البين أهلهاأيادي سبا بعدي وطال احتبالها

احتبالها ordinarily suggests ensnaring or holding captive, which is difficult here. The translation tentatively assumes احتيالها, referring to the passage of years over the dwelling; the transmitted reading might instead refer to its enduring hold on the speaker.

On the house (dār), line 4
And nothing like what I suffer, when the clan are neighbors,does any Muslim suffer in the wake of the departing litters.
ولا مثل ما ألقى إذ الحي جيرةعلى أثر الأظعان يلقاه مسلم

The temporal relationship between 'when the clan are neighbors' and 'in the wake of the departing litters' is unclear.

On the house (dār), line 3
If only some part of Sanīr would appear to my companions,at Rawqay Ghazāl, like a gazelle’s horn.
فليت سنيرا بان منه لصحبتيبروقى غزال مثل قرن غزال

بروقى غزال is unclear. I tentatively read it as ‘at Rawqay Ghazāl,’ an unidentified place-name; its spelling and vocalization are uncertain. The translation takes مثل قرن غزال as describing the small portion of Sanīr the speaker wishes were visible, but the syntax is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 5
My two companions, may the dwellings of Jilliq be wateredby rain that quenches its parched hollows.
يا صاحبي سقى منازل جلقغيث يروى ممحلات طساسها

طساس is obscure here. I take it as the plural of طس, ‘basin,’ referring figuratively to hollows in the land.

On the house (dār), line 1
O dwelling between al-Raqqatayn and Bābil,may the clouds rend their bosoms over you.
يا دار بين الرقتين وبابلشقت عليك من السحاب جيوب

Al-Raqqatayn means 'the two Raqqas'; the precise pair of settlements intended is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 3
Be as you please: to me you are,and to everyone, one of Death’s dwellings.
وكوني كيف شئت، فأنت عنديوعند الناس من دور القبوض

The meaning of القبوض is uncertain here. I have provisionally understood it as ‘the seizer,’ an epithet of Death; a reference to seizure or confiscation may instead be intended.

On the house (dār), line 3
In this abode, in this place, uponthis throne I saw glory—and it passed away.
في هذا الدار، في هذا المكان علىهذا السرير رأيت العز فانقرضا

Sarīr, translated as 'throne,' can also mean a couch or bed; the precise setting is unclear.

On the house (dār), line 2
Honor your own self; if a dwelling grows too crampedfor you there, seek yourself another dwelling.
ونفسك فأكرمها فإن ضاق مسكنعليك بها فاطلب لنفسك مسكنا

The pronoun in بها, rendered 'there,' appears to refer back to the abode in line 1, though its reference is uncertain.

On the house (dār), line 1
If a man shows little fairness to his friendfor no known reason, there is no blame in parting.
إذا قل إنصاف الفتى لصديقهعلى غير معروف فلا لوم في الهجر

The phrase على غير معروف is awkward and its intended sense uncertain; provisionally translated as “for no known reason.”

On the house (dār), line 2
May the Merciful never remember the day or the nightwhen we took you as wife—it was no Night of Decree.
ولا ذكر الرحمن يوما وليلةملكناك فيها لم تكن ليلة القدر

The syntax of لم تكن ليلة القدر ('it was not the Night of Decree') is uncertain. It is translated as a separate statement, but it may instead qualify the preceding curse, exempting the sacred Night of Decree.

On the house (dār), line 2
Whenever my hand happens to miss my foot,must I fall, in your eyes, into a calamity that brings me to ruin?
أكلما أخطأت يوما يدي قدميهويت عندك في زوراء ترديني؟

“My hand misses my foot” is translated literally; it apparently means making a false move or committing an error, but the expression is unclear. زوراء can denote something crooked or a calamity; its precise sense here is uncertain. عندك may mean “in your presence” rather than “in your eyes.”

On the house (dār), line 2
But my heart settled there and held me back,and kept me, in abasement, from the wide-open world.
ولكن قلبي حل فيها فعاقنيوأقعدني بالصغر عن فسحة الفضا

The sense of بالصغر is uncertain here. I have taken it as 'in abasement'; it may instead suggest smallness or confinement, in contrast to the open expanse.

On the house (dār), line 1
I love the dwelling where Sulaymā lives,even if droughts efface it.
أحب الدار تسكنها سليمىوإن كانت تواريها الجدوب

تواريها الجدوب literally means “droughts conceal it.” The image is uncertain; “efface” assumes that drought obliterates the dwelling’s traces.

On the house (dār), line 3
Nor am I unmindful of those who frequented the dwelling;nor is my lovesickness dispelled, nor does my heart turn away.
ولا أنا عمن يألف الدار ذاهلولا التبل مردود ولا القلب عازف

التبل can mean rancor or a claim for vengeance, but here I take it as the affliction caused by love. The precise sense of التبل مردود is uncertain.

On the house (bayt), line 1
Indeed, ours are its beginning and its end,in judgment, and the right we shall never deny.
إن لنا أوله وآخرهفي الحكم، والحق الذي لن ننكره

The referent of the masculine pronouns is unclear in this fragment. The opening may claim precedence and final authority in adjudicating the dispute over placing the Stone.

On the house (bayt), line 2
We have built up its best and largest part,when, as they disputed, we set in place
وقد عمرنا خيره وأكثرهلما وضعنا إذ تماروا

“عمرنا خيره وأكثره” is uncertain. The translation takes عمرنا as “built up,” referring to the sanctuary; the verb can also mean to inhabit or maintain a place.

On the house (bayt), line 3
This world, for all its length, is onlya mountain pass whose ascent is death.
وإنما الدنيا على طولهاثنية مطلعها الموت

مطلعها is rendered literally as “whose ascent.” The image may instead place death at the crest of the pass; the precise spatial sense is uncertain.

On the house (bayt), line 4
If they are deposed, the Banū al-ʿAbbās were deposed before;before Ḥimṣ, the land of Baghdad stood empty.
إن يخلعوا فبنو العباس قد خلعواوقد خلت قبل حمص أرض بغداد

Ḥimṣ here is an Arabic name used for Seville. The precise earlier deposition of the Abbasids and emptying of Baghdad intended by the comparison are uncertain.

On the house (bayt), line 5
It is not love of the land that moves me, but its nearnessto his remains, and words he thought I would utter.
وما بي حب الأرض إلا جوارهاصداه، وقول ظن أني قائله

صداه is interpreted as 'his remains'; صدى can also denote the dead person's spirit or its imagined owl-form. The reference and grammatical connection of 'and words he thought I would utter' are unclear.

On the house (bayt), line 4
Grievous to me is what Jassās has done—oh,my anguish over what has unfolded, or has yet to unfold!
جل عندي فعل جساس فياحسرتا عما انجلت أو تنجلي

The wording عما انجلت أو تنجلي is syntactically unclear: the feminine verbs have no explicit subject. The translation takes it to refer to the calamity and what has unfolded or will unfold.

On the house (bayt), line 5
How strange that one who secludes himself should neglect whathe needs for the day of his repose.
عجبا لمحتجب يضيع مايحتاج فيه ليوم رقدته

محتجب literally means someone who veils or secludes himself; its intended significance here is uncertain. The reference and grammatical role of فيه in يحتاج فيه ليوم رقدته are also unclear; the translation gives the apparent general sense.

On the house (bayt), line 1
I am not one to raise the roof of another man's housewhile leaving my own house empty at Khumāl.
ولست ببان لامرئ سمك بيتهوأترك بيتي خاليا بخمالي

بخمالي is unclear; tentatively read as 'at Khumāl,' a place-name whose identification and vocalization are uncertain.

On the house (bayt), line 2
I married my daughters exclusively to my own kin;no man of high standing and beauty impressed me.
جعلت بناتي في موالي قصرةوما راعني ذو سورة وجمال

قصرة is tentatively understood as 'exclusively,' restricting the daughters' marriages to the speaker's kin; its precise force here is uncertain.

On the house (bayt), line 2
I shunned you out of apprehension, and visited you in fear;within you, always, stands a watcher of your own.
هجرتك إشفاقا، وزرتك خائفاوفيك على الدهر منك رقيب

The phrase منك رقيب, literally “a watcher from you,” is somewhat obscure. It is rendered as a watcher belonging to the house, perhaps one of its inhabitants.

On the house (bayt), line 3
At al-Jarʿ, in upper al-Junayna, stands a dwelling,wide in expanse, yet there my breast is constricted.
وبالجرع من أعلى الجنينة منزلفسيح شحا صدري به متضايق

The unvocalized شحا is taken to refer to breadth or extent, giving 'wide in expanse'; its precise form and reading are uncertain.

On the house (bayt), line 6
It is as though upon her teeth were wine, mixedwith dew from the end of night by an evening drinker.
كأن على أنيابها الخمر شابهابماء الندى من آخر الليل غابق

غابق is associated with an evening draught. 'Evening drinker' is tentative; someone serving that draught may instead be intended.

On the house (bayt), line 1
In staying away from your house, I am like onewho sees a thirst-quenching draught, yet does not drink.
وإني على هجران بيتك كالذيرأى نهلا ريا وليس بناهل

The precise reading of «نهلا ريا» is uncertain; I understand it as a draught sufficient to quench thirst.

On the house (bayt), line 1
What ails this house you used to frequent?Has someone turned you against it, after your former fondness?
ما بال ذا البيت الذي كنت آلفاأنارك فيه بعد إلفك نائر؟

The expression أنارك ... نائر is obscure; provisionally understood as someone alienating or driving the addressee away. إلفك is taken as 'your fondness/familiarity,' though it can also mean 'your familiar companion' or 'your beloved.'

On the house (bayt), line 2
I now offer you only avoidance, though I,I swear, for all my avoidance, am drawn toward you.
أصبحت أمنحك الصدود وإننيقسما إليك مع الصدود لأجنب

لأجنب is obscure here; “am drawn toward you” is a tentative rendering.

On the house (bayt), line 3
Will the life we lived within you in those days return?For since leaving you, the search for solace has grown unbearable.
هل عيشنا بك في زمانك راجعفلقد تفاحش بعدك المتعلل

The expression تفاحش بعدك المتعلل is difficult. المتعلل can denote a means of consolation or diversion; the translation tentatively takes the phrase to mean that seeking consolation after separation has become intolerable.

On the house (bayt), line 8
Nothing but remembrance of the past, and a yearningallotted to a love-enslaved heart that cannot forget.
إلا تذكر ما مضى وصبابةمنيت لقلب متيم لا يذهل

The construction beginning إلا is elliptical, rendered as 'Nothing but.' The unvocalized منيت is tentatively understood as مُنِيَتْ, 'was allotted or destined.'

On the house (bayt), line 3
They stayed the three days of Minā in the sweetest ease,though on a journey—by your life, they seemed not to be.
لبثوا ثلاث مني بأنعم عيشةوهم على سفر لعمرك ما هم

The abrupt phrase «لعمرك ما هم» is ambiguous. The translation tentatively takes it as denying that their comfortable stay felt like travel, with the predicate left unstated.

On the house (bayt), line 9
I left him to blind conjecture; I was not oneto debate with a slanderer when he spoke against Laylā.
تركت على عمياء ظن ولم أكنإذا ما وشى واش بليلي أناظره

Read بليلي as بليلى, “about Laylā.” The spelling as given is uncertain. The object of تركت, “I left,” is understood as the inquirer mentioned in line 8.

On the house (bayt), line 1
Though I have not come to the tents of Baḥdal,I gaze toward Umm Yaḥyā from as far as sight can reach.
وإني وإن لم آت أبيات بحدلإلى أم يحيى من مدى العين ناظر

The identities of Baḥdal and Umm Yaḥyā are uncertain.

On the house (bayt), line 4
Even if she had what Ibn Bajra possessesof wine, she would not moisten my palate with a single measure.
ولو أن ما عند ابن بجرة عندهامن الخمر لم تبلل لهاتي بناطل

ناطل denotes a measure or small quantity of wine; its precise quantity here is uncertain.

On the house (bayt), line 2
Remembrance tears his heart and mine;he is neither carefree nor clear-headed.
تقطع قلبه الذكرى وقلبيفلا هو بالخلي ولا بصاح

بصاح can mean ‘sober’ or ‘awake’; ‘clear-headed’ takes it as describing someone overcome by longing, though the intended sense is uncertain.

On the house (bayt), line 3
Poverty—enough for me!—and an eye that cannot see,and misery, and a decrepit old man, misery’s companion.
عدم فحسبي، وعين غير مبصرةوشقوة وحليف الشقوة اليفن

Al-yafan means a very old or decrepit man. Its grammatical connection to the preceding list is unclear; the phrase probably describes the poet himself as misery’s aged companion.

On the house (bayt), line 4
The clouds came one after another, and it was a house;they turned away, and it was the middle of the road.
تواصلت السحائب وهو بيتوصدت وهو قارعة الطريق

I read وصدت as wa-ṣaddat, ‘and they turned away,’ referring to the clouds. The contrast between the house and the middle of the road is obscure; it may suggest that the rain left the dwelling exposed or destroyed.

On the house (bayt), line 2
The beetle has a dung heap for its dwelling,yet I have neither companion nor dwelling as it does.
والخنفساء لها من حشها سكنوليس لي مثلها إلف ولا سكن

حشها is understood here as a dung heap or privy, though حش can also mean a garden. The precise sense is uncertain.

On the house (bayt), line 5
I gather the fruits of peoplewhose dwellings have grown desolate without them.
وأجتني من ثمار قومقد أوحشت منهم الرباع

The 'fruits' may be literal produce or, figuratively, works left by people now gone; the intended sense is uncertain.

On the house (bayt), line 1
Yes, may God send rain upon homes in al-Ḥimā,their curtains drawn over beauties;
نعم سقى الله بيوتا بالحمىمسدلة على الدمى أستارها

Al-Ḥimā means 'the protected pasture'; its geographical reference here is uncertain.

On the house (bayt), line 2
Others now dwelt in their home, and down streamedtears from my eyelids, with more like them still remaining.
وفي دارهم قوم سواهم فأسبلتدموع من الأجفان باق مثيلها

باق مثيلها literally means ‘their like remaining.’ I understand this to mean that more tears remain to be shed, but the expression is unusual and its precise sense uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
I am a sojourner whose departure is at hand;whoever greets him greets him as he stands ready to leave.
وإني ثوى قد أحم انطلاقهيحييه من حياه وهو على رجل

I read ثوى as ثَوِيّ, ‘guest’ or ‘sojourner.’ The expression على رجل appears to describe someone poised to depart, though its precise sense here is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
Salmā says—and she found it strange—
تقول سلمىواستنكرت

The line is incomplete. استنكرت can mean finding something strange or expressing disapproval; its object is missing. Without vowels or further context, its subject is also uncertain; the translation takes it as Salmā.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
Why are parts of you being ravaged?
ما بال أشياء منك تنتهك

The expression «أشياء منك تنتهك», literally “things of/from you are violated,” is unclear. “Parts of you being ravaged” is tentative; the reference might instead be to things belonging to the addressee being violated.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
I am like one with cracks that nearly shatter his bone;blows will not spare even sound bone for long.
كذي وقرات كدن يكسرن عظمهولن تلبث العظم الصحيح القوارع

وقرات is understood provisionally as cracks or notches in bone; its precise sense here is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
For I, in hoping to live when they have gone,am like one held back from an ascent, yet bound to climb it.
فإني وتأميلي الحياة، وقد مضواكمحتبس عن مطلع، وهو طالع

The image in محتَبِس عن مطلع وهو طالع is uncertain. I take مطلع as an ascent and وهو طالع as expressing the inevitability of climbing it, apparently an image of unavoidable death; the latter phrase could also mean 'while he is climbing.'

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
I was defiant of restraint, heedless;then I looked straight ahead, and my neck straightened.
قد كنت أشوس في المقادة سادرافنظرت قصدي واستقام الأخدع

فنظرت قصدي is elliptical; I take it to mean 'I looked straight ahead.' الأخدع literally denotes a neck vein, apparently standing here for the neck. The precise force of this image is uncertain, but it seems to contrast humbled obedience with former defiance.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
Many a man have I lowered into a grave,each in the first bloom of youth, well favored.
ولرب من طأطأته في حفرةمن كل مقتبل الشباب محبر

محبر can suggest someone adorned, handsome, or living in comfort; its precise nuance here is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
They went forth like Indian swords, entering a maelstromof death—an entry that allowed no return.
غدوا كسيوف الهند وراد حومةمن الموت أعيا وردهن المصادر

The wording أعيا وردهن المصادر is difficult. The translation takes المصادر as departures or returns, contrasting with ورود, entry or arrival. The feminine plural pronoun in وردهن may refer back to the swords, but its reference is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 4
They seemed, beneath the fluttering banners, as they wenttoward death, like lions of the two thickets, crushing their prey.
كأنهم تحت الخوافق إذ غدواإلى الموت أسد الغابتين الهواصر

الغابتين literally means 'the two thickets/forests'; it is unclear whether a particular locality is intended.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
We once had a nabʿ tree whose branches sheltered us;now death has reached all but a few of its roots.
وكان لنا نبع تقينا فروعهفقد بلغت إلا قليلا عروقها

The syntax of فقد بلغت إلا قليلا عروقها is uncertain. I understand it as saying that nearly all the tree’s roots have been reached, supplying death as the agent from the following verses.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 8
And generosity in years of dearth, whenthe cold season brings drought and the clouds depart.
وسماح لدى السنين إذا ماقحط القر، واستقل الغمام

القر is read as al-qurr, 'cold,' here understood as the cold season. The phrase قحط القر is unusual. استقل الغمام is also uncertain: it may describe clouds rising or departing, or clouds becoming scarce.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
Death and doom were given power over them;their skulls lie amid the echoes of the graves.
سلط الموت والمنون عليهمفلهم في صدى المقابر هام

The phrase «في صدى المقابر هام» is uncertain. I have rendered صدى as “echoes” and هام as “skulls,” but both words can also designate owls associated in ancient Arab belief with the dead; that imagery may be intended.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
My father's sons, he has struck at you with all his weaponsand gained all he wished—this ever-youthful Fate.
بني أبي، قد رمى فيكم بشكتهونال ما شاء هذا الأزلم الجذع

الأزلم الجذع is understood as the traditional epithet of Time or Fate. الجذع suggests enduring youth; the precise literal force of الأزلم in this epithet is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
Their graves now lie scattered, yet what unites themis death’s havoc; no single land gathered them together.
أضحت قبورهم شتى، وتجمعهمزو المنون، ولم يجمعهم بلد

The uncommon expression زو المنون is rendered as “death’s havoc,” following the gloss supplied in line 3; its precise force is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
But one grave is in Miṣr, and in Shayzaranother grave, while my home lies far away in the lands of the ʿAjam.
لكن بمصر قبر، وفي شيزر قبر وداري بمنتأى العجم

Miṣr can mean Egypt or its capital. The ʿAjam are non-Arabs, often specifically Persians; the precise region intended by منتأى العجم is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 6
They went ahead against my wish and hastened toward their own;I lost them—and every side has a place where it must fall.
سبقوا هوى، وأعنقوا لهواهمففقدتهم، ولكل جنب مصرع

هوى appears to represent هواي, 'my wish.' The contrast with لهواهم, 'toward their own desire,' is difficult: the first phrase likely means that the sons died before their father wished, but what their own desire refers to is not explicit.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 5
Now I walk among dwellings that seema defective substitute for the dwellings of al-Kāhiliyya.
فأصبحت أمشي في ديار كأنهاخلاف ديار الكاهلية عور

The unusual phrase خلاف ديار الكاهلية عور is interpreted with the help of the prose gloss supplied as line 6. Al-Kāhiliyya apparently designates a woman associated with Kāhil, but her identity is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 7
I call out whenever [he] mounts a lookout in the course of time—to what listener, if anyone with sight would answer?
أنادي إذا أوفى من الدهر مربئالأي سميع، لو أجاب بصير

The syntax is uncertain, particularly the subject of أوفى and the construction من الدهر مربئا. The translation provisionally takes مربئا as a lookout or elevated vantage point. The relationship between سميع (“one who hears”) and بصير (“one who sees”) in the second hemistich is also unclear.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
And how, when they have become bones and graves,whose owls and death-birds cry out at dusk?
وكيف وقد صاروا عظاما وأقبرايصيح صداها بالعشي وهامها؟

Ṣadā and hām, rendered “owls” and “death-birds,” can denote owl-like birds associated with the dead, including birds imagined to emerge from their heads. Ṣadā can also mean “echo”; the precise distinction between the two terms here is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 9
I have never seen a day like the day of your loss:the stars appeared in it and never set.
فلم أر مثل يومك كان يومابدت فيه النجوم، فما تغيب

The precise significance of stars appearing during the day and never setting is unclear; the image is translated literally. 'Your day' is understood as the day of the addressee's loss.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 11
Whatever must come, with no escaping it,the bringer will in time bring to you.
وما يك جائيا لا بد منهإليك فسوف تجلبه الجلوب

الجلوب means 'the bringer' or 'that which brings,' but its referent is unclear here, possibly fate or death.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
If calamities have changed me,I have seen none among the fallen like Ziyād’s two sons.
فإن تكن الحوادث غيرتنيفلم أر هالكا كابني زياد

The identity of Ziyād’s two sons is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
I parted from them without hatred or aversion,but the passage of time had kept them occupied.
هجرتهم من غير بغض ولا قلىولكن مر الدهر كان لهم شغلا

The unvocalized مر الدهر may mean either 'the passage of time' or 'the bitterness of fate.' The former reading is adopted here; the precise implication of time keeping them occupied is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 4
Now I call on no one among mensave children in the house, lacking sound judgment.
فأصبحن لا أدعو من الناس واحداسوى ولدة في الدار غير حكيم

I take ولدة to mean “children,” but its construction with the singular غير حكيم (“not wise”) is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 4
Their richest is like their poorest oncethe span of life's comforts has run its course.
فأغناهم كأعدمهم إذا ماتقضت مدة العيش الرقيق

«العيش الرقيق» literally means 'tender/delicate living'; it is rendered here as 'life's comforts,' though the intended nuance is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
O my brothers! There are no true brothersI can befriend after you, save the stone slabs.
أإخواني، ولا إخوان صدقأصافي بعدكم إلا الصفاح

الصفاح can mean broad, flat stones or broad sword blades. I have taken it as stone slabs, perhaps those of graves, but the intended sense is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
If the reckoning of my days were in my hands,I would hurry them by, hastening my death.
لو في يدي حساب أيامي إذنخطرفتهن تعجلا لوفاتي

خطرفتهن is an unusual verb with ‘days’ as its object. I take it as ‘I would hurry them by,’ from a root associated with rapid movement, but the precise sense is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
Can any man after Yaḥyā shoulder responsibilities as he did,or can anyone give as generously as al-Faḍl?
هل يستقل كيحيى بعده بشرأم هل يجود كجود الفضل من أحد؟

يستقل has no expressed object. “Shoulder responsibilities” takes it to mean bearing the burdens of leadership, though the precise sense is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
They waded into death’s pool—clear of debris, laid bare.
خاضوا غدير الموت منجردا من الأقذاء حاسر

I read من / جردا across the hemistich boundary as منجرداً, ‘stripped, clear,’ describing the pool. The syntax of حاسر (‘bare, uncovered’) is uncertain; if it also describes the pool, حاسراً would normally be expected.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 7
and bought his life with my right hand,though my fingers and forearm were severed from me.
وبالكف من يمنى يدي حياتهففارقني منها بناني وساعدي

The grammatical connection of حياته (‘his life’) to the preceding line is unclear. ‘Bought’ is supplied from the apparent sense of exchanging wealth and a hand for his life.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 8
Then we would have lived with three hands between us;true amity in life means giving it with mutual gratitude.
فعشنا لنا أيد ثلاث وإنماتصافي الحياة بذلها بالتحامد

The wording تصافي الحياة بذلها بالتحامد is obscure. The translation tentatively takes it to describe amity expressed through giving one’s life, accompanied by reciprocal gratitude or praise.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 5
My pain was eased, after I had nearly flung myselfupon the sword until it reached my belly and jaws,
وهون وجي بعد ما كدت أنتحىعلى السيف حتى يبلغ الجوف والشحى

الشحى is an obscure anatomical term here, tentatively rendered “jaws.”

On weeping for family and brothers, line 8
For a generous gamester among them who played the stakes, and a horseman,when calamity rode upon withers and humps.
على يسر منهم يسير، وفارسإذا ارتدف الشيء الحوارك والذرى

يسر is understood as a participant in the arrow-game associated with distributing slaughtered camel meat. The following يسير is unclear; “who played the stakes” is conjectural.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
They were my pride in life and my strength,and my refuge whenever I cried, 'O my lions!'
وكانوا جمالي في الحياة وعدتيوحرزي إذا ما قلت أي أسودي

I read أي as the vocative particle ay ('O'), making أي أسودي an appeal to 'my lions'; the unvocalized wording is somewhat uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 4
Handsome of face, chaste in conduct,honorable in reputation, neither inept nor aloof from battle.
حسان الوجوه طيب حجزاتهمكريم نثاهم غير لف معازل

The precise force of لف معازل is uncertain. لف may denote tongue-tied or ineffectual men; معازل may denote men who remain apart from battle or go unarmed.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 4
But Abū Sufyān shattered my strength, though I had never beendistraught or bewildered by calamities.
فهد أبو سفيان ركني، ولم أكنجزوعا ولا مستنكرا للنوائب

Abū Sufyān's identity is uncertain. The context indicates that his death is what shattered the speaker's strength.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 5
Who thrust with everysupple spear, every shattering shaft and blade,
والطاعنين بكل مارنة وقاصمة وقاصم

مارنة is understood as a supple spear. قاصمة وقاصم are feminine and masculine forms meaning something that breaks or shatters; their precise weapon referents are uncertain. ‘Shaft and blade’ is tentative.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 10
With every wail of mourning,I have mourning of my own, and mourning weighs upon me.
مع كل رنة مأتملي مأتم، وعلى ماتم

وعلى ماتم appears to stand for وعليّ مأتم, ‘and upon me is mourning.’ The translation follows this reading, though the wording is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 4
And when a turtledove voices her sorrowone day upon a branch, I raise my own cry of grief.
وإذا دعت قمرية شجنا لهايوما على فنن دعوت صباحي

The expression دعوت صباحي is uncertain. It is rendered as raising a cry of grief, possibly referring to the traditional cry of alarm or distress wā-ṣabāḥāh.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
After Zirr’s sons and after Ibn Jandal,and ʿAmr, can I hope to enjoy life at ease?
أبعد بني زر وبعد ابن جندلوعمرو، أرجى لذة العيش في خفض

أرجى is understood as “I hope for,” probably representing أُرَجِّي; the printed spelling leaves the reading uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 5
I would not choose life at the cost of disgracethat Banū Saʿd would hold against me while I lived.
ولست بمختار الحياة بسبةتثنى بها حيا على بنو سعد

The wording تثنى بها حيا على is uncertain. I tentatively read تثنى as تُثني and على as عليّ, taking the phrase to mean that Banū Saʿd would speak reproachfully of him for this disgrace during his lifetime.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 4
It is as though death—the nearest destination—has already brought my body to you in your graves.
كأنكما، والموت أقرب غايةبجسمي في قبريكما قد أتاكما

The syntax is difficult, particularly كأنكما (“as though you two”) and its connection to قد أتاكما (“has come to you two”). The translation tentatively takes death as the subject of أتاكما and بجسمي as “bringing my body.”

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
He was noble, then fell among the fallen;every cracked branch must break.
كان حرا فهوى فيمن هوىكل عود ذي شعوب ينكسر

The sense of shuʿūb in «كل عود ذي شعوب» is uncertain. I have understood it as cracks or splits in a piece of wood; it might instead refer to branching.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
O Time, spare my surviving kinsman:you have had from me what you desire.
ألا يا دهر أفرش عن شريديفقد أدركت مني ما تريد

شريدي literally means 'my fugitive' or 'my straggler'; it is understood here as a surviving kinsman whom the speaker begs Time to spare. The person's identity is unclear.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 4
Is there grit in your eye that will not leave it,or an inflammation—or why does it shed tears?
أقذى بعينك ما يفارقهاأم عائر، أم مالها تذري؟

ʿĀʾir (عائر) can denote an eye affliction or an irritating particle in the eye; “inflammation” is tentative.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 15
fasting through the blaze of every midday,forsaking his pleasure though able to enjoy it;
صوام وقدة كل هاجرةتراك لذته على قدر

على قدر is taken to mean “despite having the ability [to enjoy it].” The terse expression is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 16
forsaking what souls desire, whentheir cravings called them to paltry gain;
تراك ما تهوى النفوس إذارغب النفوس دعت إلى النزر

النزر ordinarily means something scant or paltry. “Paltry gain” interprets it as meager worldly advantage, but its intended sense here is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
You two, join me in streaming grief,with tears poured out in abundance.
أسعداني بعبرة أسرابمن دموع كثيرة التسكاب

The form أسراب is unclear in this construction. It is tentatively understood as describing streaming or freely flowing tears.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
May God, Lord of humankind, never cast far away—by the bond of salt!—those whom Khālida bore.
لا يبعد الله رب العباد والملح ما ولدت خالدة

والملح, literally 'and/by salt,' is obscure here. I tentatively take it as an oath invoking a bond of kinship or mutual obligation, figuratively expressed by salt.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 6
And the soul that has remained after themwill follow in their wake to the watering place they reached.
وإن التي بقيت بعدهمعلى إثر موردهم وارده

The feminine phrase التي بقيت ('she/that which has remained') has no explicit antecedent. 'The soul' is supplied tentatively; it may refer to the speaker's surviving soul or to the bereaved woman.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
O Umaym, youth is far away; youth has gone,and good sense has driven my youthful folly from me.
أميم، هيهات الصبي، ذهب الصبيوأطار عني الحلم جهل غرابي

I understand الصبي here as الصبا, ‘youth.’ The phrase جهل غرابي literally means ‘my raven’s folly’; I take the raven as an image of youth, possibly through its association with black hair, but the precise expression is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
They had an assembly of stout-necked chiefs,swift to defend their honor or assail their foes.
لهم مجلس غلب الرقاب مرازببدار الحفاظ أو يعدن الأعاديا

The second hemistich is uncertain. بدار is tentatively understood as بُدّار, ‘quick to act.’ أو يعدن الأعاديا is unclear as transmitted; ‘assail their foes’ is conjectural and may require reading يعدون for يعدن.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 6
The dwelling-sites of those whom Shaʿūb—Death—destroyed; nowtheir encampments weep and make the mourners weep.
مغاني من غالت شعوب فأصبحتحلولهم تبكي، وتبكي البواكيا

حلولهم is rendered ‘their encampments,’ but it can also denote encamped groups or inhabitants; the intended sense is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
Whose abode is this, like worn-out scabbard coverings,dating from the earliest ages of time?
لمن الدار كأنضاء الخللعهدها من حقب الدهر الأول

الخلل is tentatively understood as coverings or linings of sword sheaths; the precise object in the comparison is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 9
And grazing herds whose night attendants are clamorous,whose drovers are exhausted on watering day.
وسوام لجب سامرهطلح ذادته يوم النهل

سامره is obscure here. The translation tentatively takes it to mean the herds' nighttime attendants, with لجب describing their clamor. طلح ذادته is understood as saying that the drovers are exhausted.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 7
Rain clouds rising over the needy:if the rain failed, they never failed.
غيوثا تنوء على المقترين إن يكذب الغيث لم تكذب

The exact force of تنوء على المقترين is uncertain. I take it as rain clouds rising over the destitute, an image of benefactors coming to their aid.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
A clan’s dwelling, once theirs in the time of repentance—men neither unarmed nor unskilled in riding.
دار حي كانت لهم زمن التوبة لا عزل، ولا أكفال

التوبة, split across the hemistichs, reads 'repentance.' The precise reference of 'the time of repentance' is unclear. أكفال is understood as men unskilled in riding, possibly implying cowardice.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
O Lord, keep my purpose and discernment sound,and grant me piety until I meet those men.
فيا رب سلم نيتي وبصيرتيوهب لي ألتقي حتى ألاقي أولئكا

The printed ألتقي is unclear in this construction. The translation conjecturally reads التقى, ‘piety,’ giving ‘grant me piety.’

On weeping for family and brothers, line 9
My last moment with you, O Shaghab, was a breath of your scentat Sharj, in farewell, as the camels bore us through the night.
وآخر عهد منك يا شغب شمةبشرج وداعا والمطي بنا تسري

شرج is treated as a place name, provisionally vocalized Sharj; its identification is uncertain. شمة literally denotes an act of smelling, rendered here as 'a breath of your scent'; the precise farewell gesture is unclear.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
Had you seen the weeping of Hindand Ramla as they slapped their cheeks,
فإنك لو رأيت بكاء هندورملة إذ تصكان الخدودا

The identities of Hind and Ramla are uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
O Death, who does no wrong,give me rest, for you have taken every dear friend.
ألا أيها الموت الذي ليس جانياأرحني، فقد أفنيت كل خليل

ليس جانيا literally means 'is not a wrongdoer.' This description is unexpected in an appeal reproaching Death; the wording has been retained, though its intended force is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 4
The carefree man slept, heedless of me, but I did not sleep,just as a solitary man with an empty courtyard cannot sleep.
ونام خلي البال عني ولم أنمكما لم ينم عاري الفناء عزيب

The referent of عاري الفناء عزيب, literally 'bare of courtyard, solitary,' is uncertain. I have taken it as a lonely man whose household is empty.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 10
They gave the cup of death to those they killed;for the living, too, there is a portion of their breath.
سقين بكأس الموت من قد أمتنهوفي الحي من أنفاسهن ذنوب

أنفاسهن literally means 'their breaths,' apparently referring to the decrees of fate, but the image is unclear. ذنوب can mean a full bucket or an allotted portion; the latter is used here.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
They were the last of my friends; Time came between us.What can my grief avail—or how can I bear their loss?
بقية خلاني أتى الدهر دونهمفما جزعي أم كيف عنهم تجلدي؟

The force of فما جزعي is uncertain. I have rendered it as questioning the usefulness of grief; it could instead ask about the nature or extent of his grief.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
I parted from them, yet my eye is still an eyeafter them, and my heart still a heart.
فارقتهم، فالعين عين بعدهم، والقلب قلب

The force of 'the eye is an eye ... and the heart a heart' is uncertain. I take it to express surprise that both remain intact after separation, in keeping with the following lines; عين can also mean a spring of water.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 3
and men of resounding voices in the assembly; neverdid their bounty and generosity cease there.
ومهادير في الندى ولا ينفك فيه منهم ندى وسماح

I take مهادير to mean men with loud, resounding voices, and read the first الندى as النديّ, 'the assembly.' As written, الندى can also mean 'generosity,' so the phrase remains uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 4
If you weep among the traces of the dwellings, they arethe dwellings of Banū Zayd—can one bear being without them?
فإن تبك في رسم الديار، فإنهاديار بني زيد وهل عنهم صبر؟

The particular clan intended by Banū Zayd is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 1
My night stretched long at al-Ghaṭāṭ, toward al-Ghamr,and all night my bed was lined with fiercely burning coals.
تطاول ليلى بالغطاط إلى الغمروبات فراشي مشعرا جاحم الجمر

الغطاط and الغمر appear to be place-names, but their identification and vocalization are uncertain. The relationship expressed by إلى الغمر is also unclear; it is rendered literally as “toward al-Ghamr.”

On weeping for family and brothers, line 5
A speaker of sound judgments, an unraveler of knotted affairs,a solver of perplexities, one who holds back those approaching the water;
قوال محكمة، نقاض مبرمةفراج مبهمة، حباس أوراد

The precise force of حباس أوراد is uncertain. Literally it describes someone who holds back parties coming to water; it may refer to keeping enemies from a watering place or to checking advancing war bands.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 5
It descended upon them when they felt secure,neither holding back nor turning aside.
فحل بهم وقد أمنوافلم يقصر ولم يشطب

The sense of يشطب is uncertain here; it is rendered as 'turning aside,' taking the verb to mean departing or moving away.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 7
O eye, weep for themwith tears pouring freely from you.
ألا يا عين فابكيهمبدمع منك مستغرب

مستغرب is understood here as describing copious or unrestrained tears, though its precise force is uncertain.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
Let every troop of horsemen weep for al-Mughīrawhen combat has worn away its mettle.
ليبك على المغيرة كل خيلإذا أفنى عرائكها اللقاء

عرائكها is uncertain here; 'mettle' provisionally takes it to mean the cavalry's strength or stamina.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 11
Forbearing among his kin, even whendisputation loosens the knee-bands of forbearing men.
حليم في عشيرته إذا ماحبا الحلماء أطلقها المراء

I take حبا to be ḥubā, the bands or garments drawn around the knees while sitting. The apparent image is of dispute making even forbearing men undo these bindings and rise in agitation; the unvocalized wording leaves some uncertainty.

On weeping for family and brothers, line 2
When Ḥawrān appeared, with mirage before it,you looked, yet could see nothing with your own eyes.
ولما بدت حوران والآل دونهانظرت، فلم تنظر بعينيك منظرا

The unvocalized نظرت can mean either “I looked” or “you looked”; “you looked” is adopted to agree with بعينيك (“with your two eyes”). The intended force of the following negation—literally, “you saw no sight”—is uncertain.

Names and places

A person or place the translator could not identify, or whose name it had to vocalize by guesswork.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
As though, since those who knew them last were there,the dwellings at al-Dhanūb and the two passes of Wāḥif were written pages.
كأنها بعد عهد العاهدين بهامن الذنوب وخرمى واحف صحف

I tentatively read «خرمى واحف» as «خَرْمَيْ واحف», 'the two passes of Wāḥif,' rather than as separate place names. The identification and vocalization of al-Dhanūb and Wāḥif are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Al-Muṣallā has faded away; the dunes lie emptyof me, then al-Mirbadān, then al-Labab.
عفا المصلى فأقوت الكثبمني فالمربدان فاللبب

Al-Muṣallā, al-Mirbadān, and al-Labab are treated as place-names, though their precise locations here are uncertain. Al-kuthub, translated as 'the dunes,' may also be a place-name.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
Then the mosque that gathered manly virtue and gloryfell into ruin, then al-Ṣammān, then al-Raḥb.
فالمسجد الجامع المروءة والمجد عفا فالصمان فالرحب

The precise locations intended by al-Ṣammān and al-Raḥb are uncertain; the vocalization of al-Raḥb is also uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
I passed a dwelling-site in Siyāth, and was stirredby the clamor of stones there beneath the pickaxes.
مررت بربع من سياث فهاجنيبها زجل الأحجار تحت المعاول

The place-name سياث is unvocalized; its rendering as Siyāth is tentative.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
A dwelling has stirred this heart,desolate at al-Baliyyayn.
هاج ذا القلب منزلبالبليين محول

البليين is treated as a place name, provisionally transliterated al-Baliyyayn; its vocalization and location are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Come, you two, briefly greet the traces of the dwellingsin the watercourses of Salmānayn or the soft plains of ʿĀqil.
ألا حييا قصرا رسوم المنازلبسلان سلمانين أو ميث عاقل

The function of قصرا is uncertain; 'briefly' is a provisional reading. The precise locations of Salmānayn and ʿĀqil are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
You remembered, and the traces of the dwellings made you weep,at Qārah, now deserted, or at Sūqah, now altered.
تذكرت فاستبكاك رسم المنازلبقارة أقوى أو بسوقة حائل

I take Qārah and Sūqah as place names, and aqwā and ḥāʾil as descriptions of the deserted and altered traces. Their precise locations, and this parsing of the unvocalized text, are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
They stand empty of all inhabitants, and have received in their placethe gazelles of al-Salīl, instead of horses and camel herds.
خلت من جميع ساكن وتبدلتظباء السليل بعد خال وجامل

The rare word khāl is tentatively rendered as 'horses'; its intended sense here is uncertain. Al-Salīl appears to be a place name, but I cannot identify it securely.

On encampments (manāzil), line 4
A man whose chief concern lies at al-Sīfand Baṭnān—longing never leaves him alone.
وإن امرأ بالسيف أكبر همهوبطنان ليس الشوق عنه بغافل

Al-Sīf and Baṭnān are taken as place names. The introduction suggests locations associated with Iraq and Syria respectively, but their precise identification is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
A dwelling at one of al-Rijlatayn, as thougheffaced for years, though not yet settled anew.
دار بإحدى الرجلتين كأنهاقد عفيت حججا، ولما تحلل

Al-Rijlatayn is unidentified; the unvocalized name’s pronunciation is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Whose are the dwellings, deserted at ʿAbāʾ?Had I wished, they would have stirred my tears this morning.
لمن المنازل أقفرت بعباء؟لو شيت هيّجتِ الغداةَ بكائي

ʿAbāʾ (عباء) appears to be a place name, but its identification and vocalization are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
I said: “My eye has a tear for these dwellings,born of longing, which patience could neither restrain nor turn back.”
وقلت لعيني في المنازل عبرةمن الشوق لم تملك بصبر فتردد

The syntax and vocalization are uncertain. The translation takes وقلت as “I said,” followed by a statement beginning لعيني, and reads لم تملك ... فتردد as passive verbs referring to the tear.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
My companions heaved a sigh that day at Dhū al-Athl,whose blaze melts hearts and ribs.
تزافر صحبي يوم ذي الأثل زفرةتذوب قلوب من لظاها وأضلع

Dhū al-Athl appears to be a place name; its location is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Does the dwelling at al-Janāb remain as I knew it,where, whenever I wished, I found what I sought?
أعلى العهد منزل بالجنابكان فيه متى أردت طلابي؟

I take al-Janāb as a place name; its precise identification is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
At Qinān Wadʿa and al-Buqayl, they have changedSince I left; the winds moan mournfully through them.
بقنان ودعة والبقيل تغيرتبعدي تحن بها الرياح حنينا

The locations and their vocalizations are uncertain. قنان ودعة is rendered as Qinān Wadʿa, but could mean ‘the peaks of Wadʿa’; البقيل is provisionally vocalized al-Buqayl.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
My eyes have never seen a spring encampment like the oneat Dhū al-ʿIshsh—if only bliss would last.
ولم تر عيني مربعا مثل مربعبذي العش لو أن النعيم يدوم

The location and precise vocalization of Dhū al-ʿIshsh (ذي العش) are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
May the dust-colored al-Ṣafarāt around Tabālah be watered,as far as Raḥb in al-Washm, by an all-enveloping rain.
سقى الصفرات العفر حول تبالةإلى رحب بالوشم غيث مطبق

Al-Ṣafarāt and Raḥb appear to be place-names; their precise identification and vocalization are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Greet the dwellings between Ḥumma and al-Liwā,if you are absorbed in them, stricken with love.
حي المنازل بين حمة فاللوىإن كنت مشتغلا بهن عميدا

The identification and vocalization of حمة, rendered here as Ḥumma, are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
What longing a dwelling at Dhū al-ʿAlam stirred,between Liwā al-Manjanūn and al-Salam!
ما هاج من منزل بذي العلمبين لوى المنجنون فالسلم

The precise locations of Dhū al-ʿAlam, Liwā al-Manjanūn, and al-Salam are uncertain; their vocalizations are provisional. The opening is understood as an exclamation, with longing implied rather than explicitly named.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
If, on the day at Rāmah, you two cannotjoin me in mourning, then leave off reproach.
إن لم تطيقا يوم رامهأن تسعدا، فذرا الملامه

Rāmah is taken as a place-name; its precise location is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Look with me—it is but a glance nearby:is that the landmark on the slope?
أنظر معي، فهي نظرة أممأعلم السفح ذلك العلم؟

العلم may mean a landmark or a mountain. السفح is translated as 'the slope,' though it could be a place-name, al-Safḥ.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
You are blameless for the eye’s confusions;my gaze is suspect because of tears.
أنت بريء مما تشبهه العين، وطرفي بالدمع متهم

مما تشبهه العين is ambiguous: it concerns what the eye makes to resemble something else, presumably a mistaken identification of the distant landmark.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
She has a dwelling in al-Ghawr, between a palaceloftily built and a garden spreading its carpet.
لها منزل بالغور بين مفدنمشيد ومنشور البساط مروض

مفدن is taken as a palatial building, though its precise form and sense here are uncertain. Al-Ghawr may designate a particular lowland region, but the location is not securely identifiable from these verses.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
I ask after Saʿdā, though since she left there have passedover the dwelling’s precincts seven full years.
أسائل عن سعدي، وقد مر دونهاعلى حجرات الدار سبع كوامل

The name سعدي is taken as سعدى, provisionally vocalized Saʿdā. وقد مر دونها is understood to mean that the years have intervened since her departure.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Bid Uthaylah’s dwellings speak—at the valley bend, the bend of al-Qarn, not yet worn away.
قل للمنازل من أثيلة تنطقبالجزع جزع القرن لما تخلق

Uthaylah appears to be a personal name, though a place name is possible; Al-Qarn is an unidentified locality. I read «لما تخلق» as ‘not yet worn away,’ but the unvocalized wording leaves some uncertainty.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
May God water the dwellings between Sharjand Nawāẓir with gentle, lasting rains.
سقى الله المنازل بين شرجوبين نواظر ديما رهاما

Sharj and Nawāẓir appear to be place names; their locations and the vocalization of Sharj are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 4
And what good are greetings when we have alightedat the sandy bend of Lām—may God bring blame upon Lām!
وما يغني السلام إذا نزلنالوى لام، ألام الله لاما

Lām is unidentified; it may name a person or tribe associated with the sandy tract (Liwā). The unusual curse ألام الله لاما is understood as asking God to make Lām blameworthy.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
O two abodes of Thabjāʾ, from the valley of Wāsiṭto Dhū al-Arāṭī—how have you both fared since I left?
أمنزلتي ثبجاء من بطن واسطإلى ذي الأراطي، كيف حالكما بعدي؟

Thabjāʾ appears to be a woman's name, though a place name is also possible; in that case, the opening would mean ‘O two abodes at Thabjāʾ.’

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
My two companions, stir up tears, or halt with usat a dwelling between al-Buqayʿa and al-Ḥabl.
خليلي هيجا عبرة أو قفا بناعلى منزل بين البقيعة والحبل

The places البقيعة and الحبل are unidentified here; the vocalizations al-Buqayʿa and al-Ḥabl are provisional.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Greet the dwellings at al-Bardayn, now worn away,where the tribe once lived; nothing remains of them but traces.
حي المنازل بالبردين قد بليتللحي لم يبق منها غير أبلاد

The place البردين, provisionally transliterated al-Bardayn, is unidentified; its vocalization is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
that longing visits me repeatedly at the sand dune of al-Bishrayn.
أن الهوى بنقا البشرين معتادي

البشرين is an unidentified place name; the vocalization al-Bishrayn is tentative. نقا is understood as نقا/نقى, a sand dune or ridge.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Do you not recognize the dwellings of Umm ʿAmrat the bend of al-Nawāṣif in Abān?
ألم تعرف منازل أم عمروبمنعرج النواصف من أبان؟

Al-Nawāṣif appears to name a locality associated with Abān; its precise identification is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
O dwelling of the tribe on the sandy flats of Lajab,whose familiar traces vanished in ages past.
يا منزل الحي بالأجراع من لجببادت معارفه في سالف الحقب

The place-name لجب is provisionally vocalized Lajab; its vocalization and geographical identification are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
Whenever I remember the people of al-Ghamr, I am joinedby a torrent of tears pouring down my cheeks.
إذا تذكرت أهل الغمر ساعدنيموار دمع على الخدين منسكب

Al-Ghamr is treated as a place-name, but the particular location intended is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
How many years and ages have passed over the dwellingsof Asmāʾ’s people at al-Quffayn and al-Rukn!
كم للمنازل من عام ومن زمنلآل أسماء بالقفين فالركن

The exact locations of al-Quffayn and al-Rukn are uncertain; the vocalization of القفين as al-Quffayn is also tentative.

On encampments (manāzil), line 5
to my two companions, as the day waned around us:“Do you discern any women riding away in the hollow of al-Jaww?”
لصاحبي وقد زال النهار بنا: هل تؤنسان ببطن الجو من ظعن

Al-Jaww is a place-name here, but I cannot securely identify the locality intended.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Has the site of Asmāʾ’s dwellings stirred your longing,at Rawḍat Nuʿmā and Burq al-Ajāwil?
أهاجك من أسماء ربع المنازلبروضة نعمى فبرق الأجاول

The precise locations of Rawḍat Nuʿmā and Burq al-Ajāwil are uncertain. The unvocalized برق is read here as Burq, meaning stony tracts.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Salmā has dwellings east of al-Qanān,and a trace still standing in the desert of al-Lubayyayn.
لسلمى بشرقي القنان منازلورسم بصحراء اللبيين ماثل

The vocalization and identification of اللبيين, provisionally transliterated al-Lubayyayn, are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Do you recognize, in the desert east of Shābik,dwellings deserted by their people, and a place of play?
أتعرف بالصحراء شرقي شابكمنازل أعراها الأنيس وملعبا؟

Shābik appears to be a place-name; its location is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
We came to greet a dwelling of Uthaylah,its landmarks still fresh at Dhū al-Anṣāb.
جئنا نحيي من أثيلة منزلاجددا معالمه بذي الأنصاب

I take جددا as جُدُدًا, ‘fresh’ or ‘new,’ describing the dwelling’s landmarks. The unvocalized name أثيلة is provisionally rendered Uthaylah; its vocalization and whether it names a woman or a place are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 2
He asks the dwellings about them; upon al-Liwālie faded traces that, if you question them, will not answer.
يسل المنازل عنهم، وعلى اللوىدمن دوارس إن تسل لم تخبر

Al-Liwā may be a place-name or a descriptive term for a bend in the sands.

On encampments (manāzil), line 3
O owner of the palms, from the valley of Arthadto the palms of Waddān—what has become of Nuʿm?
أيا صاحب النخلات من بطن أرثدإلى النخل من ودان ما فعلت نعم؟

The vocalization of the place name أرثد, rendered Arthad, is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Ask the dwelling in al-Ghawr where its lovely maidens are,and where its full moon and its stars have gone.
سل المنزل الغوري أين خرائدهوأين تولى بدره وفراقده

Al-ghawrī means situated in a lowland or depression, possibly al-Ghawr, the Jordan Valley; the precise location is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Is it longing, now that the dwellings have stirred you,where the thickets of Bayshatayn meet?
أللشوق لما هيجتك المنازلبحيث التقت من بيشتين الغياطل

Bayshatayn (بيشتين) appears to be a place name; its identification and vocalization are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Would that the dwellings had departed on the day at Mutāliʿ,since the companionship of those who dwelt there did not endure.
ليت المنازل سرن يوم متالعإذ لم يكن أنس الخليط مقيما

Mutāliʿ is apparently a place-name; its precise location is uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Sulaymā’s dwellings have changed,at Rāmah, then al-Kathīb, as far as Biṭāḥ.
تغيرت المنازل من سليمىبرامة فالكثيب إلى بطاح

Al-Kathīb and Biṭāḥ are treated as place names; their precise locations and the vocalization of بطاح are uncertain.

On encampments (manāzil), line 1
Does the gazelle of al-Munḥanāhave an answer, that he might be asked?
هل عند ظبي المنحنىإجابة فيسألا؟

Al-Munḥanā may be a place name or simply a descriptive expression meaning 'the bend,' often a bend in the dunes.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
The dwellings of your father's sons have become as thoughat al-Barqatayn, they were traced with pens.
أضحت ديار بني أبيك كأنهابالبرقتين تخط بالأقلام

The precise location of al-Barqatayn is unidentified.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Al-Waʿsāʾ lies deserted of Ḥarām;once they were men of sober judgment
أقفرت الوعساء من حراموقد يكونون ذوي أحلام

Al-Waʿsāʾ is taken here as a place-name, though the word can also describe soft, sandy ground; the location is uncertain. Ḥarām refers to Banū Ḥarām, named in the introduction.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Whose are the dwellings at Abraq al-Ḥannān,then at al-Barq, then on the heights of Admān?
لمن الديار بأبرق الحنانفالبرق فالهضبات من أدمان

The vocalizations of the place names, particularly al-Barq and Admān, are uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
Whenever I visit a dwelling of hers at Burqat Wāsiṭand Liwāʾ Bayna, it makes me weep.
فإذا غشيت لها ببرقة واسطولواء بينة منزلا أبكاني

The reading and identification of لواء بينة are uncertain; it is provisionally transliterated as Liwāʾ Bayna. Liwāʾ may instead be a descriptive term for a bend or stretch of sand.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Ah, would that I knew: shall I ever spend a nightat Ḥawza, or al-Jizʿ, or Qurān?
ألا ليت شعري هل أبيتن ليلةبحوزة أو بالجزع أو بقران؟

Ḥawza, al-Jizʿ, and Qurān are treated as place names; their identification and exact vocalization are uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Ah, dwellings of the tribe, between Muḥajjarand the edge of al-Qumrī, as though unchanged!
ألا يا ديار الحي بين محجرإلى جانب القمري كأنه لم تغير

Muḥajjar and al-Qumrī appear to be place names; their identification and vocalization are uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Whose are the dwellings on the summit of al-Ḥijr?They have lain deserted for years, for an age.
لمن الديار بقنة الحجرأقفرن من حجج ومن دهر

الحجر is treated here as the place-name al-Ḥijr, but its vocalization and geographical identification are uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
At the memory of dwellings I had visited,between the crags of Ḍāḥik and al-Hazīm.
من ديار غشيتها ذكرة مابين صارات ضاحك فالهزيم

The syntax of ذكرة is uncertain: it may mean that remembrance prompted the visit, rather than that the dwellings are now remembered. صارات is taken as rocky heights or crags. The places ضاحك and الهزيم are unidentified here; their vocalizations are tentative.

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
May al-Liwā be watered—no, rather, our time at al-Liwā—the days when we spent spring at al-Liwā and summer there.
فسقى اللوى، لا بل سقى عهد اللوىأيام نرتبع اللوى ونصيفه

The precise location intended by al-Liwā is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
Balad is emptied of its inhabitants, and desolateare the spring encampments of Sinjār, where heavy rain pours down.
خلت بلد من ساكنيها وأوحشتمرابع من سنجار يهمي بها الوبل

بلد is taken as the place name Balad, a town near Mosul, rather than the common noun meaning 'town' or 'land.'

On dwellings (diyār), line 4
The courts of Mārid stand empty of al-Qamqām,as does all the ground those ravines and sands enclose.
وأقوت من القمقام أعراص ماردفما ضمنت تلك الأعقة والرمل

القَمْقام can mean 'a great lord' or 'chieftain'; it is retained as al-Qamqām because it may designate a particular person. The referent is uncertain, and the location intended by Mārid is not securely identified.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
O dwellings of the tribe at Khabt al-Liwā,you have become a surmise, though once you were real.
يا ديار الحي من خبت اللوىعدت ظنا بعد ما كنت حقيقه

Khabt al-Liwā is treated as a place-name; its precise location is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Have the dwellings at al-ʿAbūqara stirred your longing?Yes—their abodes are empty of us.
أشاقك بالعبوقرة الديارنعم منا منازلها قفار

العبوقرة appears to be a place name; its identification and vocalization are uncertain. It is provisionally transliterated al-ʿAbūqara.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
And yet, Umm ʿAmr, I am stirredby your deserted dwellings at al-Abraqayn.
على أنني يا أم عمرو تهيجنيديار لكم بالأبرقين خلاء

The precise location of al-Abraqayn is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
except one there resembling some of themin its dark eyes with their clear whites, and its dusky lips.
إلا شبيه بها لبعضهمفي حور المقلتين واللعس

The unnamed creature resembling former inhabitants is presumably a gazelle or wild antelope, but the animal is not explicitly identified.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
The peak of Ṣāmiʿ appeared to me and al-Taymī,despite its distance, like a caparisoned stallion.
بدا لي وللتيمي قلة صامععلى بعدها مثل الحصان المجلل

Ṣāmiʿ appears to be a mountain name, but its identification is uncertain. Al-Taymī, the speaker’s companion, is unidentified.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Whose are the dwellings at Barqat al-Rawḥān,from when we would not trade our days for any other time?
لمن الديار ببرقة الروحانإذ لا نبيع زماننا بزمان

The vocalization of الروحان, rendered al-Rawḥān, is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Turn aside, you two, to the time-worn ruins, that we mayweep for the dwellings as Ibn Khidhām wept.
عوجا على الطلل المحيل لعلنانبكي الديار كما بكى ابن خذام

The source spells the name خذام, rendered here as Khidhām; it is also transmitted as حذام (Ḥidhām). The allusion is to an earlier poet who wept over abandoned dwellings, but his identity and the vocalization of his name are uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
As though the tribe’s dwellings at al-Zurq were fresh growthfrom the earth, or words written in ink.
كأن ديار الحي بالزرق خلفةمن الأرض أو مكتوبة بمداد

The sense of خلفة is uncertain here; it is provisionally rendered as “fresh growth,” a possible botanical meaning. The location and vocalization of الزرق (al-Zurq) are unverified.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
There ʿAlwa had a summer home and a spring abode,at Bānqūsā, Bābīlā, and Baṭyās.
فيها لعلوة مصطاف ومرتبعمن بانقوسا وبابيلا وبطياس

The precise identifications and vocalizations of the place names بانقوسا، بابيلا، بطياس are uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Come, greet the dwellings at Saʿd, for Ilove the dwellings for love of Fāṭima.
ألا حي الديار بسعد إنيأحب لحب فاطمة الديارا

Saʿd appears to be a place-name; its location is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Has it stirred your longingor not—a spring encampment at al-Sitārayn, and a desolate trace in the sandy tracts of al-Ghadīrayn?
أهاجكأم لا بالستارين مربع ورسم بأجراع الغديرين بلقع

The precise locations of al-Sitārayn and al-Ghadīrayn are uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
I lay sleepless, my companions at the pass of ‘Amq,watching lightning spread across the sky from Tihamah.
أرقت وصحبتي بمضيق عمقلبرق من تهامة مستطير

The location and vocalization of عمق, provisionally rendered ‘Amq, are uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 2
May it bring Salmā rain! But where are Salmā’s dwellings,now that she lives beside al-Sadīr?
سقى سلمى، وأين ديار سلمىإذا كانت مجاورة السدير

The precise location intended by al-Sadīr is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 3
She has settled in the land of Banū ʿAlī,while my people are between Zamirah and Kīr.
إذا حلت بأرض بني عليوأهلي بين زامرة وكير

The identification and vocalization of Banū ʿAlī are uncertain; Zamirah and Kīr have not been securely identified.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Deserted since Sulaymā left are the valley of Ghawl and Yadhbul,and Ghamrat Fayf al-Rīḥ, and al-Mutanakhkhil.
عفا من سليمى بطن غول فيذبلفغمرة فيف الريح، فالمتنخل

The grouping of «غمرة فيف الريح» is uncertain; it is provisionally treated as the compound place name Ghamrat Fayf al-Rīḥ. Al-Mutanakhkhil is unidentified, and its vocalization is uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 5
They press onward, lean as spear-shafts, scattering dust,bearing Qanān, al-Ḥamās, and Raʿbal.
تواغل جردا كالقنا حاثيةعليها قنان والحماس ورعبل

Qanān, al-Ḥamās, and Raʿbal are unidentified; they may designate individuals or tribal groups. Their vocalizations, particularly those of the latter two names, are uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
Whose are these abodes, as though never inhabited,south of Asnima and at Quff al-ʿUnṣul?
لمن الديار كأنها لم تحللبجنوب أسنمة فقف العنصل

The locations and exact vocalizations of Asnima and Quff al-ʿUnṣul are uncertain.

On dwellings (diyār), line 1
I have not seen Hind since a brief encounterat Anʿam, as she wandered among the dwellings.
ولم أر هندا بعد موقف ساعةبأنعم في وسط الديار تطوف

أنعم is taken as the place-name Anʿam; its location is uncertain.

On haunts (maghānī), line 1
Rābigh lies deserted of its people, and al-Ẓawāhir;the outskirts of Harshā lie effaced, and al-Aṣāfir.
عفا رابغ من أهله فالظواهرفأكناف هرشي قد عفت فالأصافر

Al-Ẓawāhir and al-Aṣāfir appear to be place names; their precise locations are uncertain.

On haunts (maghānī), line 1
O haunts of youth at Bāb Ḥanāk,not at Raml al-Ghaḍā or Wādī al-Arāk!
يا مغاني الصبي بباب حناكلا برمل الغضا ووادي الأراك

I could not identify باب حناك; the vocalization ‘Bāb Ḥanāk’ is tentative.

On haunts (maghānī), line 1
Has your Saʿdā’s familiar dwelling-place stirred your longing,at Rawḍat Nuʿmā and on to Dhāt al-Asāwid?
أهاجك من سعداك مغنى المعاهدبروضة نعمي فذات الأساود؟

The locations of Rawḍat Nuʿmā and Dhāt al-Asāwid are uncertain. The spelling نعمي has been read as نعمى (Nuʿmā); its vocalization is not certain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Stop, you two, and greet the ruins at the foot of al-Liwā;but is there any gain in greeting the traces?
قفا حييا الأطلال من مسقط اللوىوهل في تحيات الرسوم جداء

Al-Liwā may be a place-name or a descriptive term for a curving tract of sand. I understand مسقط اللوى as its foot or lower slope.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
“Is it for a dwelling between Lawdhān and al-Naqāthat your eyes race to shed tears on the morning of departure?”
أمن أجل دار بين لوذان فالنقىغداة النوى عيناك تبتدران؟

Lawdhān (لوذان) is an unidentified place; its vocalization is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
May God water the ruins among the dunes of al-Ḥimā,though they have revealed to everyone what ails me.
سقى الله أطلالا بأكثبة الحمىوإن كن قد أبدين للناس ما بيا

Al-Ḥimā literally means a protected pasture or reserve; the particular location is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
And one sign of my anguish—though gray hair gives the discerning self-command—is weeping over the ruins on the day of al-Rawākis.
ومن جزعيوالشيب إحكام ذي النهى بكاء على الأطلال يوم الرواكس

«الرواكس» (Al-Rawākis) is unidentified; it may be a place name. The reference in «يوم الرواكس», ‘the day of al-Rawākis,’ is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Whose ancient ruins are these at Dhū Khaym,still visible, their remnants like tattoos?
لمن طلل بذي خيم قديميلوح كأن باقيه وشوم

Dhū Khaym is a place-name; its precise location is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
My two friends, turn aside today, that we may greeta ruined campsite between al-Naqā and al-Akhārim.
خليلي عوجا اليوم حتى نسلماعلى طلل بين النقا والأخارم

Al-Naqā and al-Akhārim are treated as place-names, but their locations are unidentified here. The words can also describe terrain: a sand dune and clefts or mountain passes.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 3
Can an encampment return a greeting, when it seems,desolate on a sandy fringe, like the backs of speckled snakes?
وهل يرجع التسليم ربع كأنهبسائفة قفرا ظهور الأراقم؟

I take sāʾifa (سائفة) as a sandy fringe or tract rather than a place-name; its precise topographical sense here is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 3
Dwellings of Saʿdā, effaced at Dhū al-Khāl,on which every dark, rain-laden cloud has poured relentlessly.
ديار لسعدى عافيات بذي الخالألح عليها كل أسحم هطال

Dhū al-Khāl is a place-name; its precise location is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 3
So the marks of the dwellings were altered as they decayed;and against time’s vicissitudes there is no guarantor
فغيرن آيات الديار مع البلىوليس على ريب الزمان كفيل

The unvocalized فغيرن is difficult in context. I tentatively read it as passive, فَغُيِّرْنَ, with ‘the marks of the dwellings’ explaining the feminine plural pronoun. An active reading, ‘they altered,’ would leave the subject unidentified in the supplied text.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
Can the tears of my unrelenting eyes bring backthe nights when the tribe camped among the hills of ʿArān?
وهل دمع عيني اللجوجين راجعليالي حل الحي هضب عران

The place عران has not been securely identified; the vocalization ʿArān is tentative.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Whose are the ruins between al-Kurāʿ and al-Qaṣr?The streaming rain conceals their traces from us,
لمن طلل بين الكراع إلى القصريغيب عنا آيه سبل القطر

The precise locations of al-Kurāʿ and al-Qaṣr are uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
save for enduring hearthstones that never shift, and cold ashes,and a splintered tent peg the young girl drives firmly in with a handstone.
إلى خالدات ما تريم، وهامدوأشعث ترسيه الوليدة بالفهر

The objects are described rather than explicitly named: خالدات (‘enduring things’) probably means hearthstones, هامد (‘extinguished, lifeless’) ashes, and أشعث (‘shaggy, disheveled’) a weathered or splintered tent peg. These identifications, especially the last, are interpretive.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
From the hollow of Qaww, her breaking with us was proclaimedon the morning of parting by a harsh-voiced, hopping crow.
وصاح بصرمها من بطن قوغداة البين شحاج حجول

Qaww is a place name, but its precise location is uncertain. The feminine pronoun in bi-ṣarmihā ('her breaking off') is taken to refer to Baljāʾ.

On ruins (aṭlāl), whole poem

Baljāʾ is interpreted as a woman’s name, though a place-name is also possible. The precise locations of al-Ghaḍā and ʿĀqil are uncertain here.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
My two friends, turn your she-camels asidetoward a ruined campsite between ar-Rabnah and al-Ḥabl.
خليلي عوجا عوجة ناقتيكماعلى طلل بين الربنة والحبل

The places الربنة and الحبل are not securely identified; ar-Rabnah and al-Ḥabl are provisional vocalizations.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
My two friends, rise at ʿAṭālah and look:is it a fire you see from the folk of Yabrīn, or lightning?
خليلي قوما في عطالة فانظراأنارا ترى من آل يبرين أم برقا؟

ʿAṭālah appears to be a place-name, but its location is uncertain. I take آل يبرين as 'the folk of Yabrīn'; آل can also mean 'mirage,' making the phrase ambiguous.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 3
It belongs to Umm ʿAlī, who lit it in hopeof travelers returning, that it might serve them well.
لأم علي أوقدتها طماعةلأوبة سفر أن تكون لهم وفقا

Umm ʿAlī is unidentified. The final phrase is understood to mean that the fire would be useful to the returning travelers.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Do you recognize ruins at Wahbayn and al-Khaḍr,Mayy's, like the bands of green striped cloth?
أتعرف أطلالا بوهبين فالخضرلمي كأنيار المفوفة الخضر

The places وهبين and الخضر are not securely identified here; their vocalizations as Wahbayn and al-Khaḍr are tentative.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Upon you, O ruins of Mayy at Shāriʿ,though your days are long past, be peace.
عليكن يا أطلال مي بشارععلى ما مضى من عهدكن سلام

Shāriʿ appears to be a place name; I cannot securely identify its location.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 3
A longing for you keeps calling, asone dove called to others on the sandy stretches of al-ʿAqīq.
هوى لك لا ينفك يدعو كما دعاحماما بأجراع العقيق حمام

Several places bear the name al-ʿAqīq; the particular location intended here is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Was it the ruins of Salmā’s people that you recognized,at Dhū Ḥaraḍ, still plainly standing?
أمن آل سلمى عرفت الطلولابذي حرض ماثلات مثولا

The place ذي حرض is provisionally transliterated Dhū Ḥaraḍ; its precise location and vocalization are uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
Did you not halt, so the ruins might tell you—at Bayna, their traces faded and changed?
ألم تربع فتخبرك الطلولببينة رسمها عاف محيل

ببينة is tentatively read as 'at Bayna,' a place name whose identification and vocalization are uncertain. It could instead mean 'with clear proof.'

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
My two companions, turn your she-camels asidetoward a ruined campsite between al-Qilāt and Sāriʿ.
خليلي عوجا عوجة ناقتيكماعلى طلل بين القلات وسارع

I have not identified al-Qilāt or Sāriʿ; the vocalization of القلات is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 4
It lies empty save for the wild herds of al-Ṣarīm, though once you could seethere women with gleaming throats and dark eyes.
خلت غير آجال الصريم وقد ترىبها وضح اللبات حور المدامع

الصريم may be a place-name, rendered here as al-Ṣarīm, or a common noun meaning a detached stretch of sand. حور المدامع describes eyes with a pronounced contrast between their dark centers and whites.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 1
O remnant of the tribe’s camp at Dhāt al-Ṣamad,by God, tell me: how have you been since I left?
يا طلل الحي بذات الصمدبالله خبر كيف كنت بعدي؟

Dhāt al-Ṣamad is an unidentified place; its vocalization is uncertain.

On ruins (aṭlāl), line 2
Have you sensed any trace of Daʿd and her companion?May rain bless Asmāʾ, daughter of al-Ashadd!
أحسست من دعد وترب دعدسقيا لأسماء ابنة الأشد

Daʿd, her unnamed companion, and Asmāʾ daughter of al-Ashadd are unidentified. The vocalization al-Ashadd is tentative. ترب denotes a companion of the same age.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 3
And what do we greet of traces that seem,at the foot of Salmānayn, like a worn and tattered cloth?
وماذا نحيي من رسوم كأنهابأسفل سلمانين سحق صديع

Salmānayn appears to be a place-name; its precise location is uncertain.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 2
At the recognition of ruins whose outlines seemedat Wahbayn like embroidery or a chain-patterned cloak?
لعرفان أطلال كأن رسومهابوهبين وشيء أو رداء مسلسل

وشيء appears to be an error for وشي, ‘embroidery’ or ‘figured fabric.’ وهبين is treated as the place name Wahbayn, but its vocalization and location are uncertain. مسلسل is understood as describing a chainlike pattern on the cloak.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
Did the tribe’s encampments at Dhū al-Niʿājstir your heart—though encampments are only encampments—
أمن الجميع بذي النعاج ربوعهاجت فؤادك والربوع ربوع

Dhū al-Niʿāj is a place-name whose location I could not identify.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
Misfortunes have visited al-Jizʿ of Urwiyya;the ages have carried off the freshness of her dwelling.
قد نابت الجزع من أروية النوبواستحقبت جدة من ربعها الحقب

Urwiyya (أروية) is unidentified; both its vocalization and whether it names a woman or a locality are uncertain. Al-Jizʿ may instead be descriptive: 'the valley-bend.'

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 2
The decay of al-Liwā has swept away your patience;longing carried off your wits when al-Labab lay deserted.
ألوى بصبرك إخلاق اللوى وهفابلبك الشوق لما أقفر اللبب

Al-Liwā and al-Labab are treated as place-names, though they can also describe sandy terrain: a bend in the sands and a sandy slope, respectively.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
Come, greet a dwelling on the opposite valley-side,which, among those abodes, stirs longing.
ألا حي ربعا باللديد المقابليهيج الهوى من بين تلك المنازل

اللديد can mean the side of a valley, as translated here; it may instead be a place name, al-Ladīd.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 4
It was not the gazelle of al-Gharr that stirred desire,but her likeness, Umm Wāṣil.
فما ظبية الغر التي هاجت الهوىولكنما شبهتها أم واصل

الغَرّ is provisionally treated as a place name, al-Gharr; its vocalization and identification are uncertain. The unvocalized شبهتها is also ambiguous: “her likeness” is a tentative nominal reading, though the letters can also represent a verb meaning “I likened her.”

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 3
May God send rain upon a house whose people I do not approach,and which you visit only when reproached.
سقى الله بيتا لست أقرب أهلهولا أنت إلا أن تعنف زائره

The syntax and vocalization are uncertain. I read لست أقرب as lastu aqrabu ('I do not approach') and تعنف as passive tuʿannaf ('you are reproached'), with زائره as the delayed predicate of أنت ('you are its visitor'). The resulting shift from 'I' to 'you' and the precise sense of the condition remain uncertain.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 3
How strange the heart—how it confesses!And the soul—once reconciled, how it submits!
فيا عجبا للقلب كيف اعترافهوللنفس لما وطنت كيف ذلت

اعترافه means ‘its acknowledgment/confession,’ but what the heart acknowledges is unstated. وطنت is also ambiguous without vocalization; ‘once reconciled’ takes it as the soul becoming accustomed or resigned to its situation.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
My two friends, turn aside a moment, then offer greetings;perhaps the campsite at al-Jarʿāʾ will speak.
خليلي عوجا عوجة ثم سلماعسى الربع بالجرعاء أن يتكلما

Al-Jarʿāʾ may be a place name or simply a description of sandy ground; its specific location is uncertain.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
Does the campsite at al-ʿAlyāʾ speak, altered as it isby windblown sand and a racing cloud with trailing fringes?
هل ينطق الربع بالعلياء غيرهسافي الرياح ومستن له طنب

Al-ʿAlyāʾ may be a place name or simply mean 'the high ground.' I take مستن له طنب to describe a racing cloud with extended fringes, though the referent is not explicit.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
O dwellings of Sallāmah at the bend,at Khayf Salʿ, may pouring rain water you!
أربع سلامة بالمنحنىبخيف سلع جادك الهاطل

The meter supports reading سلامة as Sallāmah rather than Salāmah; the person is unidentified. المنحنى may be a place-name, al-Munḥanā, rather than simply 'the bend.'

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 1
Linger at those dwelling placesbetween al-Liwā and al-Ajraʿ.
أربع بتلك الأربعبين اللوى فالأجرع

Al-Liwā and al-Ajraʿ are treated as place names, but may instead describe a bend of sand and an open sandy tract.

On spring camps (rabʿ), line 9
And is there, for the days of youthfulplay and al-Ḥimā, any return?
وهل لأيام التصابي والحمى من مرجع؟

Al-Ḥimā is unidentified here; الحمى may simply mean the protected pastureland rather than a particular named place.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 1
Between al-Saqīfa, al-Liwā, and al-Ajraʿlie traces of dwellings, left to the four winds.
بين السقيفة فاللوى فالأجرعدمن حبسن على الرياح الأربع

Al-Saqīfa, al-Liwā, and al-Ajraʿ are treated as place names; their precise locations are uncertain. The latter two can also denote terrain: curving sands and a sandy tract.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 1
The valley of Khabt, though its caravans have gone far away,will not leave us without its ruins stirring our longing.
ما جو خبت وإن نأت ظعنهتاركنا أو تشوقنا دمنه

I take جو خبت as 'the valley of Khabt'; the precise location is uncertain. The construction أو تشوقنا is unusual here; I understand it as 'without its ruins stirring our longing,' though 'until its ruins stir our longing' is also possible.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 2
I said: “Halt, my two companions, at the campsite’s tracesat Dhū al-Ramth, whose dwellings have long lain deserted.”
فقلت: أربعا يا صاحبي بدمنةبذي الرمث قد أقوت منازلها عصرا

Dhū al-Ramth is a place name; its location is unidentified.

On dung-marked traces (diman), line 4
There is no Mayy—only a visit at Mushrifor al-Zurq to the desolate traces of her encampments.
ولا مي إلا أن تزور بمشرفأو الزرق من أطلالها دمنا قفرا
